"Just as, Puṣkarasārin, these are called Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras;
therefore, all this is indeed one."
326.008. Furthermore, I shall tell you how it was conceived by the brahmins: 326.009.
The sky with its stars is the head, and the atmosphere is likewise the belly. (57)
The two thighs are the mountains, and the feet are the surface of the earth;
the sun and moon are the eyes, and the grasses and forests are the body hair.
326.012. Tears he called rivers, and their flow he called streams;
326.013. even the oceans he called impurity—thus did Brahmā Prajāpati declare.
326.014. Examine for yourself the specific characteristic of a Brahmin. Since the Brahmins were born from the Brahman, therefore the Kṣatriyas, the Vaiśyas, and the Śūdras were also born [from it].
326.016. If birth were indeed [determined] by reality, then there would certainly be a distinction based on caste.

326.018. If Brāhmaṇas alone were to go to the world of Brahmā, while the other three castes did not go to heaven, then there would be a distinction based on caste; but if that is not so, then there are no four castes. (60)
Since even one of the fourth caste goes to heaven by means of his own performed action,
and since asceticism practiced here is praised as belonging to the sages, therefore it cannot be a distinguishing mark of the twice-born alone.
If there were a brahmin here who was truly unique—one with two tongues and likewise four ears, four tusks, many feet, and two heads—only then would there be a distinction based on caste. (62)

327.001. Indeed, acts such as the killing of others, various forms of harassment, and the destruction of a living being’s merit—all these were performed by those brahmins who committed evil deeds. //63//
327.005. War, dispute, and frequent quarrels, as well as the ritual sprinkling of cows, were indeed contemplated by the Brahmins.
327.007. Furthermore, the Atharvan rites and acts of intimidation—these mantras were composed by the learned priests.
327.009. Evil desire, the deceiving of many people, guile, and likewise stubbornness for an eon—having thus reflected on what is harmful to others, when will they ever go from here to heaven? //65//
Those brahmins who possess fierce austerity, who are disciplined by their vows and always endowed with virtuous conduct,
who are non-violent and delight in self-control and restraint— those brahmins go to the city of Brahmā.
327.017. Together with bones and flesh, with nails and skin, suffering and pleasure, urine and excrement are all one.
327.019. Since there is no distinction by means of the five sense faculties, this fourfold classification of castes does not truly exist. //67//
327.021. "For example, O Brahmin, suppose a certain man had four sons.
He would give them names—perhaps Nandaka, or Jīvaka, or Aśoka, or Śatāyus.
Furthermore, these sons would be dear to that man."
327.023. In that regard, he who is Nandaka shall rejoice; he who is Jīvaka shall live;
he who is Aśoka shall not grieve.
He who has a lifespan of a hundred years shall live for a hundred years.
327.025. Furthermore, O Brahmin, their distinction is known by name, not by birth.
Why is that?
For here, O Brahmin, a son is born from a father.
And therefore, regarding this, there is this traditional explanation:
"The mother is but a leather bag; the son belongs to the father; he by whom one is born is indeed oneself.
If you understand it thus, O sir, then [your sons] do not belong to you.
In some cases, they have become others. //68//

327.029. Examine thoroughly, O Brahmin: who here is a Brahmin, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra? 327.030–031. All are one-eyed and hunchbacked, or else all are afflicted with epilepsy; some have leprosy and others skin diseases, and they are individually fair or dark in complexion. (69)
328.002. For those beings have marrow, bones, nails, skin, flanks, bellies, and faces that are all equal by virtue of their own karma.

328.003. This being so, O Brahmin, there is no distinction whatsoever; what distinction could there be based on birth? 328.004. Since there is no distinguishing mark of birth, there is truly no such thing as the four castes. (69) (a)

"Therefore, O Brahmin, I say to you: this notion of the world—that 'this is a Brahmin,' or 'this is a Kṣatriya,' or 'this is a Vaiśya,' or 'this is a Śūdra,' or 'this is a Caṇḍāla'—is a mere designation. All this is one; all this is one.
Give your daughter Prakṛti to my son Śārdūlakarṇa to be his wife."
328.007. "I shall give you whatever bride-price you deem appropriate."

328.008. Having heard these words again, the brahmin Puṣkarasārin said this to Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas: "Have you studied the Ṛgveda? Have you studied the Yajurveda? Have you studied the Sāmaveda?"
The Arthaveda has been studied, the Ayurveda has been studied,
and the Kalpādhyāya as well.
Internally as well,
whether it be a circle of deer or a host of constellations.
Have you studied the sequence of lunar days (*tithi*)? Or have you mastered the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*)?
Or have you studied the science of limbs (*aṅgavidyā*), the science of garments (*vastravidyā*), the science of omens (*śivāvidyā*), or the science of birds (*śakunividyā*)?
"Or have you studied the movements of Rāhu, or the movements of Śukra, or the movements of the planets?
Or have you studied Lokāyata, or the exposition of the Bhāṣya, or the Pakṣādhyāya, or Nyāya?
When this was said, Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, said this to the brahmin Puṣkarasārin: "O brahmin, all this has been studied by me, and even more besides."
328.015. Furthermore, there is more to follow.
328.015. Even if you, O Brahmin, should think, "I have reached the further shore of the mantras," regarding that, O Brahmin, I shall state an inference in accordance with the Dharma.
"Indeed, O Brahmin, it did not occur to those beings of the first eon thus: 'One is a Brahmin,' or 'One is a Kṣatriya,' or 'One is a Vaiśya,' or 'One is a Śūdra.
This whole world was one; this entire world was one."
328.019. Then, O Brahmin, among those beings—both those who were dissimilar and those who were similar to one another—other beings began to cultivate, protect, and sow fields of *śāli* rice;
thus the designation "Kṣatriya" arose for them. 328.020. Then, O Brahmin, it occurred to certain other beings there: "Possession is a disease; possession is a tumor; possession is a thorn."

"What if we were to abandon our possessions, go to a forest retreat, gather grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage, and having constructed either a hut of grass or a hut of leaves, enter it and practice meditation?

Then those beings, having abandoned their possessions, went to a forest retreat, and there they constructed either a hut of grass or a hut of leaves using grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage. Having done so, they remained right there.
Having entered, they meditated.
For the sake of an evening seat, they would enter the outskirts of the monastery grove, and for the sake of a morning meal, they would enter the village for alms.

Then this thought occurred to those beings living in the village: "Alas, these beings are doers of what is difficult, who, having abandoned their own possessions, have gone out from the villages, towns, and districts.
Because they had turned their minds toward the outside, the designation "brāhmaṇas" arose for them. Furthermore, those beings living in the village honored them exceedingly.
And they thought that these [gifts] should be given to them.
329.001. Then, among those very beings, certain beings, unable to cultivate those meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), descended into the villages and recited mantra-words.
329.002. The village-dwellers said to them: "These beings are not merely [ordinary] beings;
these are teachers."
The designation "their teachers" arose in the world;
this is the cause and this is the condition for the appearance of brahmins in the world.
329.005. Then, certain beings engaged in various types of work associated with the time for seclusion that were connected with diverse purposes.
329.006. For them, the designation "vaiśyas" arose.
Then, certain beings made their livelihood by means of lowly work;
for them, the designation "śūdras" arose.
329.009. Once upon a time, Brahmin, a certain being, having taken his bride, mounted a chariot and went to a certain region of the forest.

329.010. There the chariot broke down. From that circumstance, the designation "Mātaṅga" (Elephant) arose [for him]. 329.010. [The thought occurred: "Do not go [there]! (*mā tvaṃ gāḥ*). Thus the name originated.
329.011. Among those who plow the field, the designation "farmers" has come into use.
And by delighting the assembly with his discourse on the Dharma through the correct practice of ethical discipline and observances,
he became known as "Rāja" (The King).
329.014. Then other beings made their living by means of trade;
for them, the designation "merchants" (vaṇija) arose.
Then other beings went forth into homelessness.
Having gone forth, they conquered others and conquered the afflictions; thus, the designation "those who have gone forth" (pravrajita) arose for them in the world.
"Furthermore, Brahmin, there arose in the world a single designation;
I shall declare it to you:
Brahmā causes these Vedas to be recited in this world."
329.018. Brahmā, the supreme ascetic among the gods, used to teach the Vedas to Indra Kauśika. 329.019.
Indra Kauśika, in turn, taught the Vedas to Araṇemi-Gautama.
329.019. Araṇemi—Gautama was teaching the Vedas to Śvetaketu. 329.020. Śvetaketu was teaching the learned Śuka.
329.020. And the learned Śuka used to analyze the Vedas.
329.021. For example: Puṣya for the Bahvṛcas; Paṅkti for the Chandogas; twenty-one for the Adhvaryus;
Kratu for the Atharvāṇikas.
329.022. Ba... [text fragment]
And furthermore, O Brahmin, all these are explained:
Puṣya, having been one, has split into twenty-five parts.
329.023. For example: "The white ones and the bark-garments of Māṇḍavya. In that regard, there are ten white ones and eight bark-garments.
329.024. There are seven Māṇḍavyas.
Thus, O Brāhmaṇa, this is the branch of the Bahvṛcas;
Puṣya, having been one, became divided into twenty-five.
"O Brahmin, inference (*anumāna*) is also a means of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*) for the Chandogas.
All these Brahmins are Chandogas;
having been one as the *paṅkti*, they have become divided into eighty thousand branches."
Namely: the Śīlavalkas, the Araṇemikas, the Laukākṣas, the Kauthumas, the Brahmasamas, the Mahāsamās, the Mahāyāgikas, the Sātyamugras, and the Samantavedas.
329.029. Therein, there are twenty Śīlavalkas; twenty Araṇemikas;
and forty Laukākṣas.
329.029. One hundred [disciples] of the Kauthumas;
329.030. one hundred of the Brahmasamānas;
329.030. one hundred of the Sātyamugras.
329.031. There are one hundred Samantavedas. Thus, O Brahmin, this branch of the Chandogas has become one known as Paṅkti and has been divided into eighty thousand parts.
330.001. Inference (*anumāna*) is also a means of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*) for the Adhvaryus.
These Brahmins, having become twenty-one types of Adhvaryus, are divided into one hundred and one branches.
For example: the Kaṭhas, the Kaṇimas, the Vājasaneyins, the Jātukarṇas, the Praṣṭhapadas, and the Ṛṣis.
Therein, there are ten Kaṭhas, ten Kaṇimas,
and eleven Vājasaneyins.
330.003. There were thirteen Jātukarṇas; 330.003. sixteen Ṣoṣṭhapadas; 330.004.
forty-one Ṛṣis.
330.004. Thus, O Brahmin, this is the branch of the Adhvaryus.
Having been twenty-one Adhvaryus, they have split into one hundred and one divisions.
330.006. O Brahmin, inference (*anumāna*) is also a means of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*) for the followers of the Atharvaveda. All these mantras belong to the Atharvavedins.
Having been one, the ritual sacrifice (*kratu*) became divided into two.
Having become fourfold, it was divided into eight;
having become eightfold, it was divided into nine [and] ten.
This is the branch of the Brahmans who follow the Ṛgveda.
The single sacrifice is divided into twelve hundred and sixteen parts.

330.010. Furthermore, O Brahmin, inference (*anumāna*) is also a means of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*). Based on this, these twelve hundred divisions and sixteen divisions have been correctly perceived by the Brahmins who are experts in the Purāṇas.
330.011. Whether in Vedic meter (*chandas*), grammar (*vyākaraṇa*), worldly science (*lokayata*), or the investigation of words (*padamīmāṃsā*), 330.012.
no further reasoning or refutation (*ūhāpoha*) is discerned regarding them.
330.012. That is to say, having understood that one is indeed of a single birth, one ought to be a kinsman.
330.012. Therefore, O Brahmin, I tell you: this in the world—namely, "Brahmin," or "Kṣatriya," or "Vaiśya," or "Śūdra"—is a mere designation. This entire world is one; all this is one.
"Give your daughter Prakṛti to my son Śārdūlakarṇa as his wife.
I shall provide whatever bride-price you deem appropriate."

330.016. Having heard these words of Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, the brahmin Puṣkarasārin remained silent, crestfallen, with shoulders drooping and face cast down; rendered speechless, he stood lost in thought.
330.018. Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, saw the brahmin Puṣkarasārin sitting silent as a mute, with drooping shoulders and downcast face, devoid of confidence and absorbed in deep reflection.

330.019. Having seen him, he spoke again: "O brahmin, even if it should occur to you that there will be an alliance with one who is unequal to yourself, 330.020. you should not, O brahmin, view it in such a manner."
330.020. For what reason?
Because those supreme qualities of the world—such as authority, learning, moral conduct, and wisdom—are found in my son Śārdūlakarṇa.
330.022. Furthermore, O Brahmin, you might think: "Those who perform the Vājapeya sacrifice..."
"They perform the horse sacrifice, the human sacrifice, the Śāmyaprāśa, and the Nirargaḍa sacrifice;
all of them, upon the dissolution of the body, are reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world among the gods.
"But, O Brāhmaṇa, you should not view it in this way."

330.024. For what reason? O Brahmin, those performing the Vājapeya sacrifice, as well as those performing the Aśvamedha, Puruṣamedha, Śāmyaprāśa, and Nirargaḍa sacrifices, while setting forth various mantras, also set forth the harming of living beings.
Therefore, O brahmin, I say to you: this is indeed not the path to heaven.
O brahmin, I shall explain to you the path to heaven;
listen to that.
The wise person, seeking the three kinds of happiness— praise, the acquisition of wealth, and rejoicing in heaven— should guard their moral conduct.
"O Brahmin, those by whom the Vājapeya sacrifice was previously performed here,
by whom the Aśvamedha, by whom the Puruṣamedha, by whom the Śāmyaprāśa, and by whom the Nirargada sacrifice were performed—
they have fully grasped desire through desires that are unrestrained."
330.031. "Nāka is to be sought from here.
O Brahmins, those who hereafter shall perform the Vājapeya sacrifice, those who shall perform the Aśvamedha, and those who shall perform the Śāmyaprāśa and Nirargaḍa sacrifices—"
They will encounter a great calamity that is utterly fruitless.
Therefore, O Brahmin, I say to you: come, enter into a kinship with me.
And for what reason?
For by means of dharma, even caṇḍālas become beyond reproach.
Moreover:
faith, virtue, austerity, renunciation, learning, knowledge, and compassion—these alone [constitute it].
331.006. Indeed, the vision of all the Vedas consists of the words concerning the vows for attaining heaven.

331.007. There are eight kinds of means for attaining heaven. 331.008. It is by these eight methods that the going to heaven is desired; indeed, it is generally known, and especially so through various manifold sacrifices.
331.008. Furthermore, O Brahmin, these eight sisters who are designated as equal to mothers exist in the world.
They are as follows: Aditi is the mother of the gods; Diti is the mother of the Dānavas.
331.009. Manu is the chief of human beings;
331.010. Surabhi is the chief of the cattle; 331.010. Vinatā is the chief of the Suparṇas.
331.010. Of the Kadrū nāgas;
331.010. the earth is the mother of all beings and of all seeds;
331.011. [this is] the great festival of the Maruts.
The seers perceive Mahākāśyapa with their minds.

331.012. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall declare the seven lineages of the brahmins; let them be heard: namely, the Gautamas, the Vātsyas, the Kautsas, the Kāśyapas, the Vāsiṣṭhas, and the Māṇḍavyas—these, O brahmin, are the seven lineages.
331.014. Each one of these lineages is divided into seven [sub-branches].
331.014. Among these, those who are Gautamas are Kauthumas, those are Gagaras, those are Bhāradvājas, those are Ārṣṭiṣeṇas, those are Vaikhānasas, and those are Vajrapādas.
331.015. Among them, those who are Vātsyas are Ātreyas, those are Maitreyas, those are Bhārgavas, those are Sāvarṇyas, and those are Bahujātas.
331.016. Among them, those who are Vātsyas are Ātreyas, those are Maitreyas, those are Bhārgavas, those are Sāvarṇyas, those are Salīlas, and those are Bahujātas.
331.016. Among them, those who are Kautsas are Maudgalyāyanas, those who are Gauṇāyanas, those who are Lāṅgalas, those who are Lagnas, those who are Daṇḍalagnas, and those who are Somabhuvās.

331.017. Among them, those who are Kauśikas are Kātyāyanas, those who are Darbhakātyāyanas, those who are Valkalins, those who are Pakṣins, those who are Laukākṣas, and those who are Lohitāyanas (or Lohityāyanas).
331.018. Among them, those who are Kāśyapas are Maṇḍanas, those who are Iṣṭas, those who are Śauṇḍāyanas, those who are Rocaneyas, those who are Anapekṣas, and those who are Agniveśyas.
331.019. Among them are the Kāśyapas, the Jātukarṇyas, the Dhānyāyanas, the Pārāśaras, the Vyāghranakhas, the Āṇḍāyanas, and the Aupamanyavas.
331.021. Among them are the Māṇḍavyas, the Bhāṇḍāyanas, the Dhomrāyaṇas, the Kātyāyanas, the Khalvavāahanas, the Sugandhārāyaṇas, and the Kāpiṣṭhalāyanas.
331.022. Thus, O Brahmin, these forty-nine lineages have been correctly observed by the ancient Brahmins in the Veda, in grammar, and in the investigation of words.
331.023. Furthermore, other lineages have been recited by me in detail; they are not known by others.
331.024. They are not understood by others.
"Namely, having understood that there is oneness, you ought to be my kinsman.
Therefore, O Brahmin, I tell you: this commonality of the world—whether it be called 'Brahmin,' 'Kṣatriya,' 'Vaiśya,' or 'Śūdra'—is a mere designation. This entire world is one; all this is one."
"Give your daughter Prakṛti as a wife for my son Śārdūlakarṇa.
I shall provide whatever family dowry you deem appropriate."

331.029. Upon hearing these words of Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, the brahmin Puṣkarasārin became silent; he stood there crestfallen, with shoulders slumped, head bowed, speechless, and lost in deep reflection.
331.030. Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, saw the brahmin Puṣkarasārin standing silent, crestfallen, with shoulders slumped, head bowed, speechless, and lost in deep reflection.
And having seen this, he spoke again:
"Just as the seed that is sown, so is the fruit obtained.
For if there were only one Lord of Creatures (Prajāpati), then there would be no distinction [between actions and their results]. (72)

332.005. Nor is any difference in the sense faculties or any distinction in their functions observed; 332.006. whether among Brahmins or those of other castes, there is no disparity whatsoever among them. //73//
For self-exaltation and the claim of superiority are not appropriate here;
for both [the father and the mother] are equal, having arisen from semen and blood and from the womb.
332.009. I shall explain the four castes and the discourse on the dharma of cattle to you.
332.010. You may have a wife who is destined for rebirth; this [practice] is not appropriate for a Brahmin. (75)
332.011. If this world were indeed created by Brahmā himself, 332.012. then a Brāhmaṇī would be the sister of a Brāhmaṇa, and a Kṣatriyā the sister of a Kṣatriya. //76//

332.013. Furthermore, for a Vaiśya, whether she be a Vaiśya woman or a Śūdra woman, she is not a wife but a sister, even if she was produced by a Brāhmaṇa. 332.014. [This is] proper, even if she was born from a Brāhmaṇa.
332.015. Sentient beings are not born from Brahmā; these are born of afflictions and born of karma.
332.016. Sentient beings are seen as low and high, with various supports and distinct [conditions]. (78)
And because of the commonality of their birth, knowledge arises equally among them—among the brahmins, the kṣatriyas, as well as the vaiśyas and the śūdras. (79)
332.019. The Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and also the Atharvaṇa; 332.020.
the Itihāsa and the Nighaṇṭu—from where does meaningless meter originate? (80)
332.021. Among our studies as well are the Maitrī-vidyā, the Śikhī, the Saṃkrāmaṇī, the Prakrāmaṇī, the Stambhanī, and the Kāmarūpiṇī. //81//
Manojavā, Gāndhārī, Ghorī, Vidyāvaśaṃkarī, Kākavāṇī, Mantra, Indrajāla, and Bhañjanī. //82//
332.025. We had men who were learned scholars well-versed in the sciences;
332.026. there were the Maṇipuṣpas, the Ṛṣis, and the radiant Mahārṣis. //83//
332.027. Having attained divine supernatural power, why do you practice medicine through spells?
332.028. Even outcastes (caṇḍālas) who have not studied become Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas. //84//
332.029. Kapiñjala and others have been born and have reached the perfection of mantras.
332.030. For he is not the son of a Brahmin woman; what do you think, O Brahmin? (85)

333.001. Kālī, while sitting, gave birth to the sage Dvaipāyana, who was fierce, radiant, formidable, possessed of the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*), and a great ascetic. 333.002–333.003. He was certainly not the son of a Brāhmaṇī; what then will you say, O Brāhmaṇa? (86)

A Kṣatriya woman named Reṇukā gave birth to Rāma, the great sage—learned, disciplined, and proficient in all the scriptures. He was certainly not the son of a Brāhmaṇa; what, O Brāhmaṇa, will you say to this? (87)

And those men who were endowed with splendor and ascetic power, who were wise and disciplined, and who were esteemed as seers in the world—they were not the sons of the Brāhmaṇī; what then will you say, O Brāhmaṇa? (88)
333.010. This designation was created for the world: "Brahmins" and likewise "Kṣatriyas," 333.011.
as well as "Vaiśyas" and "Śūdras"—this is how this designation is proclaimed. (89)
"Therefore, O Brahmin, I tell you: this notion of the world—that one is a 'Brahmin,' or a 'Kṣatriya,' or a 'Vaiśya,' or a 'Śūdra'—is merely a designation. This entire world is one; all this is one.
Give your daughter Prakṛti to my son Śārdūlakarṇa to be his wife."
"I shall give you whatever bride-price you deem appropriate."

333.015. Having heard these words again from Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas, the brahmin Puṣkarasārin said this to Triśaṅku, the king of the Mātaṅgas: "Of what lineage are you? He replied: "I am of the Ātreya lineage.
"What was your former name? He replied: "Ātreya."
333.017. What is its branch (*caraṇa*)?
He said: the Kāleya-Maitrāyaṇīya.
333.017. How many *pravara*s does it have?
He said: "There are three lineages:
namely, the Vātsyas, the Kautsyas, and the Bharadvājas.
Who are your fellow religious students? We are Chandogas."
333.018. How many divisions are there among the Chandogas? Six. 333.019. Which are they? He said: namely— 333.019. the Kauthumas;
The Cārāyaṇīyas,
the Lāṅgalas,
and the Sauvarcasas.
The Kāpiṃjalayas;
the Ārṣṭiṣeṇas.
"What is your maternal lineage?
He replied, "The Pārāśarīya.
"Then you, sir, recite the Sāvitrī."
How does it come to be?
How many syllables does the Sāvitrī have?
How many sections (gaṇḍa)? How many feet (pada)?
The Sāvitrī consists of twenty-four syllables;
it has three divisions and eight-syllable feet.
333.023. "May your honor recite the Sāvitrī.
333.024. "Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall proclaim the Sāvitrī together with its origin."
333.024. Therefore, let it be heard.
333.024. May your honor relate it.
333.025. Once upon a time, O Brahmin, in the past, there was a seer named Vasu.
He possessed the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*), was of fierce splendor and great majesty, and had attained the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*).
There, he took as his wife the daughter of Takṣaka named Kapilā.
With his mind impassioned by her, he engaged in sexual intercourse with that maiden.

333.027. That seer, having fallen from supernatural power and been deprived of his meditative concentrations, was bereft of his psychic abilities. Remorseful and censuring his own misconduct, at that moment he recited the Sāvitrī verse, as follows:
333.029. Namely—
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ.
We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ;
may he inspire our thoughts.
333.031. "For it was for the sake of purifying ignorance, O brahmin, that this very mantra was recited by that brahmin day and night.
333.032. This is the Sāvitrī of the brahmins;
Prajāpati is its progenitor."
334.001. Having become an ascetic with matted hair, he took refuge in a dense forest. 334.002.
There, in Gambhīrāvabhāsa, he was devoted to his own ascetic penances. (90)
334.003. Having offered the king his choice food and sat down, he recited this mantra:
334.003. "This is the *sāvitrī* of the *kṣatriyas*.
For wonderful indeed is the daughter of a *vaiśya*."
334.004. Now, that girl was proficient in the meaning [of the texts].
334.004. This is the *sāvitrī* for the Vaiśyas.
334.005. *Atapaḥ*, *sutapaḥ*.
"May we live for a hundred autumns;
may we see for a hundred autumns.
This is the *sāvitrī* of the Śūdras.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ!
Indeed, sensual desires are the supreme obstacles for living beings in this world when it comes to abandoning the afflictions.
Therefore, sirs, abandon sensual desires; thereby you shall attain the incomparable Brahma-world. (91)
334.011. Thus, O Brahmin, this Sāvitrī was spoken by Brahmā Sahāpati and has been approved by the perfectly awakened ones of the past.
"Recite, O Triśaṅku, the lineage of the constellations. "Very well; sir, may your honor speak.
"Listen."
"O Puṣkarasārin,
I shall explain the lineage of the constellations.
It is as follows:"
334.015. Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśirā, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, Maghā, Pūrvaphalgunī,
Uttaraphalgunī, Hastā, Citrā, Svātī, Viśākhā, Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Mūlā,
Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Abhijit, Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, Pūrvabhādrapadā, and Uttarabhādrapadā.
Revatī, Aśvinī, and Bharaṇī—
these, O Puṣkarasārin, are the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
334.019. How many stars do they have, what are their shapes, with how many muhūrtas do they conjoin, what is their food, who are their deities, and what are their lineages?

334.021. O Puṣkarasārin, the lunar mansion Kṛttikā has six stars; its shape is like a razor; it conjoins for thirty muhūrtas; its food is curd; its deity is Agni; and its lineage is Vaiśyāyanīya. 334.022. The lunar mansion Rohiṇī has five stars; its shape is like a cart; it conjoins for forty-five muhūrtas; its food is the flesh of deer; its deity is Prajāpati; and its lineage is Bhāradvāja.

334.023. The constellation Mṛgaśiras has three stars, is shaped like the head of a deer, is conjoined with thirty muhūrtas, has fruits and roots as its food, has Soma as its deity, and belongs to the Mṛgāyaṇīya lineage by clan.

334.024. The constellation Ārdrā has one star, is shaped like a sesame seed, is conjoined with fifteen muhūrtas, has clarified butter scum as its food, has Sūrya as its deity, and belongs to the Hārītāyanīya lineage by clan.

334.026. The constellation Punarvasu has two stars, is shaped like a footprint, is conjoined with forty-five muhūrtas, has midday meals as its food, has Aditi as its deity, and belongs to the Vāsiṣṭha lineage by clan.

334.027. The Puṣya constellation has three stars, a shape like a *vardhamāna* (an increasing vessel), a conjunction lasting thirty *muhūrtas*, honey-sweetened food as its sustenance, Jupiter (*Bṛhaspati*) as its presiding deity, and the Aupamanyava lineage as its clan.

334.028. The Āśleṣā constellation has one star, a shape like a *tilaka* (a sectarian mark), a conjunction lasting fifteen *muhūrtas*, milk-rice (*pāyasa*) as its food, the serpent (*Sarpa*) as its presiding deity, and the Maitrāyaṇīya lineage as its clan.
334.029. Thus, O Puṣkarasārin, these are the seven constellations that have the eastern gate.

334.031. The Maghā constellation has five stars, is shaped like a river-bend, is conjoined with thirty muhūrtas, has sesame and *kṛsara* as its food, and has the Pitṛs as its deity; it belongs to the Piṅgalāyana lineage by clan. 335.001.

The Pūrvaphalgunī constellation has two stars, is shaped like a footstep, is conjoined with thirty muhūrtas, has the *bilva* fruit as its food, has Bhava as its deity, and belongs to the Gautama lineage by clan.

335.002. The Uttaraphalgunī constellation has two stars, is shaped like a footstep, is conjoined with forty-five muhūrtas, has wheat and fish as its food, has Aryaman as its deity, and belongs to the Kauśika lineage by clan.

335.003. The *hasta* lunar mansion has five stars, is shaped like a hand, is conjoined with thirty *muhūrtas*, has *śyāmāka* grain as its food, the Sun as its deity, and the Kāśyapa clan as its lineage.

335.004. The *citrā* lunar mansion has one star, is shaped like a beauty mark (*tilaka*), is conjoined with thirty *muhūrtas*, has mung-bean rice-porridge, clarified butter cakes, and other foods as its sustenance, Tvaṣṭṛ as its deity, and the Kātyāyanīya clan as its lineage.

335.005. The *svātī* lunar mansion has one star, is shaped like a beauty mark (*tilaka*), is conjoined with fifteen *muhūrtas*, has mung-bean rice-porridge and fruit as its food, Vāyu as its deity, and the Kātyāyanīya clan as its lineage.

335.007. The Viśākhā constellation has two stars, is shaped like a pair of horns, is conjoined for forty-five muhūrtas, has sesame flowers as its food, and has Indra and Agni as its presiding deities; Śākhāyana is its lineage by clan.
335.008. These, O Puṣkarasārin, are the seven constellations of the southern gate.

335.009. The lunar mansion Anurādhā consists of four stars; its configuration is that of a string of jewels; it has a conjunction lasting thirty muhūrtas; its food is wine and meat; its presiding deity is Mitra; and its lineage is Ālambāyanīya. 335.010. The lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā consists of three stars; its configuration is that of a grain of barley in the middle; it has a conjunction lasting fifteen muhūrtas; its food is rice-gruel; its presiding deity is Indra; and its lineage is Dīrghakātyāyanīya. 335.011. The lunar mansion Mūla consists of seven stars; its configuration is that of a scorpion; it has a conjunction lasting thirty muhūrtas; its food is roots and fruits; its presiding deity is Nairṛti; and its lineage is Kātyāyanīya.

335.012. The constellation Pūrvāṣāḍhā consists of four stars; its shape is like the stride of a bull; it is conjoined with thirty muhūrtas; its food is the decoction of the *nyagrodha* tree; its presiding deity is Water (*toya*); and it belongs to the Maudgalāyana lineage by clan. 335.013. The constellation Uttarāṣāḍhā consists of four stars; its shape is like the stride of an elephant; it is conjoined with forty-five muhūrtas; its food is honey and parched grain (*lāja*); its presiding deity is Viśva; and it belongs to the Maudgalāyana lineage by clan.

335.015. The constellation Abhijit has three stars, is shaped like the head of a cow, is associated with six muhūrtas, has wind as its sustenance, and has Brahmā as its deity; it belongs to the Kātyāyana lineage. 335.016. The constellation Śravaṇā has three stars, is shaped like a barley grain in the middle, is associated with thirty muhūrtas, has bird-flesh as its sustenance, has Viṣṇu as its deity, and belongs to the Kātyāyana lineage.
335.017. These, O Puṣkarasārin, are the seven constellations belonging to the western gate.

335.019. The *dhaniṣṭhā* lunar mansion has four stars, is shaped like a bird, is conjoined with thirty *muhūrtas*, has *kulattha*-pulse cakes as its food, has Vasu as its deity, and belongs to the Kauṇḍinyāyana lineage by clan.

335.020. The *śatabhiṣā* lunar mansion has one star, is shaped like a sectarian mark (*tilaka*), is conjoined with fifteen *muhūrtas*, has rice gruel as its food, has Varuṇa as its deity, and belongs to the Tāṇḍyāyana lineage by clan.

335.021. The *pūrvabhādrapadā* lunar mansion has two stars, is shaped like a foot, is conjoined with thirty *muhūrtas*, has meat and blood as its food, has Ahirbudhnya as its deity, and belongs to the Jātūkarṇya lineage by clan.

335.022. The lunar mansion Uttarabhādrapadā has two stars, is shaped like a footstep, has a conjunction lasting forty-five muhūrtas, has meat for its food, and has Aryaman as its presiding deity; it belongs to the Dhyāna-Drāhyāyaṇīya lineage by clan. 335.024. The lunar mansion Revatī has one star, is shaped like a sesame seed, has a conjunction lasting thirty muhūrtas, has honeyed milk-rice for its food, has the Gandharvas as its presiding deity, and belongs to the Maitrāyaṇīya lineage by clan.

335.026. The lunar mansion Bharaṇī has three stars, is shaped like the female organ (bhaga), has a conjunction lasting thirty muhūrtas, has sesame and rice for its food, has Yama as its presiding deity, and belongs to the Bhārgavīya lineage by clan.
335.027. Thus, O Puṣkarasārin, these are the seven constellations belonging to the northern gate.
335.028. "O Puṣkarasārin, among these twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), six mansions have a conjunction (*yoga*) of forty-five *muhūrta*s.
They are as follows: Rohiṇī, Punarvasu, Uttaraphalgunī, Viśākhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Uttarabhādrapadā.
Five mansions have a conjunction of fifteen *muhūrta*s."
They are as follows: Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Svātī, Jyeṣṭhā, and Śatabhiṣā.
One, Abhijit, has a conjunction of six muhūrtas;
the remaining [nakṣatras] have a conjunction of thirty muhūrtas.
336.001. "O Puṣkarasārin, among these seven constellations belonging to the eastern gate, Kṛttikā is the first by name, and Āśleṣā is the last by name.
336.002. Among these seven constellations belonging to the southern gate, Maghā is the first by name."
Viśākhā is called the last.
Among these seven constellations belonging to the western gate, Anurādhā is called the first, and Śravaṇā is called the last.
336.004. Among these seven constellations that have the northern gate, Dhaniṣṭhā is named the first, and Bharaṇī is named the last.
336.006. "O Puṣkarasārin, among these twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), there are seven that possess power.
What are the seven?
Namely, the three *pūrva*s, Viśākhā, Anurādhā, Punarvasu, and Svāti."
336.007. Three [constellations] are formidable: Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, and Bharaṇī. 336.008.
Four are to be honored.
Namely, the three Uttarās and Rohiṇī;
and five that are mild:
Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Mūlā.
336.009. There are five constellations that bring retention: Hasta, Citrā, Āśleṣā, Maghā, and Abhijit. 336.010.
There are four that accomplish things quickly.
Namely: Kṛttikā, Mṛgaśirā, Puṣyā, and Aśvinī.
"O Puṣkarasārin, for these twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), there are three types of conjunctions (*yoga*): the bull-following conjunction (*ṛṣabhānusārī yoga*),
the calf-following conjunction (*vatsānusārī yoga*),
and the yoke-bound conjunction (*yuganaddha yoga*)."
336.012. In that regard, if the lunar mansion moves in front and the moon follows behind, this is called the "bull-following" conjunction (*ṛṣabhānusārī yoga*).
336.013. That is to say, when the moon moves in front and the lunar mansion follows behind.
Then the conjunction (yoga) follows the calf.
Furthermore, if both the moon and the lunar mansion move together equally at the same time,
that is called a conjunction (yoga).
336.016. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall proclaim the planets; let that be heard. They are as follows: Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Śanaiścara, Budha, Aṅgāraka, Sūrya, and Tārādhipati.

336.018. While the world thus revolves and the constellations are distributed [among the months], how do the decrease and increase of nights and days occur? This is explained: 336.019. In the second month of the winter season, on the eighth day when the moon is in conjunction with Rohiṇī, the day consists of twelve muhūrtas;
336.020. the night consists of eighteen muhūrtas.
In the last month of summer, on the eighth day under the asterism Rohiṇī, the day consists of eighteen muhūrtas;
the night consists of twelve muhūrtas.
In the last month of the rainy season, on the eighth day under the asterism Rohiṇī, the day consists of fourteen muhūrtas.
The night consists of sixteen muhūrtas.
"O Triśaṅku, what is the starting point of nights and days?
Day after day. What is the starting point of a fortnight? The first lunar day (pratipad)."
336.024. What is the starting point of the year? Pauṣa. 336.024. What is the starting point of the seasons? The rainy season (prāvṛṭ).
"O Triśaṅku, what is the measure of a *kṣaṇa*? What is that of a *lava*?
And what is that of a *muhūrta*?"
For example, O Puṣkarasārin, it is like the length of thread drawn out by a woman spinning who is neither too tall nor too short.
Such is the duration of a *tatkṣaṇa*. One hundred and twenty *tatkṣaṇas* constitute one *kṣaṇa*.
Thirty *lava*s constitute one *muhūrta*.
By this sequential connection, one night and day (*rātridivasa*) is inferred to consist of thirty *muhūrta*s.
These *muhūrta*s have the following names:
336.029. When the sun rises with a shadow of ninety-six *pauruṣas*, the muhūrta named Catur-ojas occurs.
336.029. When the shadow is sixty *pauruṣas* long, the muhūrta named Śveta occurs.
336.030. When the shadow is twelve *pauruṣas* long, the muhūrta named Samṛddha occurs.
When the shadow is six *pauruṣas* long, there is the muhūrta named Śarapatha.
When the shadow is five *pauruṣas* long, there is the muhūrta named Atisamṛddha.
When the shadow is four *pauruṣas* long, there is the muhūrta named Udgata.
When the shadow is three *puruṣas* long, there is the *muhūrta* named Sumukha. When midday has passed, there is the *muhūrta* named Vajraka.
When midday has turned and the shadow is three *puruṣas* long, there is the *muhūrta* named Rohita.
337.003. When the shadow is four *pauruṣas* long, it is the *muhūrta* called Bala. 337.004. When the shadow is five *pauruṣas* long, it is the *muhūrta* named Vijaya.
337.004. When the shadow is six *pauruṣas* long, it is the *muhūrta* named Sarvarasa.
When the shadow is twelve *pauruṣas* long, the hour is named Vasu; when the shadow is sixty *pauruṣas* long, the hour is named Sundara;
and as the sun descends, when the shadow is ninety-six *pauruṣas* long, the hour is named Parabhaya.
337.007. These are the muhūrtas of the day.
337.008. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the moments (muhūrta) of the night.
337.008. When the sun has set, there is the moment named Raudra.
337.009. Following that is the moment named Tārāvacara.
The muhūrta named Samyama;
the muhūrta named Sāmpraiyaka;
the muhūrta named Ananta.
The muhūrta named Gardabha;
the muhūrta named Rākṣasa;
and when midnight has arrived, the muhūrta named Avayava.
When midnight has passed, there is the muhūrta named Brahmā;
the muhūrta named Diti;
and the muhūrta named Arka.
The muhūrta named Vidhamana;
the muhūrta named Āgneya;
the muhūrta named Ātapāgni.
337.013. The moment named Abhijit.
337.013. These are the names of the moments of the night. 337.013. Thus, O Puṣkarasārin, these are the thirty moments by which a day and night are known.
A *kṣaṇa*, a *lava*, and a *muhūrta* [are units of time].
Among these, a *lava* is the thirtieth part of a *muhūrta*;
a *kṣaṇa* is the sixtieth part of a *lava*.
One hundred and twenty moments (*kṣaṇa*) constitute one *tatkṣaṇa*.
For example, it is like the length of a thread drawn out by a woman who is neither too tall nor too short while spinning;
such is the duration of a *tatkṣaṇa*.
One *kṣaṇa* consists of one hundred and twenty *tatkṣaṇas*.
Sixty *kṣaṇas* constitute one *lava*.
Thirty *lavas* constitute one *muhūrta*.
337.018. By this sequential method, thirty muhūrtas constitute one day and night.
337.019. Thirty days and nights constitute one month.
Twelve months constitute a year.
337.019. Caturojas, Śveta, Samṛddha, Śarapatha, Atisamṛddha, Udgata, Sumukha, Vajraka, Rohita, Bala, Vijaya, Sarvarasa, Vasu, Sundara, Parabhaya;
337.020. Raudra, Tārāvacara, Samyama, Sāmpreyaka, Ananta, Gardabha, Rākṣasa, Avayava, Brahmā, Diti, Arka, Vidhamana, Āgneya, Ātapāgni, and Abhijit—these are the names of the muhūrtas.
337.022. These are the names of the muhūrtas.
337.023. O Brahmin, I shall also tell you of the arising of time; listen.
337.024. As for what the measure of time is, that is now stated:
two winks of the eye constitute one *lava*.
337.024. Eight *lava*s make one *kāṣṭhā*.
337.025. Sixteen *kāṣṭhā*s make one *kalā*. Thirty *kalā*s make one *nāḍikā*.
In that context, two *nāḍikās* constitute one *muhūrta*.
Furthermore, what is the measure of a *nāḍikā*? It is said: one *droṇa* of water; when strained through a filter, that becomes two hundred *palas*.
337.027. What is the measure of the hole in the tube? It is the size of a gold [grain].
337.028. A gold pin four finger-breadths long should be made for it.
337.028. It is circular in circumference, square on all sides, and elongated.
337.029. When that water in the jar has thus been exhausted, that constitutes one *nāḍikā*. By this measure of a *nāḍikā*, two *nāḍikās* divided [into sixty] constitute one *muhūrta*.
"O Brahmin, by this [measure] there are thirty muhūrtas,
by which nights and days are calculated."
338.001. Sixteen *nimeṣas* constitute one *kāṣṭhā*;
sixteen *kāṣṭhās* constitute one *kalā*;
sixty *kalās* constitute one *muhūrta*.
Thirty muhūrtas constitute one day and night;
thirty days and nights constitute one month;
twelve months constitute one year.
Furthermore, by this twinkling of an eye, sixteen koṭis, fifty-eight hundred thousand, and eighty-eight thousand [moments] are thus measured.
And that, O Brāhmaṇa, is explained as the arising of time.
338.005. Listen, O Brahmin, to the origin of the *troyojana*.
338.006. Seven particles of dust from a window-lattice make one particle of rabbit-dust (*śaśakraja*).
Seven rabbit hairs make one sheep hair;
seven sheep hairs make one cow hair;
seven cow hairs make one louse.
Seven *yūkās* make one *likṣā*;
seven *likṣās* make one barley grain (*yava*);
seven barley grains make one finger-breadth (*aṅguli*).
338.008. Twelve finger-breadths make one span (*vitasti*). 338.008. Two spans make one cubit (*hasta*). 338.009. Four cubits make one bow (*dhanus*).
338.009. One thousand *dhanus* make one *krośa*.
338.009. Four *krośas* make one *māgadha-yojana*.
338.010. This is the consolidated measure of a *yojana*.
338.010. Two hundred and forty-nine trillion, two hundred and twelve million atoms—this is measured as one *yojana*.
338.011. Thus is the *yojana* defined.
338.012. Listen, O Brahmin, to the origin of the measurement of gold. 338.012. May your honor explain it: 338.013. Twelve barley grains make one *māṣaka*.
338.013. Sixteen *māṣakas* make one *karṣa*. 338.013. This is the consolidated measure of gold.
338.014. [The total number of atoms is] two *koṭīs*, twenty-five thousand, five hundred, and eight *paramāṇus*.
338.014. Thus, O Brāhmaṇa, has the measurement and origin of gold been explained.
338.016. Listen, brahmin, to the measure of a *pala*:
sixty-four *māṣakas* constitute a Magadhan *pala*.
This is the total measure of a *pala* according to the Magadhan scale.
338.017. Eighty-four million, seven hundred and seven thousand two hundred and eighty atoms (paramāṇus). 338.018. Thus, O Brahmin, is the measure of a pala calculated.
338.019. Listen, O Brahmin, to the origin of the measure of liquid (rasa).
338.019. Twenty-four palas constitute a Magadhan prastha.
338.019. That is the measure for liquids.
338.020. By means of the Magadhan scale, the measure of a prastha is thus determined as a solid mass.
338.020. Two hundred and three koṭis, twenty-nine lakhs, seventy-four thousand, seven hundred and twenty atoms (paramāṇus). 338.022.
Thus, O Brahmin, is the production of the standard measure of taste (rasamāna) calculated.
338.023. Listen, O Brahmin, to the origin of the measurement of grain.
338.023. Twenty-nine palas, less one karṣa, constitute a Magadhan prastha.
338.024. This is the measured standard for the quantity of grain.
338.024. By means of the Magadhan balance, the measure of a *prastha* has been calculated as follows:
one hundred and fifty-eight *koṭis*, eighty-two hundred thousand, sixty-one thousand, five hundred, and thirty atoms (*paramāṇus*). 338.026. Thus, O Brahmin, has the measure of grain been determined.
"Recite, O Triśaṅku, the chapter named 'The Exposition of the Lunar Mansions' (Nakṣatravyākaraṇa).
"Then indeed, O Brahmin, I shall explain the chapter named 'The Exposition of the Lunar Mansions'; let it be heard.
"May your honor speak."
338.029. A man born under Kṛttikā becomes illustrious.
338.029. One born under Rohiṇī becomes fortunate and possessed of enjoyments.
338.030. One born under Mṛgaśiras becomes a seeker of battle.
338.030. One born under Ārdrā becomes a spring of food and drink.
338.031. One born under Punarvasu becomes a cattle-herder.
338.031. One born under Puṣya is virtuous.
338.031. One born under Āśleṣā becomes lustful. 339.001. One born under Maghā is wise and noble-minded. 339.001. One born under Pūrvaphalgunī has a short lifespan.
One born under Uttaraphalgunī is inclined toward fasting and is destined for heaven. One born under Hastā becomes a thief.
339.003. One born under Citrā becomes skilled in dance and song, and knowledgeable in the methods of ornamentation.
339.004. One born under Svāti becomes an astrologer.
One born under Gaṇaka-mahāmātra becomes a royal official;
one born under Viśākhā becomes a royal soldier;
and one born under Anurādhā becomes a merchant or a caravan leader.
339.005. One born under Jyeṣṭhā has a short lifespan and possesses few enjoyments.
339.006. One born under Mūla has many sons and is renowned.
One born under Pūrvāṣāḍhā becomes a practitioner of yoga (yogācāra).
One born under Uttarāṣāḍhā becomes a lord of food and is of noble birth.
One born under Abhijit becomes a man of renown.
One born under Śravaṇā becomes honored by kings;
one born under Dhaniṣṭhā becomes wealthy;
one born under Śatabhiṣā becomes a root-herbalist.
One born under Pūrvabhādrapadā becomes a commander of a band of thieves;
one born under Uttarabhādrapadā becomes a perfumer and a *gandharva*.
One born under Revatī becomes a boatman;
one born under Aśvinī becomes a horse merchant;
one born under Bharaṇī becomes an executioner.
339.011. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is called the "Exposition of the Constellations."
339.012. Recite, O Triśaṅku, the chapter titled "The Exposition of the Lunar Mansions.
339.012. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter titled "The Exposition of the Lunar Mansions.
339.013. Let it be heard.
339.013. May you speak:
339.014. "When situated under the Kṛttikās, the city indeed blazes with splendor; 339.015.
one should describe that city as being resplendent with abundant jewels. (92)
One should designate that city as being situated under Rohiṇī. There, the people shall be righteous and possess abundant stores of wealth;
they will be endowed with the nature of learning and devoted to their own wives. (93)
When [the moon] is situated in Mṛgaśīrṣa, it is surrounded by women, cattle, and wealth;
it is crowded with garlands and enjoyments, and honored with wonders.
339.021. Under Ārdrā, there will be fish, meat, and wealth consisting of various kinds of food; 339.022.
and in the city, there will be cruel men of a foolish nature. (95)
When Punarvasu is established [as the presiding nakṣatra], the city shines with splendor;
having become abundant in wealth and grain, it eventually perishes. (96)
When the illustrious Puṣya is situated, the wicked subjects become placid;
they are endowed with prosperity, most righteous, and likewise long-lived. (97)
They will be radiant, long-lived, and endowed with wealth, grain, and flavors;
likewise, the lord of the forest (the tree) shall quickly flourish there again and again.
But when [the moon] is situated in Āśleṣā, the lowest of men dwell there—unfortunate, fond of quarreling, ill-behaved, and partakers of suffering. (99)
When the moon is situated in Maghā, mortals are born who are learned, possess great wealth,
delight in their own wives, and are endowed with excellent prowess.
340.001. Under Phālgunī, women [should receive] garlands, auspicious food, and clothing;
340.002. and grains endowed with fragrance shall be found in the settled city. //101//
When Uttaraphalgunī is occupied by Mars, there will be grain and wealth;
however, the people will be foolish and the city will be infested with women.
But when [the moon] is situated in Hasta, those possessing knowledge and great wealth will have agreeable beds with one another in the city. //103//
When the moon is situated in Citrā, all men are dominated by women;
one should declare that city to be prosperous, lovely, and radiant.
When the moon is situated in the asterism of Svāti, there will be a great accumulation of wealth in the city;
however, many people in that city will be greedy, cruel, and foolish.
When the city is situated under Viśākhā, it blazes with splendor;
one should declare it to be filled with people devoted to sacrifice and ending in weapons.
When the moon is situated in Anurādhā, people will be virtuous in character and have conquered their senses;
they will be devoted to their own wives, meritorious, and dedicated to the practice of recitation and fire-offerings.
But when [the moon] is situated in Jyeṣṭhā, the city is filled with beings endowed with many jewels and wealth, who are knowers of the Vedas; it increases constantly.
A city established at Mūla, though endowed with grain and wealth,
becomes crowded with people of immoral character and perishes due to dust.
If the city is situated under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, it shall possess wealth and grain;
yet the lowest of men who dwell there will be greedy, cruel, and foolish.
When Uttarā Phalgunī is established [in the lunar mansion], there is an accumulation of wealth and grain;
moreover, the people will be endowed with knowledge by nature yet fond of quarreling.
When Abhijit was established in that city, all the people there were joyful; they were always delighted and affectionate toward one another.
340.025–026. One should predict that [the country] will be settled in Śravaṇā, endowed with abundant grain and wealth, and filled with a great multitude of healthy people. //113//
If [the moon] is situated in Dhaniṣṭhā, one should predict that the city is ruled by women;
it will have an abundance of garments and garlands, yet be devoid of sensual enjoyments.
When the moon is joined with Śatabhiṣā at the beginning [of the month], people will be fond of folly and deceit;
they will be addicted to women and drink, and they shall perish by water. (115)
341.001. When the moon is in the constellation Pūrvaproṣṭhapadā, the people there are fond of happiness;
341.002. they are harmful to others, foolish, and devoid of pride and desire. //116//
341.003. But when [the asterism] is situated in Uttarā, there is constant and unsurpassed prosperity; one should declare it to be full of wealth and grain and rich in jewels. 117.
341.005. When Revatī has set in the east, the people will be handsome;
341.006. there will be abundance of donkeys, camels, and cattle, as well as great wealth and grain. //118//
341.007. One should declare a city established under Aśvinī to be auspicious;
341.008. it shall be filled with healthy people and crowded with handsome folk. //119//
341.009. But when [the moon] is situated in Bharaṇī, base men who are unfortunate, fond of quarreling, ill-behaved, and partakers of suffering dwell there. (120)

341.011. Having carefully observed the conjunctions of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), a wise man should establish cities, kingdoms, and likewise houses during an auspicious and praised time; this was understood by me in a previous birth. (121)
341.015. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter titled "The Exposition of the Constellations."
341.016. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall proclaim the chapter titled "The Exposition of the Positions of the Twenty-eight Constellations.
341.017. Let that be heard!
341.017. May the Blessed One speak.
341.018. "O Puṣkarasārin, the lunar mansion Kṛttikā belongs to Kaliṅga and Magadha.
Rohiṇī belongs to all subjects.
Mṛgaśiras belongs to Videha and to those who serve the king."
In this way, Ārdrā belongs to the Kṣatriyas and the Brāhmaṇas;
Punarvasu belongs to the Sauparṇas;
and the Puṣya constellation belongs to all those dressed in white garments and to the attendants of the royal court.
341.020. Āśleṣā belongs to the Nāgas and those from the Himalayas. 341.021. The lunar mansion Maghā belongs to the Gauḍikas.
341.021. And Pūrvaphalgunī belongs to the thieves.
341.021. Uttaraphalgunī belongs to the people of Avanti; 341.022. Hastā belongs to the people of Saurāṣṭra;
341.022. Citrā belongs to birds and bipeds.
341.022. Svātī is for all those who have entered the supreme state of renunciation. 341.023. Viśākhā is for those who work with water.
341.023. Anurādhā is for merchants and cart-drivers.
Jyeṣṭhā belongs to the gatekeepers;
Mūlā to the travelers;
and Pūrvāṣāḍhā to the Bāhlīkas.
341.024. Uttarāṣāḍhā belongs to the Kāmbojas; 341.025. Abhijit belongs to all those of the southern regions and the Tāmraparṇikas;
341.025. Śravaṇā belongs to the Ghātakas and the thieves.
341.025. Dhaniṣṭhā belongs to the Kurus and Pañcālas.
341.026. Śatabhiṣā belongs to the Maulikas and the Ātharvaṇikas.
341.026. Pūrvabhādrapadā belongs to the perfumers (gandhika) and the Yavanas and Kambojas.
341.027. Uttarabhādrapadā belongs to the gandharvas; Revatī to the sailors;
and Aśvinī to the horse-dealers.
341.028. Bharaṇī is for those engaged in the work of the Bhadrapadas and for those with auspicious bodies.
341.028. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter titled "The Exposition of the Designation of the Positions of the Constellations."
"Recite, O Triśaṅku, the chapter named 'The Seasonal Oblations' (Ṛtuvaṣa).
I shall speak it; let it be heard.
May the Blessed One explain."
342.001. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Kṛttikā, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas.
342.002. The rain lasts for ten nights.
342.002. When the full moon is in Śravaṇā or Proṣṭhapadā, there will be a lack of water during the rainy season.
342.003. There will be danger from fire, danger from weapons, and danger from water.
342.004. This has been said regarding Kṛttikā.

342.005. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Rohiṇī, he rains twenty-one āḍhakas. In that case, agriculture should be carried out in low-lying areas. 342.006. There, agriculture should be performed in the depressions.
342.006. Dry lands should be avoided.
Furthermore, this rainy season is one of abundant water and brings the crops to maturity.
342.007. However, two diseases become prevalent here.
There will be diseases of the abdomen and diseases of the eyes;
moreover, the quarters of the earth will abound in thieves.
And this has been said regarding Rohiṇī.
342.009. When the god rains during the last month of summer under the asterism Mṛgaśīrṣa, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas.
The rainy season will be one of abundant obstruction.
Afterwards, it produces rain;
the kings there lay down their weapons;
and the quarters of the world become secure and well-governed.
And in this case, the districts become joyful.
Thus it has been said regarding Mṛgaśiras.

342.012. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the constellation Ārdrā, he rains eighteen āḍhakas. In that case, low-lying lands should be cultivated. 342.013. There, depressions should be made for irrigation.
342.013. Dry lands are to be avoided;
342.013. and treasures are to be guarded against.
342.014. Furthermore, the directions there abound with thieves.
The kings will lay down their weapons.
Furthermore, three diseases will prevail there: fever, dyspnea, and throat-obstruction.
There will also be death among children, both boys and girls.
Thus it was said regarding Ārdrā.
342.016. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Punarvasu, he rains ninety āḍhakas; he brings forth great clouds.
342.017. He produces massive rain-clouds.
When Āṣāḍhā has entered, it rains gently;
immediately thereafter, it rains continuously.
And in this [period], kings lay down their weapons.
Furthermore, it was said regarding Punarvasu:
342.019. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Puṣya, he rains thirty-two āḍhakas. In this case, farming should be carried out in low-lying areas.
342.020. Dry lands should be avoided;
it is evident that these are the primary rainy seasons, and they bring the crops to fruition.

342.021. There will be conflict between the brahmins and the kṣatriyas; fanged creatures will become powerful there. Furthermore, three types of diseases will arise: glandular swellings, pustules, and scabies.
Thus it was said regarding Puṣya.

342.023. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Āśleṣā, he rains twenty-one āḍhakas. In that case, agriculture should be carried out in low-lying areas. 342.024. There, agriculture should be performed in the depressions.
342.024. Dry lands are to be avoided.
342.024. And turbulent winds blow there.
342.025. Furthermore, wise men and kings become agitated in such places.
This rain brings all crops to fruition;
however, discord arises between husbands and wives, as well as between kings and their ministers.
Thus it has been said regarding Āśleṣā.
342.027. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the constellation Maghā, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas.
342.028. This rain brings all crops to fruition;
however, the embryos of wild animals, birds, cattle, and humans perish therein.
342.029. "And there will be death among the people here. Thus it was said regarding the Maghā constellation.

342.030. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the constellation Pūrvaphalgunī, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas. This rain brings all the crops to fruition. 342.031. This rain causes all the grain to ripen.
And although that grain is produced, people oppressed by foreign armies do not enjoy it with ease.
The gestations of both animals and humans therein become comfortable.
Thus it was said regarding Pūrvaphalgunī.
343.001. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Uttaraphalgunī, he rains eighty āḍhakas.
One such year brings all things to fulfillment.
In this [age], kings will lay down their weapons;
there will be conflict between the Brahmins and the Kṣatriyas;
and the subjects, lacking righteous governance, will quickly perish.
Thus it was said regarding Uttaraphalgunī.
In the last month of summer, when it is *hasta*, the god rains;
he rains forty-nine *āḍhakas*.
And the god rains exactly as circumscribed.
And the crops will fall, their essence and flavor diminished, lacking vigor, with little nourishment and little water.
There will be famine there;
so it is said in the *Hasta* [constellation].
343.008. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Citrā, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas.
343.009. Thereafter, the rain produces abundant growth and obstructions.
The kings lay down their weapons,
and the people of the countryside become joyful;
this was said regarding the constellation Citrā.
343.011. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Svāti, he rains twenty-one āḍhakas.
343.012. And kings will lay down their weapons.
343.012. And in this case, the thieves become more powerful.
Thus it was said regarding Svāti.
343.013. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Viśākhā, he rains eighty āḍhakas.
343.014. Such a year brings all things to fulfillment.
343.014. Furthermore, kings in this age will be full of flaws; 343.014. fires and conflagrations will be powerful here;
343.015. and even the strong fanged beasts will go to their destruction.
This was said concerning Viśākhā.
343.016. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Anurādhā, he rains sixty āḍhakas.
343.017. And during the last month of summer under Jyeṣṭhā, the crops here become firm.
343.017. Thus it was said regarding Anurādhā.
343.018. If the god rains here during the last month of the summer season in Jyeṣṭha, he rains sixteen āḍhakas.
343.019. In that case, the agricultural operations must be brought to a halt.
343.019. The yokes and traces must be removed.
343.019. One's own grain must be gathered in.
343.020. The sacred fires must be extinguished.
343.020. The plows must be withdrawn.
343.020. This country will inevitably be ruined;
it will be oppressed by a hostile army.
Thus it was said regarding Jyeṣṭhā.
343.022. If the god rains here during the last month of the summer season at its root, he rains sixty-four *āḍhakas*;
one [type of] crop will be brought to fruition.
343.022. Furthermore, the directions there will abound with thieves.
343.023. And three diseases will be powerful there: swellings caused by wind (vātagaṇḍa), pain in the sides (pārśvaśūla), and eye disease (akṣiroga).
343.024. Yet, flowers and fruits will be abundant there.
343.024. And in this [age], kings lay down their weapons.
343.025. This was stated in the root [text].
343.026. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the constellation Pūrvāṣāḍhā, he rains sixty āḍhakas. 343.027.
And there are two seizing factors in this case.

In the month of Proṣṭhapada or in the fortnight of Āśvayuja, one year brings all crops to full maturity. However, two diseases become prevalent during this time: diseases of the stomach and diseases of the eyes.
343.028. This has been said regarding Pūrvāṣāḍhā.

343.029. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Uttarāṣāḍhā, he rains a full hundred āḍhakas. In that case, dry lands should be cultivated. 343.030. Fields for cultivation should be prepared there.
343.030. One should avoid low-lying places.
343.030. Furthermore, great currents flow there, and the water there is extremely cold.
It brings all crops to fruition.
However, three diseases become prevalent there: boils, skin eruptions, and throat ailments. Thus it has been said regarding Uttarāṣāḍhā.
344.001. If the god rains here during the month of Abhijit, the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas; and the god rains in a circular pattern.
344.002. And the god rains in a circular pattern.
344.002. Afterwards, the rain produces crops;
there is a release of watery beings.
Thus it was said regarding Abhijit.
344.004. But if the god rains here during the last month of the summer season in Śrāvaṇa, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas;
and the god rains in a circular pattern.
344.005. Afterwards, the rains bring forth the crops. 344.005. There is an overflow of watery beings. 344.006. And men become afflicted by many diseases.
And kings become severe in their punishments;
this has been stated regarding the asterism Śravaṇa.
344.007. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Dhaniṣṭhā, he rains five and one āḍhakas.
344.008. And in this case, the rains are distributed.
In that case, the low-lying areas should be ploughed and the high ground should be avoided;
for the rain will fall at night and be difficult to endure.
The crops will ripen;
however, there shall be one disease— a swelling of the glands—
and kings will take up arms.
Thus it was said regarding Dhaniṣṭhā.

344.011. If it rains during the last month of summer under the asterism Śatabhiṣā, it rains sixteen āḍhakas. In that case, agriculture should be carried out in low-lying areas. 344.012. There, the fields should be prepared for cultivation in the depressions.
344.012. Dry lands are to be avoided.
344.012. A single rain causes all the crops to ripen.
344.013. The people become mounted upon their chariots.
344.013. Men carry boys and girls upon their shoulders as they travel to other regions.
344.014. This has been said regarding Śatabhiṣā.
344.015. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the constellation Pūrvabhādrapadā, he rains sixty-four āḍhakas. 344.016.
And at the onset of the rainy season, there will be a drought lasting nineteen nights.

344.016. It destroys the flower crops. 344.017. Furthermore, these rains will be accompanied by many thieves. And two great diseases will arise therein: first, there will be a fever born of the heat of bile (pitta).
Afterwards, a powerful great planet arises;
there occurs the death of mortals and women.
Thus it was said regarding Pūrvabhādrapadā.
344.020. If the god rains here during the latter part of the summer under the constellation Uttarabhādrapadā, he rains a full hundred āḍhakas.
344.021. Great torrents flow forth.
344.021. Villages, towns, and market towns are swept away by floods. 344.021. And here, four diseases become prevalent:
namely, stomach disease, eye disease, cough, and fever.
344.022. Death occurs for young boys and girls.
344.023. In this regard, high ground should be used for cultivation;
low-lying areas should be avoided.
And these rains produce flowers and fruits. Thus it has been said regarding Uttarabhādrapadā.
344.025. If it rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Revatī, it rains sixty-one āḍhakas. 344.026. In that case, agriculture should be carried out in low-lying areas.
344.026. Dry lands must be avoided.
344.026. A single rain brings all crops to fruition.
344.027. And those crops are enjoyed by friends, kinsmen, and people alike.
344.027. Kings lay aside the rod of punishment;
344.028. the districts become free from anxiety, yet they also become anxious.
This has been said regarding Revatī.
344.030. If the god rains here during the last month of summer under the asterism Aśvinī, he rains forty-eight āḍhakas.
344.031. And whatever rain falls in the middle of the rainy season, [it is likewise measured].
In that regard, the low-lying areas should be cultivated for agriculture;
the high ground should be avoided.
A single rainy season brings all the crops to fruition.
The regions become beset with fear,
and thieves become powerful.
Thus it has been said regarding Aśvinī.
345.001. If the god rains here during the last [fortnight] of the summer months under the asterism Bharaṇī, he rains a full hundred āḍhakas. In that case, dry lands should be cultivated.
345.002. Low-lying places should be avoided;
for there, famine occurs, and for people there is old age and death.
345.003. Furthermore, in this [constellation], kings become mutual slayers of one another, and strife arises among sons and grandsons. Thus it was said regarding Bharaṇī.
345.005. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter on the constellations, seasons, and rainfall.
345.006. "O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the ripening of the results for these twenty-eight lunar mansions when they are eclipsed by the planet Rāhu.
345.007. O Puṣkarasārin, if there is a lunar eclipse during the Kṛttikās, there will be affliction for the Kaliṅgas and the Magadhas."
345.008. If there is a lunar eclipse in Rohiṇī, there will be suffering for the subjects. 345.008. If there is a lunar eclipse in Mṛgaśiras, [there will be suffering for the subjects].
There will be oppression of the Videha country and of those who serve the king.
345.009. The same should be declared for Ārdrā, Punarvasu, and Puṣya.
345.010. If there is a lunar eclipse in Āśleṣā, [the following occurs].
There will be suffering for the Nāgas and those from the Himalayas.
If there is a lunar eclipse during the Madhā constellation, there will be affliction for the Gauḍikas.
345.011. If the moon is seized while in Pūrvaphalgunī, there will be affliction for thieves. 345.012. If the moon is seized while in Uttaraphalgunī, [there will be affliction for kings].
There will be affliction for the Avantīs.
If the moon is seized in the Hasta constellation,
there will be affliction for the Saurāṣṭrikas.
345.013. If the Soma is drawn under Citrā, there will be suffering for birds and bipeds.
345.014. If the Soma is drawn under Svātī, [there will be suffering for quadrupeds].
There is suffering for all who have entered the religious life.
If the moon is seized during the asterism Viśākhā,
there is suffering for aquatic beings.

345.016. If the moon is seized during Anurādhā, there will be affliction for merchants and carters. 345.017. If the moon is seized during Jyeṣṭhā, [there will be affliction for those who live by water].
There will be suffering for the gatekeepers.
If the Moon is seized in Mūla,
there will be suffering for those traveling on the road.

345.018. If the moon is seized while in Pūrvāṣāḍhā, there will be suffering for the people of Avanti. 345.019. If the moon is seized while in Uttarāṣāḍhā, [there will be suffering for the people of the Śakas].
There will be suffering for the Kāmbojas and the Vāhlīkas.
If the moon is seized while the moon is in Abhijit,
there will be suffering for those of the southern region and for the inhabitants of Tāmraparṇī.

345.020. If the Soma is drawn during the Śravaṇa asterism, there will be affliction for thieves and murderers. 345.021. If the Soma is drawn during Dhaniṣṭhā, [there will be affliction for those who live by weapons].
There is suffering for the Kurus and Pañcālas.
If the Soma is drawn under Śatabhiṣaj, there is suffering for the Maulikas and the Ātharvaṇikas.

345.023. If the moon is seized in Pūrvabhādrapadā, there will be suffering for perfumers and for the Yavanas and Kambojas. 345.024. If the moon is seized in Uttarabhādrapadā, [there will be suffering for the same].
If Soma is drawn under Revatī, there will be suffering for the Gandharvas; if it is drawn under Revatī,
there will be suffering for the boatmen.
345.025. If the Soma is taken under Aśvinī, there will be suffering for horse-dealers.
345.025. If the Soma is taken under Bharaṇī, [there will be suffering for those who carry burdens].
There will be suffering for the people of Bharukaccha.
345.027. Thus, O Puṣkarasārin, in whichever lunar mansion a lunar eclipse occurs, there will be affliction for that particular region.
345.028. Thus ends the chapter on the ripening of the results of the Rāhu eclipse.
345.029. Listen to the rites as they are described in the *Pratinakṣatravaṃśaśāstra*.
345.030. O Brahmin, this which is being spoken is according to the words of the ṛṣis. (122)

One should know that Kṛttikā consists of six stars; one should perform the taking of refuge under them, as well as the installation of the sacred fire, the domestic sacrifices (pākayajña), and whatever brings about prosperity and progeny. (122a)
346.001. One should stir clarified butter there and construct a cowshed. 346.002.
Goats and sheep should be purchased, and a bull should be released for the cows. //123//
346.003. One should have all the vessels here made of stone; 346.004. one should also cause the work of goldsmiths, as well as archery and weaponry, to be practiced.
346.005. Metṛka should measure out here a small hut and a place for fire;
346.006. furthermore, one should sow there the seeds of yellow and red flowers. //125//
346.007. One should have a house built here and likewise arrange a dwelling; 346.008.
one should wear new clothing and should not engage in buying or selling here. //126//
346.009. Cruel deeds such as war, siege, and imprisonment are accomplished [under these conditions].
346.010. However, a wise person should not employ even these for the purpose of harming others. //127//
346.011. One should have all types of weapons and surgical instruments made here; 346.012. one should also have vessels made of metal and purchase them. //128//
346.013. Bathing the head promotes longevity, as do protective charms for women;
346.014. yet if there is excessive rain from the god, the enmity here will not be pacified. //129//

One born under Kṛttikā is prone to anger, yet is joyful, brave, radiant, and fond of daring deeds; such a person is long-lived, famous, and devoted to the performance of sacrifices. //130// Under Kṛttikā.
346.017. One should employ all agricultural work under Rohiṇī.
346.018. One should cause fields, property, monasteries, and new houses to be built.
One should employ wheel-turners, weavers, servants, and livestock in the house;
one should sow all kinds of seeds and certainly have garments woven.
One should not repay a debt there, for in this case enmity increases;
one should avoid both war and the consumption of liquor. (133)
346.023. The raining of the god [Indra] and his birth are praised here.

346.024. One born under Rohiṇī is compassionate, endowed with patience, fond of women, and greedy for food. 346.025. He is long-lived, possesses cattle, is fortunate, and is born here with great enjoyments. //134// Under Rohiṇī.
One should know that Mṛgaśiras is gentle and consists of three straight stars.
One should perform all those actions which are mild under this asterism. One should also perform all those actions which are prescribed for Rohiṇī.
One should cause trees that yield milk and seeds that produce milky sap to be planted;
one should also cause royal palaces, turrets, and parasols to be constructed.
346.031. One may engage in discourse on all types of work, but one should not cause [others] to dwell in the practice of worldly conduct.
346.032. One should even break in oxen and bulls for the purpose of plowing. //137//
347.001. One should clothe [the officiant] in new garments and provide him with ornaments;
347.002. indeed, one should have all the rites for the twice-born performed here.
One should predict abundant rainfall and excellent showers from the god here;
likewise, such a person becomes inclined toward sleep, fearful, yet wise. (139)
In Mṛgaśiras.
347.005. Under Ārdrā, one should seek wealth and perform auspicious deeds.
347.006. Cruel acts succeed under this asterism; therefore, the wise man should avoid them. //140//
347.007. He should cause wells, ditches, and ponds to be constructed there.
347.008. He should wait for the first rain to fall, and he should not sell cattle at that time.
347.009. There are the occupations of oil-pressers and likewise the shops of liquor-sellers. //141//
One should crush stalks of sugarcane or sow seeds of sugarcane;
one should know that there will be rain from the god with abundant flow.
One born under Ārdrā becomes irascible, fond of hunting, and desirous of meat. (142) Under Ārdrā.
Furthermore, when the moon is conjoined with Punarvasu, one should indeed undertake the observance of vows;
the gift of a cow and the initiation ceremony—all these are successfully accomplished here.
One should take a woman who is giving birth and bring her home;
if one so desires, one may have her perform tasks there again and again.
347.017. One should not practice medical treatment if one desires no defeat.
347.018. Furthermore, the rain of the deity and birth are praised during this time. (145)
In this regard, a person may become restless, or even fickle toward women;
such a one is said to be of variegated character, with a mind that is not fixed upon a single object. (146)
In Punarvasu.
One should always employ [rites] under the Puṣya asterism; they bring fortune, fame, and long life.
One may have all the various rites performed by all members of the twice-born classes.
One should employ the king’s minister and practice service and discipline;
one should consecrate the king and adorn one's own body.
One should perform the work of shaving the beard and the clipping of hair and nails;
one should appoint a domestic priest and cause a banner-top to be fashioned.
One should predict that the rain from the god will be light; there shall be neither disease nor thieves, and there will always be security in this place.
347.029. Being constantly joined with Puṣya, one should accomplish all rites.
347.030. One should avoid those people who are hostile or who employ emetics and purgatives.
347.031. Under Puṣya, one is born long-lived, illustrious, and possessed of great wealth. //151// Puṣya.
348.001. A fierce rite is accomplished under Āśleṣā, and one should perform it then; 348.002. one may here provide hard-to-grasp ornaments and construct a rampart.
348.003. One should undertake the construction of buildings, the building of dams, and the performance of treaties.
348.004. There will be an abundance of gadflies and mosquitoes, and the rain falls only sparingly.
348.005. A person born here under Āśleṣā is prone to anger, habitually sleeps much, and is deceitful. //153// Under Āśleṣā.
Under Maghā, one should sow all kinds of grain and also gather them in;
one should perform collective undertakings and have a pleasant face fashioned here.
348.008. One should construct storehouses and deposit grain therein.
348.009. And one should always perform the *śrāddha* ceremony here for the ancestors and the gods. //155//
348.010. If the rain-god pours down rain here, there will be an abundance of crops.
348.011. One becomes a friend, a gatekeeper, and one who desires savory flavors. 348.012. He is long-lived, has many sons, is fond of women, and is greedy for food. //156//
In that battle, one who initiates the attack first is defeated;
therefore, the wise man should avoid such cruel deeds under the Maghā asterism.

348.015. Under the *pūrvaphalgunī* asterisms, one should perform rites for the sake of good fortune. 348.017. One should also have auspicious ceremonies performed for young maidens and have them undergo ritual bathing.
348.018. And one should likewise cause a monastery (*vihāra*) to be built for the purpose of conveying a maiden [in marriage]. //159//
348.019. One should have houses constructed there and employ a Vaiśya for this purpose. 348.020. One should also employ those who subsist on their share [of the produce] to perform the work. //160//
One with indistinct hair, or even hairless, is born here as fortunate;
one should predict abundant rain and excellent showers from the god.
One should declare that whatever is lost, pierced, or done no longer exists.
Under Pūrvaphalgunī.
Under Uttaraphalgunī, however, one should have all rites performed;
under this [asterism], one is born intelligent, handsome, and renowned. (162)
348.026. Then, one should declare that everything lost or burnt therein has been recovered. 348.027. And one should know that the raining of the god signifies unsurpassed prosperity. (163)
In Uttaraphalgunī.
348.028. With his hand, he should perform all light tasks;
348.029. and he should cause all the twice-born to perform all their duties. //164//
One should have an elephant-rider mahout construct a lotus pond;
however, theft is successful there, and therefore the wise man should avoid it.
349.001. When the rain-god pours down rain that is heard throughout the rainy season, 349.002. one should know that a child born at this time will be a hero, a thief, and wise;
349.003. skilled in all branches of knowledge, free from disease, and long-lived. (In the *Hasta* nakṣatra. //166//
349.004. Under Citrā, one should have new clothes and ornaments made.
