349.005. One should look upon a king adorned with finery and observe the array of an army. //167//
349.006. One should measure out gold, silver, wealth, and cities;
349.007. and likewise, one should adorn oneself with perfumes, garlands, and ointments. //168//
He should teach the science of calculation, as well as instrumental music, dancing, and singing;
he should train former artisans in metalwork and chariot-making,
and have painters, scribes, and those skilled in book-making perform their crafts.
One should predict a rain of diverse colors from the deity during the Pravarṣaṇa period.
[The person born then] will be intelligent, handsome, have variegated eyes, and be greedy for food.
Under Citrā, one is born gentle in character, timid, fickle-minded, and curious; moreover, such a person is long-lived, fortunate, and lustful toward women. (171)
Under Svāti, one should mobilize warriors, horses, mules, and donkeys; as well as those who carry provisions for rapid travel, food supplies, porters, and road-maintenance workers.
One should cause kettledrums, clay drums, small drums, and large drums to be sounded;
and one should arrange for invitations, marriages, and acts of friendship therein.
349.019. There is banishment of enemies, yet one does not depart from one's home of one's own accord.
349.020. There is heavy rainfall from the god of rain, and wind and rain occur frequently.
349.021. One is born intelligent but with many ailments and a fickle mind. (174) [Under] Svāti.
349.022. Under the asterism Viśākhā, one should employ ploughs and the work of tilling;
349.023. however, one should avoid operations involving barley, wheat, and pulse crops. //175//
349.024. One should plant rice, sesame, beans, and trees with beautiful branches under Viśākhā; one should also undertake house-building work. 349.025–026.
One should perform head-baths and generally carry out purificatory rites. (176)
One should know that under the rain-god (Parjanya), there is a continuous flow like that of a kalpa.
One born here is high-minded, handsome, and intelligent.
Under Viśākhā, one is prone to anger, has few children, is unfortunate, and is greedy for food. //177//
Under Anurādhā, one should cultivate association with friends and virtuous people;
all gentle actions and sweetness should be practiced here.
350.001. One should have a haircut performed here, and one should have surgical operations carried out.
350.002. One should employ the application of joined ends and should constantly form alliances.
350.003. One may predict that what is lost or afflicted by distress will be recovered with little effort. //179//
350.004. Furthermore, one is born here with virtuous character, surrounded by friends and well-wishers.
350.005. One should predict that the rain-god will send down a bountiful and excellent rainfall. 180.
Under Anurādhā.
350.006. Under Jyeṣṭhā, one should be a pioneer; one should consecrate a king. 350.007.
One should measure out and begin the construction of cities, market towns, and villages.
350.008. One should cause all the duties of kṣatriyas and kings to be performed. //181//
Among brothers, he who is born of the eldest wife becomes the eldest;
he is long-lived, renowned, and takes great interest in the learned.
In this situation, one should ascend a palace, an elephant, a horse, or likewise a chariot;
and within villages, towns, and kingdoms, one should station the army under the leadership of a merchant-chief.
One should declare that what is lost or consumed by distress is due solely to affliction (*kleśa*).
A wise person should avoid those [omens] where cruel things are accomplished. Furthermore, one should predict good rain when there is a downpour from the sky. (184)
In Jyeṣṭhā.
At the root, however, one should employ all those things produced from roots, such as radishes, tubers, and bulbs, as well as all seeds beginning with roots.
Whether there be an old debt or some objective standing before one, everything—beginning with the primary limb for the sake of accomplishing the root—should be undertaken in that manner. 186.
350.020. Whatever medical treatments there are here for women, boys, and girls, 350.021. as well as bathing in rivers—one should employ all of these at the foot of the tree. //187//
350.022. Here, formidable rites are accomplished, and one should perform auspicious ceremonies.
350.023. One should not prepare preparations of fermenting agents or wine in association with enemies. 188.
One born here under Mūla becomes wealthy, possesses many sons, and is endowed with roots (foundations).
Furthermore, one should declare that whatever is lost or burnt here does not exist [to be recovered].
One should also predict excellent rain when the god sends down showers. (189) —[In the case of] Mūla.
In the month of Āṣāḍha and under the Pūrvāṣāḍhā constellation, one should cause rivers and lakes,
as well as ponds, wells, water-stations, and tanks to be constructed.
One should cultivate flowers as well as roots and fruits; one should establish pleasure groves and employ those who subsist on alms.
Furthermore, those fierce rites which are successful here [are also to be performed].
351.001. One should declare that what has been lost or acquired no longer exists.
351.002. There, one is born long-lived, virtuous in conduct, and handsome. (192)
In Pūrvāṣāḍhā.
351.003. Under Uttarāṣāḍhā, one should not engage in enmities.
351.004. One may have all clothes woven, but one should not put on new ones. //193//

351.005. One should neither seize nor cause division regarding building sites; otherwise, the architectural work will not succeed. 351.006. Likewise, the king should oversee the construction of halls for cattle and other livestock, as well as for the village headman in the village.
351.007. Furthermore, the king shall establish guilds and enforce the agreements therein. (194)

351.008. One who is born under this [asterism] becomes bold, sociable in assemblies, and accomplished. 351.009. He is diligent in the service of friends and discerning in the discussion of counsel. //195//
One should predict that what is lost or afflicted will indeed be recovered;
and one should predict that the rain of the god [Indra] will be well-showered. //196//
In Uttarāṣāḍhā.
351.012. One should not perform the worship of Brahmadeva during the Abhijit [nakṣatra]. During Abhijit.
One should not perform any martial activities under Śravaṇā;
likewise, the study of vocal training and song will indeed be accomplished without delay.
One should perform the piercing of the ears and consecrate the king;
furthermore, one should employ all the ritual duties of the twice-born.
One should perform offerings and also display one's powers; there, one is born intelligent, free from disease, strong, and devoted to sacrifice. (200)
351.019. One should predict that the rain will fall as a well-timed, bountiful shower.
351.020. And what has been lost is recovered there when the Moon is situated in Śravaṇā. [201] In Śravaṇā.
351.021. Dhaniṣṭhā is a light asterism, honored for all undertakings.
351.022. Having completed his studies, a Brāhmaṇa should perform the ceremonial bath; a king should have himself consecrated [under this asterism]. //202//
He should cause all the twice-born to perform all their prescribed duties;
he should appoint a merchant-leader in the country and a head of the guilds among the guilds.
One who is born here becomes intelligent, renowned, possessed of great enjoyments and great wealth; he has many offspring, is gentle, self-controlled, and high-souled. (204)
351.027. What is lost, burnt, or cast away is recovered here through nothing but mental affliction (kleśa).
351.028. One should know that when the god rains, it constitutes a well-timed and beneficial shower. //205//
In Dhaniṣṭhā.
351.029. One should always administer medicines during the conjunction with Śatabhiṣā;
351.030. one should also perform acts for renown, and the rites of the Atharvaveda will succeed. //206//
352.001. One should spread out merchandise and employ a liquor-seller.
352.002. There, one should have a reservoir dug and sow sesame and beans. //207//
352.003. One should employ maritime merchandise and ships;
352.004. one should take what is to be taken from them and should not incur expenditure therein. //208//
352.005. He should employ boundary guards, gatekeepers, and scribes;
352.006. he should practice medical treatment and collect medicinal herbs. //209//
352.007. One may have a treasure-trove excavated there, or one may deposit a treasure there.
352.008. One should invest wealth here and also learn the art of medicine. //210//
352.009. Furthermore, if one searches for what is lost here, it will be found even after a long time.
352.010. One born under this [asterism] becomes free from disease yet prone to anger, and has a tendency toward sleep.
352.011. One should predict that there will be rain from the god, and that it will be a good rainfall. //211//
In Śatabhiṣā.
352.012. In the conjunction of Pūrvabhādrapadā, the accomplishment of cruel deeds is said to occur.
352.013. One should declare that what is lost, pierced, or afflicted does not exist [as such]. //212//
One born under this [asterism] has long ears, great wealth, and is always beloved by their kinsmen. Possessing vast riches, they perform no cruel deeds and are free from anger.
Furthermore, one should predict heavy rainfall and fierce showers from the god of rain. //213//
In Pūrvabhādrapadā.
352.017. However, one should perform rites for longevity and prosperity in the north.
352.018. One should not go toward the south, and one should cause a city to be established there. //214//
One is born here long-lived, illustrious, and wealthy.
In this case as well, one should find a threefold increase in either income or expenditure.
One should predict that the god will send rain, resulting in a bountiful harvest.
In Uttarabhādrapadā.
In Revatī, one should employ gems, silver, wealth, and grain; one should construct storehouses, but one should not produce fermenting agents (kinva) therein.
352.024. One should perform the work of brewing liquor, [deal in] gold, and [tend] herds of cattle.
352.025. One should establish a herd of cows here and have a cowshed built here.
352.026. One should clothe oneself in new clothing and also wear gold. //217//
One born under Revatī becomes a mendicant, generous in nature, poor, yet free from envy;
he is always a servant to his kinsmen and is knowledgeable in the Dharma.
One should predict good rain and the recovery of lost property for one born under Revatī. //218// Under Revatī.
352.030. The Aśvins should unite man and woman, and one should cause a horse stable to be constructed.
352.031. One should employ horses here, and one should also employ a chariot here. //219//
353.001. One should engage in lending money at interest and sow seeds there;
353.002. one should employ vehicles, horses, draft animals, and elephants. //220//
353.003. Administer medicine here and have medical treatment performed.
353.004. He will be sweet-tempered, handsome, and endowed with prosperity worthy of a king. //221//
353.005. One who is healthy, strong, brave, and indeed fortunate is born here.
353.006. One should predict good rain and the recovery of lost property under Aśvinī. (222) Under Aśvinī.
One should know that Bharaṇī consists of three stars; one should accomplish cruel deeds under it.
Likewise, one should select servants and laborers, and show them [the way].

353.009. In this case, one should provide him with wages, but one must not marry off his wife. 353.010. One who is prone to squatting, a deceiver, a false witness, and one born of a fraudulent marriage—these are the types [to be avoided]. //224//
One born under Bharaṇī becomes knowledgeable in ritual procedures, yet is of evil conduct and miserly.
One born here is ill-behaved and envious of one's teachers; one who torments others, greedy, and intent on slandering others. (225) [In Bharaṇī.]
When the twenty-seven lunar mansions, beginning with Kṛttikā and ending with Bharaṇī, are present,
one should perform this rite.

353.016. Among them, whenever all the crops, medicinal herbs, and forest trees are afflicted where that planet stands, 353.017–353.018. everything [regarding those afflictions] should be established according to the rites prescribed for the aforementioned lunar mansions. //227//
353.019. Thus ends the chapter entitled "The Exposition of the Activities of the Lunar Mansions."
"O Puṣkarasārin, there are four constellations that are fixed.
I shall explain them;
listen to that."
353.021. Namely: the three *uttarās* and Rohiṇī.
353.021. One should dwell in safety;
353.021. and one should sow seeds there.
353.021. And one should construct a residence here;
353.022. and one should consecrate a king;
353.022. and one should cause whatever other rites have been mentioned to be performed.
353.023. Then, whether it be lost, burnt, pierced, or even stolen, 353.024.
or if it has been thus pointed out [as lost], well-being will quickly come to pass. //228//
353.025. Then, one born here will be fortunate, possessed of knowledge, and renowned; 353.026. he will be auspicious, a possessor of great wealth, and a great yogi. //229//
353.027. O Puṣkarasārin, there are four constellations that are swift:
namely, Puṣya, Hastā, Abhijit, and Aśvinī.
353.028. In these, a wise person should have swift tasks performed.

353.028. One should undertake the recitation of sacred texts, the performance of mantras, setting out on journeys, and also employ cattle and horses here. 353.029. One should also employ draft animals for their assigned tasks and the application of medicinal herbs.
353.030. All medicinal remedies should be administered here.
353.031. There, one should cause the commencement of a sacrifice and the performance of the Cāturmāsya rites.
Furthermore, in this case, it should be declared: "Whatever has been lost, burnt, or pierced shall become well."
354.001. Now, one should know that there is a Jātaka here concerning a fortunate, illustrious king, a great enjoyer, a great yogin, and a lord. //230//
One who possesses great wealth and great enjoyments, as well as great and supreme [status];
a Kṣatriya who is generous by nature, and a Brāhmaṇa who serves as a domestic priest. //231// Thus it is said.
354.005. Indeed, Puṣkarasārin, there are five constellations that are cruel: namely—354.006. Maghā, the three Pūrvas, and Bharaṇī as the fifth.
354.007. Then, in this case, there will be nothing burnt, lost, or pierced. //232//
Thus it should be stated:
there are six [constellations] belonging to the midnight period,
namely— Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Svātī, Jyeṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, and Bharaṇī.
354.009. The nine divisions consist of six portions and two fields:
Rohiṇī, Punarvasu, and Viśākhā;
and the three Uttaras—these are the constellations with divisions on both sides.
354.010. There are fifteen fields:
Kṛttikā, Maghā, Mūlā, and the three Pūrvas. 354.011. These six belong to the eastern portion.

354.011. Mṛgaśirā, Puṣyā, Hastā, Citrā, Anurādhā, Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Revatī, and Aśvinī—these nine lunar mansions belong to the western quarter; they have a conjunction of thirty muhūrtas and are [each] a field.
Moreover, O Brahmin, there are auspicious moments (muhūrta), there are inauspicious moments, and there are moments that are both auspicious and inauspicious.

354.015. When all the conjunctions of the lunar mansions coincide with auspicious moments (*muhūrta*), they are then considered favorable. 354.016. When they coincide with inauspicious moments, [they are not].
At that time, they do not become auspicious.
But when both the auspicious and inauspicious attainments occur,
then they become common.
354.018. Now, it is explained how the decrease and increase of nights and days occur therein:
in the first month of the rainy season, the Puṣya constellation coincides with the new moon, and the Śravaṇā constellation coincides with the full moon.
The day consists of eighteen muhūrtas;
the night consists of twelve muhūrtas.
At midday, when the shadow of a sixteen-aṅgula stick is half an aṅgula long, the sun shifts its position.
The night of Āṣāḍhā passes;
the sun has entered Mṛgaśiras.
In the second month of the rainy season, Maghā occurs on the new moon day.
On the full moon day of Bhādrapada,
the day consists of seventeen muhūrtas and the night consists of thirteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is two finger-breadths long, the sun turns back; the moon in Śravaṇā brings on the night;
and the sun has reached Puṣya.
In the third month of the rainy season, on the new moon day of Phālguna, the moon is in Aśvinī;
on the full moon day, it is in Aśvinī. The day consists of sixteen muhūrtas.
The night consists of fourteen muhūrtas. When the shadow is four finger-breadths long, the sun turns back. The constellation Pūrvabhādrapadā brings the night to its end.
354.027. When the sun has entered the constellation Maghā,
in the fourth month of the rainy season, Citrā occurs on the new moon day and Kṛttikā on the full moon day.
The day consists of fifteen muhūrtas;
the night consists of fifteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is six aṅgulas long, the sun changes its course.
354.028. Aśvinī leads the night.
354.028. The Sun has gone to Phalgunī.
In the first month of winter, Anurādhā occurs on the new moon day and Mṛgaśiras on the full moon day.
The day consists of fourteen muhūrtas.
The night consists of sixteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is eight finger-breadths long, the sun turns back.
The constellation Kṛttikā brings on the night.
355.001. When the sun has entered Citrā, it is the second month of winter; on the new moon day, Jyeṣṭhā occurs, and Puṣya occurs on the full moon day.
The day consists of thirteen muhūrtas;
the night consists of seventeen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is ten digits long, the sun changes its position.
The moon passes through Mṛgaśirā during the night;
the sun has entered Viśākhā.
In the third month of winter, Pūrvāṣāḍhā occurs on the day of the new moon.
During the full moon of the month of Māgha,
the day consists of twelve muhūrtas,
and the night consists of eighteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is twelve finger-breadths long, the sun begins its course; the moon stays with the constellation Puṣya during the night;
and when the moon is in Jyeṣṭhā, the sun has reached its northern limit.
In the fourth month of winter, the new moon falls on the day of Śravaṇā;
the full moon falls on the day of Phalgunī.
At that time, the day consists of thirteen muhūrtas.
The night consists of seventeen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is ten digits long, the sun revolves;
the constellation Maghā brings on the night.
355.008. When the sun has entered Āṣāḍhā.
355.010. In the first month of summer, the new moon occurs under Uttarabhādrapadā, and the full moon under Citrā. 355.011. The day consists of fourteen muhūrtas.
The night consists of sixteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is eight finger-breadths long, the sun turns back;
it brings about the night of Phalgunī.
In the month of Śrāvaṇa, the sun has entered [the asterism] Āditya.
In the second month of summer, on the new moon day, it is in Aśvinī;
on the full moon day, it is in Viśākhā.
The day consists of fifteen muhūrtas;
the night consists of fifteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is six aṅgulas long, the sun changes its course.
355.014. The night passes under the constellation Citrā. 355.015. When the sun has entered Uttarabhādrapadā, it is the third month of summer, and Kṛttikā occurs on the new moon day.
On the full moon day of Jyeṣṭha,
the day consists of sixteen muhūrtas,
and the night consists of fourteen muhūrtas.
When the shadow is four finger-breadths long, the sun turns back;
Viśākhā brings on the night;
the sun has entered Kṛttikā.
In the fourth month of summer, Mṛgaśiras occurs on the new moon day, and Uttarāṣāḍhā on the full moon day.
The day consists of seventeen muhūrtas.
The night consists of thirteen muhūrtas.
At midday, when the shadow is two finger-breadths long, the sun turns back;
it brings about the longest night.
355.020. The sun has entered the asterism Puṣya.

355.021. Through a year-long investigation by means of specific moments (*muhūrta*), all these [constellations] (*nakṣatras*) are joined with their respective portions at the new moon and the full moon. 355.022. The deficient night and the full night are to be taken into account.
In that third year, an intercalary month occurs.
During six months, the days and nights are equal;
therefore, from that sixth month, the day begins to increase.
For six months the night increases;
for six months the day decreases by the same amount month by month;
for six months the night decreases month by month.
355.026. After six months, the sun turns back;
it travels toward the northern direction for six months, and [then] toward the southern direction for six months.

355.027. Within six months, there occurs a decrease and an increase in the volume of water in the ocean. 355.027. Through the movement of the sun and the movement of the moon, the tide of the ocean's waters increases.
355.028. In this regard, one should maintain mindfulness through calculation and vigilance.
355.028. Thus the year is explained.
355.029. The Moon, the Sun, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Mercury—these are the planets.
Among these planets, Jupiter is the one who abides throughout the year.
In this way, Śanaiścara, Budha, Aṅgāraka, and Śukra—these are the planets that move in their respective orbits.
355.031. Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, and Mṛgaśirā—these constitute the first common circle.
355.031. Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, and Aśleṣā—these constitute the second common circle.
355.032. Maghā, the two Phalgunīs, Hastā, and Citrā—these constitute the third common circle.
356.001. Svātī, Viśākhā, and Anurādhā—this is the fourth common *maṇḍala*.
356.001. Jyeṣṭhā, Mūlā, and the two Āṣāḍhās—all great dangers occur here.
356.002. This is the fifth *maṇḍala*.

356.002. Abhijit, Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, and both Bhādrapadas—this is the sixth lunar mansion circle, shared by these. 356.003. Revatī and Aśvinī—this is the seventh lunar mansion circle, shared by these.
356.004. If, throughout the year, any lunar mansion circle among these is afflicted, [it portends misfortune].
The affliction of that particular country or of that particular being must be pointed out.
There are twelve fixed *muhūrta*s in the day and twelve in the night;
six *muhūrta*s are variable.
356.006. Which six? Nairṛta, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Bhargodeva, Raudra, and Vicārī.
356.007. These are the six who move about.
356.008. Now, in this month of Śrāvaṇa, when the day has eighteen muhūrtas and the sun has risen, there occurs the muhūrta named Caturoja.
356.009. Midday occurs between the muhūrtas Rohita and Bala.
At the setting of the sun, however, there occurs the muhūrta named Vicārī.
356.010. When the sun has descended during a night of twelve *muhūrtas*, at the sixth *muhūrta*, there occurs the *muhūrta* named Nayamāna.
356.011. At the end of the night, there occurs the *muhūrta* named Ātapāgni.
356.011. When the month of Bhādrapada is full, on a day of seventeen *muhūrtas*, at sunrise, there occurs the *muhūrta* named Caturoja.
At midday, there is the muhūrta named Abhijit. At the sun's descent, there is the muhūrta named Raudra.
When the sun has descended into the night of thirteen muhūrtas, there is the muhūrta named Vicārī.
At midnight, there occurs the moment called Mahābhaya, which is the *muhūrta* named Vāyu.
At the end of the night, there occurs a muhūrta called Ātapāgni.
When the month of Āśvayuja is full, the day consists of sixteen muhūrtas. At sunrise, there occurs a muhūrta called Caturaja.
356.016. Between the muhūrta Samudgata and Abhijit, it becomes midday.
356.017. At the descent of the sun, the muhūrta named Bhargodeva occurs.

When the sun has descended during the night consisting of fourteen muhūrtas, there occurs the muhūrta named Raudra. Midnight occurs between the muhūrta of Abhijit and the muhūrta of Bhīṣamaṇa. At the end of the night, there occurs the muhūrta named Ātapāgni.
In the full month of Kārtika, the day and night are equal;
the day consists of fifteen muhūrtas,
and the night consists of fifteen muhūrtas.
356.022. When the day and night are equal, at sunrise, there is a muhūrta named Caturoja.
356.022. At midday, there is a muhūrta named Saṃmukha.
356.023. At sunset, there is a muhūrta named Saṃtata.

356.023. As soon as the sun has descended at night, there occurs the muhūrta named Bhargodeva. 356.024. At midnight, there occurs the muhūrta named Abhijit. 356.024. At the end of the night, there occurs the muhūrta named Ātapāgni.
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, when the day consists of fourteen muhūrtas, at sunrise, the muhūrta named Caturoja occurs.
Between the muhūrtas of Virata and Saṃmukha, midday occurs. At the setting of the sun, the muhūrta named Varuṇa occurs.
356.028. When the sun has just descended during a night of sixteen *muhūrtas*, there occurs the *muhūrta* named Saṃtāpana (the Heating).
356.029. Midnight occurs between the *muhūrta* of Rākṣasa and the *muhūrta* of Abhijit.
At the end of the night, there occurs the *muhūrta* named Ātapāgni (the Fire of Heat).
357.001. In the month of Pauṣa, when the day consists of thirteen muhūrtas, at sunrise there occurs the muhūrta named Caturoja.
357.002. At midday, there occurs the muhūrta named Virata.
357.002. At sunset, there occurs the muhūrta named Nairṛta.
When the sun has just set during a night of seventeen muhūrtas, the muhūrta is named Varuṇa. At midnight, the muhūrta is named Rākṣasa. At the end of the night, the muhūrta is named Ātapāgni.
357.005. In the month of Māgha, when the day consists of twelve muhūrtas, the muhūrta named Caturoja occurs at sunrise.
Between the muhūrtas of Sāvitra and Virata, midday occurs. At the descent of the sun, the muhūrta named Vijaya occurs.
357.007. When the sun has just descended during a night of eighteen muhūrtas, the muhūrta named Nairṛta occurs.
Between the muhūrta of Gardabha and that of Rākṣasa lies midnight.
At the end of the night, the muhūrta named Ātapāgni occurs.
As it is in Śrāvaṇa, so it is in Māgha;
as it is in Bhādrapada, so it is in Phālguna;
as it is in Āśvayuja, so it is in Caitra.
As it is in Kārttika, so it is in Vaiśākha;
as it is in Mārgaśīrṣa, so it is in Jyeṣṭha;
as it is in Pauṣa, so it is in Āṣāḍha.
357.010. Thus, the movement and the course of these lunar mansions and the muhūrtas should be understood.
Chapter One: The Examination of the Constellations.
357.012. Just as the middle of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*) undergoes increase and decrease according to the night and the day;
357.012. whether the days or months are decreasing or increasing, or when a full month, a half-month, or even a fortnight has passed;
357.013. within this interval—on the second, sixth, ninth, twelfth, and fourteenth days—the digit (*kalā*) of the moon increases.
At night, the digit wanes.
357.015. Four great kings sustain the earth: Ativṛddhi, Viśuddha, Vardhamāna, and Pṛthakśravas. (233)
The four great elements cause the earth to tremble:
water, Indra, wind, and likewise the Blessed One, fire. (234)
When those three occur on one side, there are six such onsets within a single month;
this would be an omen of another wheel [of fortune], wherein the earth trembles repeatedly. (235)
Viśākhā lasts for ten nights; Jyeṣṭhā lasts for twelve nights; Āṣāḍhā lasts for twenty-five nights; and Śravaṇā lasts for seventy-five nights. (236)
A hundred nights are prescribed for the sacrifice in the month of Bhādrapada; in the month of Āśvayuja, it is remembered as half [a hundred];
in the month of Kārttika, it is one and a half; and in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the sacrifice is remembered [as two]. //237//
In the month of Pauṣa, fifty-five [days], and in Māgha, one hundred nights are recorded;
in the month of Phālguna, one hundred and fifty, and in Caitra, thirty nights.
From these, the ripening of the earth's forces proceeds as an earthquake. (238)

357.030. When the earth trembles continuously throughout all the months, and likewise when trees shake or if the water quivers; 357.032. and if a mountain should tremble like a leaf, one should predict fear in this case. //239//
Then cities, villages, and cowherd settlements, and whoever dwelt therein,
quickly become desolate forests, becoming the refuge of wild beasts.
358.003. Wildernesses will prevail for fifteen years.
358.004. One should know that the quarters are devoid of inhabitants, shaken by earthquakes. (241)
358.005. When the earth trembles under the asterism Kṛttikā, whether in villages or in cities, 358.006. fire is released frequently and it consumes the grass huts. //242//
Black fire, the fall of thunderbolts, blacksmiths, and those who have taken up their abodes— their dwellings are destroyed, just as the elements are dissolved at the time of cosmic dissolution.
358.009. Those who have been born, those who have grown up, and those who depend upon that village—all these shall encounter misfortune when shaken by an earthquake. //244//
358.011. When the earth trembles under Rohiṇī, there is the destruction of all seeds. 358.012. Even sown grain will not sprout, and there will be difficulty in obtaining fruit. //245//
The fetuses of pregnant women will be severely oppressed;
the people will remain in a state of ruin, overcome by the calamity of famine for three parts [of the time]. (246)
358.015. Even high-souled kings, glorious and the best among men, 358.016. these fall into calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //247//
When the asterism Mṛgaśīrṣa moves, the earth trembles and there is the destruction of medicinal herbs;
physicians, Vedic scholars, matchmakers, and performers of Soma sacrifices [suffer].
358.019. Those Brahmins who have drunk the Soma juice, as well as forest-dwellers and ascetics—these all meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. 358.020. //249//
When the earth trembles under Ārdrā, milky trees perish;
food and drink vanish, and travelers are protected by fanged creatures. (250)
358.023. Well-diggers, ditch-diggers, and those who are evildoers and thieves—these shall meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. 251.
When the earth, the mandala, and the water-jar tremble under the asterism Punarvasu,
there will be hunters, water-fowls, wheel-bearers, parrots, and mainas.
358.027. Children, jugglers, butchers, and conch-shell merchants—358.028.
these suffer misfortune when shaken by an earthquake. //253//
When Puṣya is in conjunction, the earth shall tremble, as well as the leading Brāhmaṇas and those men who are long-distance travelers, merchants, and caravan leaders.

359.001. Kings, those from the mountains, and whoever falls within the scope of their devotion— 359.002. these shall encounter calamity when shaken by an earthquake. 359.003. They will rain down showers of stones; there will be a great ruin of the crops. //255//
When Āśleṣā moves, all the earth-dwellers, serpents, and reptiles, as well as insects, ants, dogs, and those wild animals with cloven hooves, shall tremble. (256)
359.006. Physicians, those who deal in poisons, and those beings who dwell in mountain caves—these shall meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //257//
359.008. When the earth trembles under the asterism Maghā, the great king suffers therein.
359.009. And those who are faithful cease; likewise, assemblies and festivals [are suspended]. 359.010.
Sacrifices and all rites for the gods are suspended here. (258)
Those who have been born, those who have grown up, and others who are preeminent scholars;
the *gandharvas* and men of noble lineage—all these meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. (259)
When the earth trembles under the constellation Phalgunī, the seasons then go astray;
a crosswind blows, and the eternal order perishes.
Travelers suffer distress, as do those who subsist by begging for beans.
Those who delight in the Dharma, those who subsist on alms, and those who live by tolls—
these all meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake.
359.019. When Uttaraphalgunī moves, merchants who travel to foreign islands, caravan leaders, courtiers, and those who live by their crafts [shall prosper]. 359.020. //262//
359.021. The Aṅgas, Videhas, Magadhas, and Nairṛtas, along with those who have taken wives, 359.022. these shall meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //263//

359.023. The earth trembled with their hands; the potters and physicians, the leaders of the guilds, the high officials, and those men who were army commanders—[all these shook the earth]. 359.024. //264//
The Tāramakas, the Nārapaṭas,
the Vipsaras,
and even the Kauṭikas.
359.026. These people fall into calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //265//
When the moon is in Citrā, the earth trembles; artisans and craftsmen, maidens, all kinds of gems, and the seeds of grain shall perish. (266)
359.029. The Vaṅgas, Daśārṇas, Kurus, Cedis, and Māhiṣakas—these shall encounter calamity when shaken by an earthquake. 359.030. //267//
360.001. Under Svāti, the earth is shaken; likewise those who are thieves, those of evil conduct, 360.002.
those who are harmful, those devoted to such deeds, and those who are importunate like rats. //268//
360.003. To the north of the Himavat, there are ascetics who subsist on air; 360.004. these suffer calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //269//
When the earth trembles under Viśākhā, there shall be the destruction of great mountains;
fierce winds blow there, and the people of Aśmaka become ill-fated.
360.007. Under Anurādhā, the earth shall tremble, and there will be great misfortune for bandits.
360.008. Likewise, there will be trouble for rogues, gamblers, and those men who are pickpockets.
The Andhras, Puṇḍras, and Pulindas will remain without refuge in a state of fear;
at that time, powerful dissension among friends arises in the world.
360.011. O Great King, when the constellation Jyeṣṭhā is active, the earth trembles and is scorched by heat.
360.012. Crows, bulls, predatory beasts, and likewise those that are fierce wild animals [become agitated]. (273)
The Kurus, the Śūrasenas, the Mallas, the Bāhlīkas, and the Nigrahas,
as well as those who are swift adversaries or devoted followers of them—
all these shall meet with calamity when shaken by an earthquake. (274)
When the earth trembles due to the root [nakṣatra], those with four legs as well as those with two,
the planets, the piśācas who dwell there, and whatever beings reside in mountain caves—
all these suffer calamity when shaken by the earthquake. (275)
360.019. It quickly causes famine, and grain shall become scarce due to lack of water. 360.020. At that time, people on earth will go to mountain caves and the bases of mountains. //276//
If the earth trembles during Pūrvāṣāḍhā, aquatic creatures such as fish, oysters, porpoises, otters, crocodiles, sea-monsters, and tortoises will perish. (277)
Those who prioritize their caste and lineage, as well as the wealthy and the wise;
those of noble second birth and those who possess great learning—these all fall into calamity when shaken by an earthquake. (278)
If the earth trembles in the north, there will be great misfortune for artisans;
blacksmiths, architects, workers in tin, and carpenters [will suffer]. (279)
360.028. Both the poor and the wealthy, as well as artisans of various kinds—360.029.
these all encounter calamity when shaken by an earthquake.
360.030. It destroys village headmen, as well as all things moving and stationary. //280//
361.001. When the earth trembled for Vaiṣṇava, then that which was undesirable occurred.
361.002–361.003. Teachers, scholars of the scriptures, poets, and masters of mantras; the Yugaṃdharas, the Śūrasenas, the Abhirājas, and the Paṭaccaras—[all these were affected]. //281//
361.004. Those men honored by kings—the Kuśaṇḍas and the Śaradaṇḍas—361.005. these shall encounter calamity when shaken by an earthquake. //282//
If the earth trembles under Dhaniṣṭhā, there will be a great misfortune for the wealthy;
likewise for the Maheśvaras, the great Nāgaras, and the merchant guild leaders.
The Pracaṇḍas, the Svastimantas, the Bhadrakāras, the Yugandharas,
the Pārikūlas, the Bhojas, and other Sannāgaras—
these all fall into calamity when shaken by an earthquake.
When the earth trembles in the quarter of Varuṇa, there is great fire in the waters;
elephants, horses, donkeys, and camels suffer terrible pain from its touch.
At that time, he will afflict the Vīrakas, Madras, Bāhlīkas, and Kekayas, as well as the helpless Cakravākas and the Janasthas. (286)
When the earth trembles with the sound of *sāja*, it shall strike down the Rākṣasa killers, as well as sheep-butchers, pork-butchers, and those from Sauvīra. (287)
He shall destroy the Vaiśyas who live by trade, the Śūdras, the Karītins, the Yavanas, the Mālavas and others, as well as the pickpockets.
When Ahibudhnya is affected, the earth trembles and there is great misfortune for merchants.
Those who are established in dharma, those who have attained perfection, and those engaged in the work of pearl-fishers [suffer]. (289)

361.021. He will soon afflict the Śibis, the Vatsas, the Vātsyas, and the Kṣatriyas of the Ārjunāyana clan; 361.022. he will torment all those who hold bows in their hands, including the kings of Sindhu.
When the earth trembles under Revatī, there shall be a most terrible battle;
village raids occur, and indeed, village strikes out against village.
One should utterly destroy the seafarers who live by the water, the Ramaṭhas, the Bharukacchas, the Sudhanvanas,
the Abhisāras, and the Sarvasenas.
When the earth trembles under Aśvinī, there will be great misfortune for horses;
village raids will occur, and brother will seek to kill brother.
361.029. Whoever here conceives a fetus and whoever are born here—361.030.
from this point on, they shall experience suffering continuously for three years. (294)
Those who are united with Citragarbha, as well as other womenfolk and the Ārjunāyana kṣatriyas— he indeed violently harms these three.
When the earth trembles under the asterism Bharaṇī, there will be great misfortune for thieves;
likewise, libertines, gamblers, and those men who are cutpurses shall suffer.
362.005. Mirror-makers, wheelwrights, rogues, as well as prison guards, 362.006.
those who live at the ends of villages, the sinful, and those who are wicked— 362.007.
they too perish there, shaken by the earthquake. //297//
When the earth trembles, a form will immediately appear;
within seven days, a desired rain-cloud will arise there.
For it is glossy, resembling collyrium, and like unto a great mountain.
And Indra pours rain there, just as the Great Seer has spoken;
thus it was declared by the Protectors, and Indra rains here accordingly.
Resembling the shape of a svastika and like Indra’s thunderbolt or banner,
clouds are seen at twilight after having eclipsed the moon and the sun.
Then clouds resembling pomegranates arise in the sky.
Having observed such a sign, one should know them to be shaken by Indra. That is the instruction there, according to the word of the Great Seer.
362.018. One should sow all kinds of seeds there with complete confidence. 362.019. And merchants may carry out their business dealings there without fear.
362.020. Among all types of earthquakes, those caused by Indra are auspicious. (302)
When the earth trembles, an immediate sign will follow:
within seven days, clouds shall cover the sky there.
Then clouds resembling silk are born in succession;
moving toward the western direction, they drift along in a favorable wind.
362.025. Clouds resembling crocodiles, water-fowls, fish, and sea-monsters are seen at twilight, having swallowed the moon and the sun. 305.
362.027. Having observed such a sign, one should know them to be shaken by water.
362.028. That is the instruction there, according to the word of the Great Seer. //306//
362.029. On dry lands, on mountain peaks, in fields, and in groves—there the seeds are sown; indeed, they perish when [the ground] is low-lying. 362.030. //307//
363.001. These [earthquakes] may perish due to mud, water, or even dust.
363.002. Among these earthquakes, those shaken by water are auspicious. //308//
363.003. When the earth trembles, an omen will immediately follow.
363.004. Within seven days, most terrible winds will blow there. //309//
363.005. A tawny twilight is seen, and the moon and sun are red.
363.006. Having observed such a sign, one should know that [the world] is shaken by the wind. //310//
363.007. Then follows the instruction according to the words of the Great Seer:
363.008. A wise person should not dwell there; rather, one should protect oneself in this regard. //311//
One should keep the secret hidden and dig a rampart and a moat; otherwise, those living on the borders will revolt and fear will arise among men. //312//
The virtues of all these earthquakes have been proclaimed; specifically, those caused by the agitation of wind are ordained for human beings. (313)
When the earth has shaken, an immediate sign will follow:
within seven days, there shall be most terrible falls of meteors.
The twilight glows red, and both the moon and the sun are crimson;
having seen such a sign, one should know that [the earth] is shaken by fire.
Fire burns both wood and guarded wealth;
columns of smoke are seen, and weapons become excessively heated.
Lutes are seen in the sky when it does not rain for nine months;
among these earthquakes, those shaken by fire are the least significant.
363.021. It triumphs over the Kṣatriyas and kings, along with the foremost of horses, elephants, and chariots, during the forenoon; it overcomes the ministers at midday. 363.023.
It causes distress to the cowherds, cattle, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras in the afternoon, and it utterly consumes thieves and those who dwell in endless [darkness] at the twilight of night. //318//
363.025. Indeed, at the onset of night here, he harms the hosts of Mlecchas; and at midnight, he harms endless women and eunuchs. 363.027.
In the third watch, he kills those who subsist on agriculture and trade; in the dark [fortnight], he who performs terrible deeds afflicts the faction of the gods.
In the bright fortnight of the moon, he burns away [impurities]; he cooks the sacrificial offerings for the Brahmins and Kṣatriyas—those of pure conduct who are foremost in dharma.
And toward the learned, he finds a gentle disposition; for he who studies becomes a Brāhmaṇa who perceives the Vedas and is honored by kings.
364.001. Four [deeds] are equal to those of Bṛhaspati through auspicious action;
364.002. four [deeds] involving the sun are equal to the deeds of Śukra; 364.003. four [deeds] involving Soma, and the deed of Brahmā, are likewise equal to them. //321//
364.004. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter entitled "The Exposition on the Trembling of the Earth."
364.005. Now, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter on the names and the arising of diseases for the twenty-eight lunar mansions (nakṣatras).
364.006. Let that be heard.
364.006. May the Blessed One speak.
364.007. A disease arising under the constellation Kṛttikā, whether in a woman or a man, shall last for four nights; thereafter, one is liberated from it. 322.
364.009. For Agni is the deity there; one should offer him an oblation of curd. 364.010. By this rite of offering, he is liberated from that disease. //323//
364.011. A disease arising under Rohiṇī will afflict either a woman or a man.
364.012. The illness shall last for five nights, after which one is liberated from it. //324//
364.013. There, one should offer an oblation with pure garlands to the god Prajāpati. 364.014. By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //325//
364.015. A disease has arisen like the constellation Mṛgaśiras for either a woman or a man.
364.016. The illness shall last for eight nights, and thereafter one is liberated from it. //326//
For Soma is the deity there; one should offer a bali-oblation with a cake (maṇḍa).
By this offering of a bali, one is liberated from that disease. //327//
364.019. A disease arising under the constellation Ārdrā affects either a woman or a man.
364.020. The illness shall last for ten nights, and after that, one is released from it. (328)
For Rudra is the deity there; one should offer an oblation of milk-rice (pāyasa). By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
If a disease should befall either a woman or a man under the asterism Punarvasu, that illness will last for eight nights; thereafter, one is liberated from it.
The deity there is Āditya; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
If a disease arises in a woman or a man during the Puṣya asterism, it will be of short duration; he shall be liberated from it after five nights.
The deity Bṛhaspati should offer an oblation there with perfumes and garlands.
By means of this ritual offering, one is liberated from that disease.
365.001. Under Āśleṣā, there will be illness for either a woman or a man.
365.002. Physicians shall not be able to treat it, for the serpent is the presiding deity there. //334//
A disease arising under the Maghā constellation, whether in a woman or a man, shall last for eight nights; thereafter, one is released from it.
The ancestors are the deities there; one should offer a bali-oblation with *kṛsara*.
By this rite of bali, one is liberated from that disease.
A disease occurring to a woman or a man born under Pūrvaphalgunī will last for seven nights; thereafter, one is liberated from it.
365.009. Āryamā is the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
365.010. By this rite of offering, one shall be liberated from that disease. //338//
365.011. In Uttarā, there shall be illness for either a woman or a man.
365.012. Physicians shall not be able to treat it; rather, the deity Bhaga is the one responsible here. //339//
Whether it be a woman or a man, a disease that has arisen may last for five nights; after that, one is liberated from it.
The Sun is indeed the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and flowers.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
A disease arising under the constellation Citrā affects either a woman or a man;
the illness shall last for eight nights, after which one is liberated from it.
For Tvaṣṭṛ is the deity there; one should offer an oblation of ghee with *udga* verses.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //343//
A disease arising under the asterism Svāti affects either a woman or a man;
indeed, that affliction lasts for twenty-five nights.
The deity there is Vāyu; one should offer an oblation with variegated garlands.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //345//
If there be illness for a woman or a man under the asterism Viśākhā,
that illness shall be severe and will last for nineteen days.
Indra and Agni are the deities there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
By this rite of offering, one shall be liberated from that disease.
A disease arising under Anurādhā affects either a woman or a man;
the illness shall last for half a month, and thereafter one is liberated from it.
366.001. For Mitra is the deity there; one should offer a vessel of clarified butter as a bali-oblation. 366.002. By this rite of bali, one is liberated from that disease. //349//
If a disease arises in the Jyeṣṭhā nakṣatra for either a woman or a man, that afflictive illness will indeed persist for thirteen days and nights. (350)
For Indra is the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
By means of this ritual offering, one is liberated from that disease. (351)
A disease that has arisen from the very root, whether in a woman or a man, shall indeed last for one month; after that, he is liberated from it.
366.009. One should offer an oblation there to the deity Nairṛti with liquor and meat. 366.010. By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //353//
366.011. Under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, there will be illness for either a woman or a man. 366.012. This illness will be distressing for eight months; of this there is no doubt. (354)
366.013. Water is the deity there; one should offer an oblation of *kṛsara* (rice and peas). 366.014. By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //355//
If there is illness for a woman or a man under Uttarā, that illness shall last for seven nights; after that, one is released from it.
For Viśva is the deity there; one should offer an oblation of milk-rice (pāyasa).
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
If a disease arises under the asterism Abhijit for either a woman or a man, that illness may persist for six months; after that time, one is liberated from it.
And Viṣṇu is the deity there; one should offer curd-whey as the sacrificial oblation.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
A disease arising from hearing [an ominous sound] will afflict either a woman or a man;
indeed, that disease shall be severe for a full twelve months.
For Viṣṇu is the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
If there is illness for a woman or a man under the asterism Dhaniṣṭhā, it shall last for thirteen days; thereafter, one is liberated from it.
366.029. Varuṇa is the deity there; one should offer an oblation of milk-rice (pāyasa).
366.030. By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease.
367.001. A disease arising from Pūrvabhādrapadā affects either a woman or a man.
367.002. Physicians shall not treat it; Ahirbudhnya is the presiding deity in this case.
367.003. For one born under Uttarābhādrapadā, illness shall afflict either a woman or a man.
367.004. The illness shall last for seven nights, after which one is released from it.
367.005. Āryamā is the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands.
367.006. By this rite of oblation, one is liberated from that disease.
367.007. A disease arises in a woman or a man during the asterism of Revatī. 367.008.
Indeed, that disease will be mild and will last for twenty-eight nights. 367.009. Thus it is said.
367.009. For Pūṣan is the deity there; one should offer an oblation with perfumes and garlands. 367.010.
By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. 368.
367.011. A disease arising under the asterism Aśvinī, whether in a woman or a man, will be a distressing illness lasting twenty-five nights. 367.012. [End of verse 369]
367.013. A Gandharva deity resides there; one should offer an oblation of barley gruel (yāvaka) to it.
367.014. By this rite of offering, one is liberated from that disease. //370//
367.015. A disease arising under the asterism Bharaṇī affects either a woman or a man.
367.016. Physicians cannot cure it; Yama, however, is the presiding deity there. 367.017.
Let the wise person guard their moral conduct; through that, they will go to heaven. (370)
367.018. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter titled "The Origin of Disease."
367.019. "O Puṣkarasārin, I shall indeed explain this chapter called 'Liberation from Bondage.
Let it be heard! 367.020.
May the Blessed One speak."

367.021. "O Puṣkarasārin, if someone is bound or obstructed under the asterism Kṛttikā, it should be said: 'He will be released after three nights. 367.021. If bound or obstructed under Rohiṇī, he will be released after three nights.
367.022. If bound or obstructed under Mṛgaśiras, he will be released after twenty-one nights."
If one is bound or obstructed under Ārdrā, they will be released within half a month;
if under Punarvasu, within seven nights;
and if under Puṣya, within three nights.
Under Āśleṣā, it is accomplished in thirty nights;
under Maghā, in sixteen nights;
under Pūrvaphalgunī, in ten nights.
Under Viśākhā, it is accomplished in twenty-six nights;
under Anurādhā, in thirty-one nights;
under Jyeṣṭhā, in eighteen nights.
Under Abhijit, it is accomplished in six nights;
under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, in fourteen nights;
and under Uttarāṣāḍhā, in fourteen nights.
Under Abhijit, it is accomplished in six nights;
under Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣaj, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, and Revatī, in fourteen nights;
and under Aśvinī, in three nights.
If [the moon] is in Bharaṇī, it should be said that he will be bound, imprisoned, or will undergo great suffering.
367.031. O Puṣkarasārin, this is the chapter titled "Liberation from Bondage."
367.032. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter on the *tilaka*;
let it be heard.
May the Blessed One speak.
368.001. But she who has a subtle, glossy tilaka on her forehead, with a color like that of a lotus—368.003.
A king shall be her husband in this world; they say there is a reflection upon her breasts.
If there should be a small mole on her head, the color of powdered collyrium, her husband will indeed be a commander-in-chief; moreover, there would be a reflection [of him] between her breasts.
If there is a mole between her eyebrows, they say that woman is a woman of ill-conduct;
she shall have exactly five husbands, yet as a woman she will obtain abundant food and drink.

If a woman has a mole (*tilaka*) or a reflection (*bimba*) on the middle part of her face, such as the nose or other areas, they say that woman will experience sorrow; they call a reflection [on the skin] a mark of hair-pores (*romapradeśa*).
368.017. They say that a woman who has a mole on her ear is one of great learning.
368.019. She is one of great learning and possesses a retentive memory if she has a reflection [of the moon] upon her nape. //376//
368.021. They say that a woman who has a mole on her upper lip is one whose truth is broken.
368.023. She indeed obtains her livelihood only with great difficulty; they say there is a "sesame-mole" upon her thighs.
368.025. If there be a mole or dark spot on her lower lip, they say that woman is a woman of ill conduct.
368.027. She obtains much sweet food and drink, for likewise there shall be a reflection [of the moon] in her private parts.
If there be a mole or dark spot on her chin, they say that woman is a woman of ill conduct;
she shall obtain much sweet food and drink, and there shall be a second reflection [mark] upon her private parts.
368.033. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter named "The Chapter on the Tilaka."
369.001. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter entitled "The Qualities of Birth under the Constellations.
369.001. Let that be heard.
369.002. May your honor Triśaṅku speak.
369.003. A man born under Kṛttikā is radiant and fond of daring deeds;
369.004. such a person is brave, fierce, and speaks kindly.
A man born under Rohiṇī will be wealthy and likewise righteous;
he will be industrious, steadfast, and brave, and he will certainly always possess happiness.
A person born under Mṛgaśiras is gentle and mild;
he will be handsome and especially beloved by women.
One born under Ārdrā will indeed be violent by nature, fierce, and excessively talkative;
he will perform cruel deeds and become a great lord over hundreds.
Furthermore, that man who is born under Punarvasu is not fickle; he is intelligent, possesses a virtuous character, yet is prone to anger.
369.013. A person born under Puṣya shall be a radiant Brāhmaṇa;
369.014. he may also become a Kṣatriya king, or a Vaiśya or Śūdra who is honored.
A man born under Āśleṣā is indeed a snorer, wrathful, cruel, ill-disposed, and fierce; one should predict all these traits for him here.
Under the Maghā asterism, a man shall be highly wise, devout, and likewise very fortunate; he will possess wealth, grain, and enjoyments.
Any man who is born under Pūrvaphālgunī will possess a mind and character inclined toward unrighteousness and will violate the wives of his elders.
One born under Uttaraphalgunī becomes possessed of enjoyments;
such a person shall be endowed with divine knowledge, possessed of discernment, and fortunate.
Born with the Hasta nakṣatra, he is pure in soul, valiant, and eats soft food;
he holds the office of commander-in-chief and shall be free from the act of theft.
One born under Citrā will have variegated eyes, be a narrator of wonderful tales,
handsome, possess many wives, and be of diverse character.
A man born under Svāti is praised by his kinsmen,
discerning, gentle, fond of drink, helpful to friends, and wise.
A man born under Viśākhā will be radiant, wealthy, and great;
he shall be heroic, valiant, skillful, and fortunate.
A mortal born under Anurādhā will be a man who possesses friends and is a gatherer of people;
he shall also be pure, grateful, and righteous in soul.
A person born under Jyeṣṭhā is born with many friends;
he takes delight in the science of archery and sets his heart upon women.
370.003. A man born under the Mūla asterism would be ungrateful and unrighteous; 370.004. that person would be firm and heroic, yet he would also be sinful.
If [the moon] is in the Pūrvāṣāḍhās, that man will be envious, of unsteady senses, fond of fish and meat, and a killer.
A man born under Viśvadeva will certainly be compassionate, generous, devoted to knowledge, and a friend to all people.
A man born under Śravaṇā shall become a teacher, an author of treatises, trustworthy, and devoted to ritual action; he shall be long-lived and prosperous. (399)
A man born under Dhaniṣṭhā will have an unstable mind, be fond of various material objects, and be suspicious of everyone. (400)
If a man is born under the lunar mansion of Vāruṇa,
he will be a person of hateful character and a detractor in every respect.
A person born here under the constellation Bhādrapadā of the former [fortnight] is endowed with virtuous conduct and qualities, is grateful, and likewise talkative.
A man born in the north will be discerning,
intelligent, possessed of many offspring, virtuous in character, and very wealthy.
A man born under Revatī is righteous by nature and devoted to his kinsmen;
though poor and possessing little wealth, he is constantly generous and free from envy.
A man born under Aśvinī becomes exceedingly discerning;
he is beloved by the masses, heroic, and fortunate.
A person born under Bharaṇī is of evil conduct and lacking in discernment; he is desirous of giving away his wealth in amorous pursuits and lives off others.
370.025. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter entitled "The Qualities of Birth under the Constellations."
371.001. "Recite, O Triśaṅku, the chapter named 'The Wheel of Portents' (Utpātacakra).
And he says:
"The Exposition of the Wheel of Portents."
371.002. Within the circle of constellations, extending to its limit of twenty-eight [lunar mansions], 371.003.
divine portents are seen among the sun, moon, planets, and other celestial bodies. //407//
If, during the first fortnight of the month of Māgha, a mountain or an earthly mass appears as smoke-rain while the sun is rising,
or if lightning is seen, then one should know that there will be a destruction of people.
371.007. If smoke issues forth from the sun in the constellation Aśvinī, it shall shroud the sky.
371.008. Then one should know that there will be no rain for twelve full years. //409//
371.009. If the sun is seen yellow in the month of Māgha while in the asterism Bharaṇī, 371.010.
the kingdom will be besieged on all sides; one should predict famine in its midst. //410//
If, during the month of Phālguna, on the day of the sun under the asterism Kṛttikā,
a moat [is dug] and the deity does not send rain, the market towns there will perish.
When the sun is seen darkened during the month of Caitra under the asterism Puṣya,
at the time of its recent rising, the protector of the earth shall be besieged.
In the month of Vaiśākha, when the sun is in conjunction with the Ardrā nakṣatra, a mock-sun (pratisūryaka) appears;
one should know that a battle will occur there, and both kings will be slain.
If the moon or the sun should be eclipsed during the month of Jyeṣṭha while the moon is in the constellations of Bharaṇī or Jyeṣṭhā,
the king, along with his ministers, shall be slain, and one should predict famine in the kingdom.
371.019. And when the sun is in Āṣāḍha and situated in Pūrvabhādrapada, a wound appears excessively red upon its orb in the evening. 371.020. //415//
Then that kingdom will be oppressed by a hostile army for six months;
and the king, along with his ministers, sons, and wives, shall be slain.
When the moon is seized during the month of Āṣāḍha under the constellation Pūrvāṣāḍhā or Uttarāṣāḍhā,
one should know that famine, strife, and disease are to be predicted therein.
Then, in the month of Śrāvaṇa, during the Mūla constellation, the moon and the sun do not shine;
sparks are seen there, and one should know that there is great fear of disease.
In the month of Āśvayuja, when the moon and the sun are eclipsed during one and the same fortnight,
there shall then occur the destruction of thousands of princes.
On the full moon day of Kārttika, the moon is without its characteristic marks and lacks luster;
both the sun and the moon appear the color of fire against a blood-red sky.
372.001. That kingdom shines like the sun, yet it shall perish again and again.
372.002. One should know that when kings are slain, the earth will indeed drink their blood. //421//
If in the month of Māgha, during the Bharaṇī asterism, a black wind arises and quickly obscures both the moon and the sun, the kingdom will perish.
In the month of Phālguna, however, if there is a wind accompanied by lightning and a rain of dust,
former kings are slain and others are established in their place.
If any planet should move together with the sun or the moon,
or if an irregular wind blows, one should then know that there will be the death of a king.
If thunderbolts and meteors arise together with the sun during the month of Vaiśākha,
one should predict calamity for the kingdom within six months.
372.011. When the sun emerges from an eclipse in the month of Jyeṣṭha, 372.012. then all the planets are afflicted by that impairment of the sun.
In the month of Jyeṣṭha, there shall be a rain of dust and the sun will be eclipsed;
one by one, thousands of kings shall be slain.
372.015. In the month of Āṣāḍha, winds blow while the moon is situated in Bharaṇī.
372.016. Wells dry up, yet all the crops flourish. //428//
372.017. If yellow winds blow in the month of Śrāvaṇa and the sky remains perpetually black, 372.018.
one should recognize that danger has arisen from all sides. //429//
If fire rains during the month of Śrāvaṇa or during the day in Pūrvabhādrapada, the clouds produce a loud sound; one should predict disease and famine.
372.021. When the sky is covered with clouds and thundering during the month of Bhādrapada, 372.022.
then a foreign army will seize the accumulation of wealth within the kingdom. //431//
In the month of Aśvayuja, a wind and rain will come from the northern direction;
it shall bring about slaughter, and thus the entire kingdom will perish.
372.025. When the moon is in Sagittarius on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, 372.026.
the kingdom perishes on all sides; one should predict famine in the center. //433//
If meteors fall or thunderbolts strike during the month of Māgha in the region of Aśvinī, the people there will perish from asthma.
If, during the month of Phālguna, there should be a rain of fire from the vault of the sky, and a sound should arise in that space, that kingdom will quickly perish. (435)
372.031. When rain is obstructed during the month of Caitra under the asterism Svāti, and there is a shower of wind, 372.032. if a rainbow is seen, that city will soon perish. //436//
In the month of Jyeṣṭha, if a sound should arise from the north during the asterism Bharaṇī,
the sky will appear yellow in color, and there will be fear of an enemy army.
Then, in the auspicious month of Āṣāḍha, when lightning is seen in the sky,
the people are released from three parts of their suffering through rains accompanied by grass and water.
When the god rains heavily during the month of Śrāvaṇa under the asterism Mūla,
and a rainbow is seen there, it portends great fear for the Kṣatriyas.
In the month of Bhādrapada, when a thunderous crash falls upon the earth,
harsh winds blow and there is then great fear of disease.
In the month of Bhādrapada, when the asterism Puṣya is present, if a sound issues forth from the intermediate directions,
the Kṣatriyas will soon become enraged, and at that time the subjects will be divided against their enemies.
If a sound should arise above during the asterisms of Bharaṇī or Aśvinī,
and if one should cast dust along with grass [into the fire], there will be great danger for ascetics.
If a terrifying sound is heard during the month of Kārttika under the constellation Ārdrā,
one should predict death for quadrupeds and farmers there.
373.015. If the sound of musical instruments should arise in the sky during the month of Mārgaśīrṣa under the asterism Dhaniṣṭhā, 373.016.
then there will be a terrible disease caused by wind in the kingdom. //444//
When a terrifying sound occurs during the month of Pauṣa under the asterism Svāti,
and lightning flashes repeatedly in the sky, there is great fear for the learned.
If a thunderous crash (nirghāta) occurs during the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, it shall constantly afflict the earth;
one should know that in the third year, there will be total upheaval throughout the kingdom.

In the month of Phālguna, during the Jyeṣṭhā nakṣatra, when the sky is filled with dark winds and the earth trembles repeatedly, there will then be fear for those practicing the celibate life (brahmacārin).
If the earth trembles during the day in the month of Caitra under the asterism Pūrvabhādrapadā,
then in that year and in that kingdom there will be great fear from enemy armies.
If, during the night of the *pūrvāṣāḍhā* constellation in the month of Caitra, the sky remains motionless,
the king will be struck by swords and the great multitude of people will be slain.
In the month of Vaiśākha, if the earth trembles frequently during the dark fortnight,
one should predict famine due to drought for six months.
If, in the month of Jyeṣṭha, during the asterism of Bharaṇī, the earth should tremble by day,
one should know that the earth will drink the blood of thousands of warriors.
373.031. When the earth trembles at night during the Mūla constellation in the month of Jyeṣṭha, 373.032.
the frontier king is slain; one should impose a tax upon the kingdom. //452//
374.001. When the moon is situated in the Puṣya constellation during the month of Āṣāḍha, the earth trembles. 374.002. There, the crops perish and the deeds of strife arise. //453//
When the caityas tremble during the asterisms of Ārdrā or Maghā,
or if they blaze or fall down, then the kingdom will soon perish.
Where the shrines tremble, laugh, and bow down,
there the king, together with his kingdom, shall soon meet with destruction.
When the moon is situated in Pūrvabhādrapadā during the month of Śrāvaṇa, the earth trembles;
the king is constantly defeated, and the kingdom is ravaged by thieves.
374.009. When, in the month of Kārttika, a shrine (caitya) collapses due to an earthquake, or if the gate of a city is destroyed, the people will for the most part perish. 374.010. //457//
If Bṛhaspati should stand upon either the left or the right horn of the Moon, those of great enjoyment, the illustrious lords of the earth, shall perish. (458)
When the planet Mars ascends the horns of the sun and moon,
one should predict affliction for the border regions due to the incantations of sorcerers.
When Saturn ascends the peak of the Moon,
then one should recognize a terrible fear of disease and predict famine in that region.
When the moon is seized by Rāhu and struck by a meteor,
one should predict misfortune for the king within six months.
Furthermore, when the moon and the sun are eclipsed by Rāhu in the same lunar mansion (nakṣatra), the king shall suffer affliction along with his kingdom.
When a comet enters the lunar mansion of the king or that of the moon,
one should predict a swoon of weapons together with neighboring kings.
When Venus enters the middle of the moon during the asterisms of Phālgunī or Maghā, all grains will wither; at that time, one should predict disease.
When Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Lohitāṅga,
and Śanaiścara eclipse the horn of the moon, one should know that there will be great danger.
When the illustrious Dhūmaketu stands mounted upon the Puṣya asterism,
one should then know that there will be the onset of foreign armies from all four directions.
If Mars should remain in Maghā, or Jupiter in Śravaṇā,
for three years, one should know that great danger has arrived.
If Venus should somehow remain in Rohiṇī during the month of Jyeṣṭha,
one may predict with certainty that there will be great danger for the Kṣatriyas.
375.001. When Jupiter and Saturn are situated near Viśākhā, or when the Moon is together with the Sun, there is then fear of an enemy army. //469//
Crows, hawks, and vultures will dwell together in joy;
they will abstain from sexual intercourse and engage in combat with others at that time.
A hawk may repeatedly alight upon the elephant’s dwelling,
and there shall also be repeated battles with a hostile army.
Where a girl gives birth who has four hands and four breasts,
there indeed occurs a most terrible death among women alone.
375.009. Where children staying in the womb laugh and speak, one should know that the destruction of that region is at hand. //473//
375.011. Where women give birth to those with one foot, three feet, or likewise four limbs, one should predict misfortune for the king. //474//
375.013. Where women give birth to deformed fetuses, lineages marked by fear, 375.014. in that region, the king shall perish. //475//
Where women give birth to those with small hands, heads, and faces who have taken on human bodies,
there the kingdom perishes.
375.017. Donkeys, buffaloes, and likewise other such animals, 375.018.
are born with two or three heads in that country where it perishes. //477//
In whatever country men are born with the forms of jackals, dogs, crocodiles, or horses, that country quickly perishes.
When a Vaiśya woman gives birth with both feet first,
one should predict the ruin of the country through a terrible invasion by a foreign army.
When the first half of the asterism is the *garbha* (womb) for birds and snakes,
a king or a royal minister perishes along with his entire country.
Where a kumbhāṇḍa with two faces or four faces is born, or even one with three eyes or three faces, one should know that there is great danger there. //481//
If one has a human body with a pig's snout,
he will undoubtedly destroy the kingdom and its inhabitants in the four directions.
But when a human is born with the form of the sun,
the entire kingdom, through delusion, goes to its destruction.
376.001. But in whatever land a child is seen lying on its back while reciting the Vedas, O best of the twice-born, that land will quickly perish. //484//
When the infant, having burst through the womb, emerges from the womb by himself,
making his helpless mother his refuge, that region quickly perishes.
376.005. Pigs, camels, snakes, and likewise birds born from the wombs of women—when these occur, one should predict danger for the country. //486//
If human, donkey, or pig figures appear in conflict over wealth, one should predict that danger has arrived when cows give birth [under such conditions].
If a woman conceives a fetus while her breasts have not yet appeared,
one should predict the destruction of that country along with its king.
Where a person with matted hair and long nails, who is very dark and harsh of skin,
is born, that kingdom along with its ruler shall be consumed by fire.
376.013. Where children are born with necks lacking vertebrae and yet possessing teeth, 376.014. all crops shall wither and the people shall go to their destruction. //490//
If a fetus with one arm and no head is born, that kingdom will itself become agitated and perish; of this there is no doubt.
When one sees fruit upon fruit, or flowers supported by flowers,
the fetuses of women will miscarry and the crown prince shall be put to death.
Where trees flower and bear fruit out of season,
or where creepers, shrubs, or climbing vines do so, there shall be danger in that region.
If one sees one's own blood flowing from above a tree,
or a bird crying out, then one should know that there will be great danger.
The shade of trees or pavilions does not shift;
there, fear among the four castes arises, as do the deeds of the Kali age.
Where trees of various species of flowers would bloom, yet are of the nature of *kalpavṛkṣa* trees, from that one should know there will be great danger. //496//
When flowers and fruits are seen on trees that do not normally produce them,
one should predict the destruction of that region, as well as famine and strife.
If trees are seen anywhere, having fallen from their proper places,
the king who was previously established will soon be displaced.
377.001. One shall behold a divine-asura battle of wondrous appearance.
377.002. There, weapons will become blunted, and likewise by thieves as before. //499//
377.003. Wherever the Teacher is seen walking, he trembles and weeps; 377.004. from that one should know there will be an invasion by a foreign army and a total defeat. //500//
377.005. In whatever place the deities dance and laugh, or shed tears, one should then know that there is great danger. //501//
Where deities sport, or flash, or blink their eyes,
or where they might move about, then another king shall arise.
377.009. When a Śiva-liṅga trembles, or is seen in the sky, or sinks into the earth, the death of the king will certainly occur. //503//
The images shift, emit smoke, and weep; they perspire and run about, for another king shall arise. (504)
The immovable may move from its place, or the movable may become immovable;
the minister slays the king, and one should predict strife in this case.
377.015. Maidens vomit blood, or they bow down toward the ten directions; 377.016. or [omens] occur when they are not joined [to their mates]; there will be great fear for the kṣatriyas. //506//
377.017. Wherever it rains flowers, or even drops of blood, or wherever various living beings appear, one should know that there is then danger from thieves. //507//
When the ancient sacrificial posts, sacred groves, temples, shrines,
and cities are enveloped in smoke, the king will soon perish.
377.021. Whether it be the moon, a lamp-tree, or a lamp that does not shine;
377.022. Or whether it be a prince desiring the kingdom, or even a mere branch, he shall be agitated. (509)
When honey-bees build a nest within the inner apartments,
or when weapons or the palace itself catch fire, one should predict calamity for the king.
Lightning fell within the inner apartments, or likewise upon a tree in the hermitage;
it fell upon the shade of a shrine in the city for the sake of the king.
If a crow builds a nest on a wall, in an armory, or at the gate-towers, the king, along with his ministers, shall perish.
Sound shall issue forth spontaneously from musical instruments even without being struck;
and by the fault of its own wheels' agitation, the entire kingdom will be plundered. (513)
When there falls a rain of flesh and blood, or of leaves, flowers, and fruits—
that rain signifies that the kingdom will be plundered by armies.
Honey, molasses, and flowers, or even rains of perfumes, as well as the burning of the quarters—these are seen as the signs of Māra’s famine. (515)
If a cloud should thunder on all sides and rain down along with *cātaka* birds,
and if there be blood mixed with hailstones, then one should know that there will be danger from an enemy.
378.007. Terrible lightning strikes and there is a rain of hailstones; 378.008. furthermore, upon seeing a city of the Gandharvas, one should know that great danger is imminent. //517//
The moon resembles blood, dark in its center and discolored; it is afflicted on all sides. One should know that there will be great fear in the kingdom. (518)
When the moon is seen resembling a blazing fire,
then the sky burns there and the world suffers from fever.
When that which resembles red ochre quickly subsides,
one should know that rain will arrive, even if the wind is blowing.
When the twilight is of a smoky color, and both the moon and the sun are visible,
severed by the form of Brahmā, one should predict rain there.
378.017. He does not sink in water, nor does he burn in fire; as before, he is not seen. 378.018. Fire will arise there, and it will consume the storehouse. //522//
Where a crow with drooping wings flutters at the top of a banner,
one should quickly withdraw from water, for there is great danger from fire.
If the water itself blazes intensely, the fish will consume it by its own nature;
at that time, one should predict drought, famine, and great terror.
If a wild forest deer should come to the city gate,
one should predict famine in both wheels [of the army] and disease within the kingdom.
When a snake with three heads or five heads is seen,
one should know that there will then be a drought and all the crops will perish.
378.027. Where a granary might be seen shaking the earth, 378.028.
storehouses shall perish, as well as other accumulations of wealth. //527//
But when a snake with its head raised fights with men, one should know that there is great danger from two wheels or from disease. (528)
379.001. When many snakes are coiled together in one place, 379.002.
then one should know that death by the sword awaits, and there is great danger for the Kṣatriyas. //529//
When swords emerge and blaze forth with focused attention,
then one will soon behold battle approaching.
If a crow, a hawk, or a vulture should alight upon one's head,
the king, along with his domestic priest, will die within six months.
The palaces, shelters, and houses tremble;
and the protector of the kingdom, possessed of great strength, shall be slain.
379.009. When all the directions are struck by thunderbolts during the dark fortnight across the four quarters, 379.010. blood shall rain down wherever the protector of the earth is slain. //533//
When a great meteor falls at the time of sunrise,
the earth shall drink the blood of thousands of princes.
If trees and serpents tremble, or if they shed their skins, one should know that there will be great fear of enemies throughout the entire kingdom. (535)
If, indeed, during the day a blazing meteor is seen falling,
one should know that there will be a bloody calamity and a battle of terrifying appearance.
379.017. One should see a blazing sword, as well as a lance and a discus; 379.018. one should know that those who see such weapons will witness a battle of terrifying appearance. //537//
If a horse sighs deeply, sheds tears,
and quickly drags [the rider] with its foot, the death of the king in battle is certain.
If a crow, having climbed onto a house, caws "Alas, my son!", then the entire region—including its cities, villages, and market towns—will utterly perish. (539)
When smoke arises where there is no fire, or when lotuses grow upon dry land,
one should predict with certainty that the destruction of that region will soon occur.
When clouds and wild beasts such as wolves howl terribly,
one should know that the destruction of that region is swiftly approaching.
Even rivers that have flowed for a long time will have their currents cut off; even houses will become dry, as if devoid of water; in such a state, there shall be danger. (542)
