When rivers flow against their currents, unobstructed,
one should predict that the regions will be constantly agitated and that there will be a destruction of the people.
380.001. Bows being drawn smoke and even burst into flames; 380.002. or other weapons likewise produce fear from enemies. (544)
380.003. A halo resembling the neck of a peacock appears around the moon.
380.004. One should know that thousands of rājavidyās will drink the blood of the earth. //545//
380.005. Neither for men nor for women does the joy of pleasure arise; 380.006. everywhere there is grief and anxiety, and great fear shall prevail therein. //546//
If the Nirgrantha sages, being present, should depart from a region—
whether by crossing a river or through its groves— that region will soon perish.
380.009. Where medicinal herbs have lost their potency and water dries up, one should know that region to be abandoned by deities, sages, and virtuous men. //548//
Where fish, tortoises, and snakes die, and where forest-dwellers perish,
there a woman's mass of wealth will be plundered by her co-wives.
Where birds never seen before appear, whether on dry land or in the water, a host of wealth shall be destroyed by a foreign army. (550)
When a great highway becomes a pathless track due to overgrown thickets,
the kingdom— including its villages and market towns— is destroyed along with its prince.
Chapter 380.017: The Exposition on the Wheel of Various Portents. 380.018: Recite, O Triśaṅku, the chapter on the *puruṣapiṇyā*.
380.018: "Very well."
"May the Blessed One speak—now, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter on the 'Pile of Men.
Listen to that.
"May the Blessed One speak."
380.020. Twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) are proclaimed, which follow along with the moon and the sun as they emerge.
380.021. In this regard, by means of a furrow twelve finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) long made with a well-plowed plow, one should know that one's own body is twelve such furrows in length.
380.022. A single cubit-measure from the tip of the foot to the top of the head shall be the measure;
fourteen cubit-measures is the extent of the constellations where they are seen, and it cannot be otherwise.
In whichever constellation one is born, there one is seen.
380.024. The "Man-Pinyā" [mark]: 380.025. For one born under Kṛttikā, there is indeed on the face, four finger-breadths from the right side, a hairy *pinyā* mark that is blackish-red. //552//
One born under Kṛttikā possesses wealth, is endowed with fame, and blazes with splendor in his physical form; indeed, such are the characteristics of one born under this asterism.
380.029. This very scar, measuring four finger-breadths, is clearly visible;
380.030. he who was born under Rohiṇī is likewise wise and always devoted to the Dharma. (554)
Adorned and endowed with wealth, possessed of a sense of shame in every respect,
he is heroic, successful in victory, and a constant crusher of his enemies.
381.001. He on whose neck a burn mark the size of half a *gṛṣṭi* is seen was born under Mṛgaśīrṣa; he is indeed brave and endowed with enjoyments. //556//
If one has a mole on the left side at the height of one and a half fingers, he is born under Ārdrā; such a person is wrathful, foolish, and a cattle-herder.
If one has a black wound on the left armpit under the asterism Punarvasu,
he will indeed be born with little intelligence, yet he will be prosperous with wealth and grain.
Likewise, one born under the Puṣya constellation is seen to possess excellent marks;
both the sun and the moon shine resplendent upon his palm and the center of his hand.
All his hair curls to the right in a half-turn;
the Leader’s body is perfectly rounded, and he has conquered all afflictions.
381.011. He in whose heart there is a burning sensation when [the moon is] in Āśleṣā is fond of quarreling;
381.012. he is ill-behaved, difficult to live with, and devoted to sexual intercourse. //561//
If a wound is seen on the chest or the back of one born under Maghā, that person will be wealthy, high-minded, and steadfast.
If a wound is seen on either the right or the left side of the navel,
one born under Pūrvaphalgunī is envious and short-lived.
381.017. He on whose navel a whorl is visible at a distance of four finger-breadths, 381.018.
born under Uttaraphalgunī, is devoted to enjoyment and diligent in sacred learning. //564//
381.019. A dark-red mole is seen on the hips of one born with [a mark] on the hand;
381.020. he is a thief, deceitful, a master of illusion, of little merit, and of dull intellect. //565//
If a mark is clearly seen fixed upon his private parts, he will certainly be born of a painted image; such a sick man is likewise devoted to dance and song.
Furthermore, if a yellowish or dark-brown complexion is observed even on the upper part of the body, one born under Svāti will be greedy, hostile toward virtue, and indeed unwise. (567)
381.025. One whose thighs are marked with red swellings from a bad bite, 381.026.
and who is surrounded by men and women, is a leading warrior under the asterism Viśākhā.
The wise one, a hero who has conquered his enemies and is ever devoted to happiness,
endowed with glory and fortitude, becomes an *acyuta* and is reborn in his own true nature.
If a second calf is seen on the thighs of a woman born under Anurādhā,
she will be virtuous and endowed with both righteousness and wealth.
382.001. He whose mole here on earth is below his thighs is born as the eldest;
382.002. he is short-lived, unpleasant, miserable, ill-behaved, and likewise wretched. //571//
382.003. He on whose [hand] a subtle scar is seen here above the knees, 382.004.
is born fortunate by virtue of his root [nakṣatra], yet he will quickly destroy his own home. //572//
For one born under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, there shall be a mole on the kneecap;
such a person is a giver, devoted to the Dharma, free from attachment, and destined for heaven.
If a tilaka mark is seen on the forehead of one born under Uttarāṣāḍhā, he will be intelligent, possessed of enjoyments, and beloved by the people. (574)
The second lunar mansion (Pinya) indicates that one will always be wealthy and possessed of enjoyments;
likewise, being fond of truth, free from disease, and steadfast, such a person goes to heaven. //575//
If a mole is seen on the shank under the asterism Dhaniṣṭhā, he will be irascible, of dull passion, wise, and devoid of enjoyments. //576//
382.013. And on the shank, two finger-breadths from the knee, a black mole is seen.
382.014. One born under Śatabhiṣā is a fool; indeed, he dies by water. //577//
If the mark is on the lower leg during Pūrvabhādrapadā, there will be a wound;
moreover, such a person is a tormentor of others, foolish, poor, and even a thief.
382.017. One whose natal star is Pinyā under Kugṛṣṭi in the latter half of Bhādrapadā will be generous in nature, possessed of mindfulness, compassionate, and confident. (579)
382.019. He on whose both feet a fine mole is seen, 382.020.
is born under Revatī as a lowly person; he even becomes a barber. //580//
He in whose thumb-cavity a blue mark is visible is born under Aśvinī; he is always healthy and strong. //581//
382.023. Furthermore, one born under Pinyā in the hand-palm (pāṇitala) division of Bharaṇī is known as inexhaustible (akṣaya).
382.024. One born under Vadhyaghāta will be of evil character and destined for hell. //582//
382.025. For this is the station of the constellations, by which movement is produced;
382.026. for this is the knowledge of the world, upon which the world is supported. //583//
382.027. Thus ends the chapter on the Pinya.
382.028. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter named Piṭakādhyāya. 382.028. Let it be heard!
382.029. May the Blessed One Triśaṅku speak.
382.030. The Chapter on the Piṭaka. 382.031.
Hereafter, I shall further proclaim the Piṭaka pertaining to all locations, 382.032.
which effects all rites for both women and men. (584)
383.001. Gain and loss, pleasure and pain, as well as life and death—learn now all that by which the wise fully understand. 383.002. //585//

In that regard, sesame seeds that have been crushed or burnt, even if they retain their original form, as well as those with the appearance of eruptions or various discolorations, are recorded in the tradition as being afflicted by pustules.
A white-colored pustule is honored among Brahmins;
one resembling a wound is for Kṣatriyas, while a yellow one is recorded for Vaiśyas.
383.007. Among the Śūdras, Asita is the best; among the Mleccha tribes, he is pale-complexioned.
383.008. When there is a mole on the crown of his head, he is known as a great king.
On the head, there is gain of wealth and grain, as well as beauty and good fortune;
one should know that on the eyebrows there is injury, while at the meeting of the eyebrows, there is the acquisition of a woman.
A boil located in the region of the eyes makes one pleasant to behold;
one on the area of the eyes or eyebrows leads to grief, while one on the cheek certainly portends the death of a son.
383.013. The falling of tears certainly brings grief; hearing [the sound] regarding cows brings destruction.
383.014. On the ear-ornament it is for adornment, but on the bridge of the nose it leads to birth. //591//
383.015. One should certainly declare that there will be the gain of a son and the gain of clothing upon the nose and cheeks.
383.016. If it appears on the tip of the nose, one does not obtain the desired enjoyments of fragrance. //592//
383.017. Likewise, on the upper and lower lips, one finds auspicious and inauspicious food and drink.
383.018. On the chin and the region of the jaw, there are wealth, cattle, and the prosperity of the virtuous. //593//
383.019. But if [the mark] is on the throat, one obtains gifts, drink, and ornaments;
383.020. and if it is at the junction of the head and the neck, one should predict the cutting off of the head. //594//
If this [planet] is born at the head, there is loss of wealth at the jaw;
if at the junction (saṃdhi), there is a life of begging; if in the heart, there is union with loved ones. //595//
If it is on the back, there will be a painful bed and the exhaustion of food and drink;
if it is on the side, there will be a comfortable bed; and if it is on the breast, there will be the birth of a son.
Through its birth, one attains auspiciousness and no encounter with the unpleasant;
it is joined with the destruction of enemies in the arms and indeed with the acquisition of women.
383.027. One born with [a mark] on the elbow of the upper arm gives ornaments when hungry.
383.028. On the wrist, it indicates restraint; on the shoulders, it indicates joy alone. //598//
383.029. He bestows good fortune and the acquisition of wealth upon those born with [these marks] on his hands; 383.030.
for they are indeed blossomed in one part of his teeth and nails. //599//
384.001. One should know from its appearance in the heart that there will be a reunion with brothers and sons; 384.002.
from its appearance in the belly, one should predict the giving of wealth (soma), and from its appearance at the navel, the acquisition of a woman.
384.003. One should know that misfortune and indeed immorality reside in the hips of a woman.
384.004. However, the birth of a son is in the testicles; if the penis is auspicious, the wife is beautiful.
384.005. If they appear at the end of the back, one shares in happiness; if on the buttocks, there is loss of wealth.
384.006. Boils arising on the thighs, however, bestow wealth and good fortune.

One should know that there will be fear of enemies as well as loss of wealth. At the joint of the knees, one should understand that victory, the acquisition of knowledge, and the birth of a son are indicated for those born [under this lunar mansion]. //603//
384.010. There may be the gain of a woman, and another [gain] on the chest shall be useless.
384.011. But on the shanks, there is service to others, and one enjoys [the fruits] from a foreign land. //604//
If a swelling appears at the wrist, one should certainly predict imprisonment;
he will suffer affliction and captivity, without a doubt.
384.014. One should know that if [the lines] are on the side or the ankle, death by the sword is certain. 384.015. On the fingers there is certain grief, and on the finger-joints there is disease.
384.016. There will be constant travel abroad, and likewise for the upper part of the foot.
384.017. For one upon whose soles and likewise upon whose palms [these marks] have appeared, 384.018. he shall obtain wealth, grain, sons, cattle, women, and vehicles. //607//
384.019. One should know that when [the planets] are in friendly signs, the result is friendly; and when they are in movable signs, the result is movable. 384.020.
When situated in fixed signs, they bestow upon men an abundant fruit arising from auspiciousness. //608//
384.021. Faded and distorted, it yields all its fruit.
384.022. Among men, those who are affectionate, those who are in the southern region, and likewise those who are honored in an inner place; 384.023. [they are the ones so described]. //609//
384.024. For women, there is a mountain at the soft regions and at the corners of the mouth.
384.025. Having understood the reality of the *piṇyās*, their location, their color, and their origin. //610//
A wise man should first declare the possible and the impossible, as well as the transformation and the course [of events], just as it has been described here.
On the left side of women, pustules are to be known as auspicious;
on the right side of men, however, they indeed bring about the accomplishment of one's goals.

384.030. However, the *piṭakas* that are contrary [to this] are known to be mostly fruitless; 384.031. and all those situated at the junctions of what has been described are known to yield no results. (613)
385.001. Those that are healed, those that are chronic, those that have burst open, as well as those that are freshly made;
385.002. and those that are like the ritual stakes of Dharma—all these are known as *piṭakas*.
385.003. "The virtues and faults of all beings, as well as others, have thus been proclaimed.
385.004. Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku to his disciples at their constant audience. (615)
385.005. Neither with a fingernail, nor with a weapon, nor in any way with iron;
385.006. one should burn [the image] with gold and pure refined metal, and feed the Brahmins. //616//
385.007. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter concerning the study of the Piṭakas.
385.008. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the manual of dreams.
Listen to it.
What more is there to say?
385.009. May the Blessed One speak—the chapter on dreams (svapnādhyāya).
385.010–385.011. [It concerns] the auspicious and inauspicious results that have been proclaimed regarding dreams.
He who sees deities, brahmins, cows, and likewise a blazing fire at the end of a dream, his family prospers.
But he who sees at the end of a dream a king, an elephant,
a horse, gold, or a bull, his household increases.
Whoever sees cranes, parrots, swans, curlews, and white birds in a dream, their family indeed prospers.
The crops are abundant, fresh, and fragrant;
likewise, there are flowering lotus ponds and full water-jars.
He who, at the end of a dream, sees clear water and various kinds of flowers, his family shall increase.
Whether on the hand, the foot, or the knee, with a weapon or even with a bow—
whenever blows are dealt [to him], his garment increases.
He who sees Tārā and the Moon, the Sun, the lunar mansions, and likewise the planets at the end of a dream, his family shall increase.
He who, at the end of a dream, mounts the back of a horse, the shoulder of an elephant, vehicles, or couches, shall attain great sovereignty.
If it has fallen, one should ascend again; while situated there, one awakens.
This should be indicated for the attainment of sovereignty and wealth, as well as for the recovery of what was lost.
Whoever mounts a chariot or a horse that has traveled a *goyūta* in a dream,
and awakens while remaining seated there, attains sovereignty.
The person who climbs a precipice or even a mountain,
and while remaining there awakens, attains sovereignty.
386.003. By mounting their seats, beds, or vehicles, there is destruction; 386.004. by mounting those [vehicles] for which mounting is prescribed, there is destruction. //628//

386.005. Those for whom there are faults from mounting [it], for them there are virtues from mounting [it]. 386.006. Three thousand [pieces of gold] would be obtained upon the throat; ten [thousand] upon the cutting off of the head. 386.007. Or one obtains a kingdom worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold] upon devouring the head. //629//
Seeing a dried-up river or lake, entering an empty house, or finding a dry well in a dream, one certainly encounters fear. (630)
If one sees a jackal, a human being, a naked person, an iguana, a scorpion, a pig, or a goat in a dream, one should predict the affliction of disease.
If one sees a crow, a hawk, an owl, a vulture, or a quail, or a peacock in a dream, one should predict misfortune for that person.
386.014. For one sees oneself naked, or indeed covered with dust; 386.015. or smeared with mud, and one shall encounter the affliction of disease. //633//
386.016. Having seen lepers, women, thieves, gamblers, as well as 386.017. those of immoral conduct, wandering bards, and rogues in a dream, there is certainly danger. //634//
A person who, while dreaming, wears vomit, urine, or feces, or applies an emetic purgative, or performs anointment with fragrant unguents, will suffer from disease upon waking.
If in the end of a dream one holds a banner, a parasol, or a canopy,
even while remaining in that state one shall awaken and it portends great sovereignty.
But for one whose city is surrounded on all sides by Antras,
and who swallows the sun and the moon, one should predict great sovereignty.
If, at the end of a dream, one swallows a region of the earth or a man,
or if one swallows this lake or the ocean, one shall attain great sovereignty.
If one obtains a bow, a weapon, a blade, red ornaments, a banner,
or armor in a dream, one should predict the acquisition of wealth.
If one sees a precipice, a mountain, a palm tree, a bull, an elephant, or a horse;
a gateway, a city, a door, or the moon and sun along with the stars—having seen these fall in a dream, one should predict calamity for kings. (640)
The rising of the moon and the sun seen in a dream is praised;
however, seeing them set, one should predict calamity for the king.
387.001. If a man climbs a tree in a cemetery, a sacrificial post, 387.002.
an anthill, or a heap of ashes in a dream, it portends misfortune. //642//
If a woman dressed in black clothes dreams that she desires a dark-skinned man while wearing a garland of oleander flowers, that is the end of his life.
If one enters darkness in a dream, or likewise [sees] the fly-whisk of Śambhu,
or falls from a tree in a dream, one should predict death for that person.
If one sees a tree, wood, or even grass withered in a dream, or if one's own head or body [is severed], one should predict his death.
Wherever the god sends rain, or wherever a thunderbolt falls,
or wherever the earth trembles— in such a dream, one should predict calamity.
387.011. If one sees the moon and the sun in a dream as broken or split apart, 387.012. or as having fallen or falling, his vision will perish. //647//
Seeing a woman clad in saffron robes, shaven-headed, wearing soiled garments, or dressed in blue and red clothes, one experiences distress.
If a man obtains tin, lead, bronze, copper, iron, silver, or collyrium in a dream, he suffers the loss of his wealth.
Whether she awakens while singing, laughing, or dancing,
or while musical instruments are being played, one should indicate that there will be exhaustion in that place.
Whether one sinks into mud, mire, or sand, or remains there, one awakens [to the truth] or encounters illness. (651)

387.021. Or one might play at dice with eight-sided pieces or other types for the sake of victory and defeat; 387.022. or one might play with unfavorable marks; having seen these in a dream, discord is certain. //652//
Whether it be a seat, a bed, a vehicle, clothing with its ornaments, or a house—
when these are lost, ruined, or fallen into decay, one undergoes great distress.
If a man drinks surā, maireya, sugarcane liquor, fermented grain-liquor,
or honey-wine in a dream, he experiences exhaustion.
When one does not see one's own reflection in clear water or in a mirror, the formation of the aggregates will certainly arise for that person; of this there is no doubt.
387.029. If the god rains constantly, or if he rains water and dust, or even if he should rain coals, one should predict death there. //656//

387.031. One should recognize that in such a region there will be slaughter of people and great terror. 387.032. Or, if one sees a net of ropes in a dream, one should predict an invasion by a foreign army. //657//
388.001. The city is indeed surrounded on all sides by water;
388.002. or by another net—in a dream, there shall be the onset of an enemy army. (658)
A man whose limbs are smeared with oil and mud, and who possesses a red throat, sings and laughs; one should predict that he will receive a blow.
If a woman dressed in black, or one who is wet or soiled,
embraces a man in a dream, one should predict his imprisonment.
If a black cobra climbs upon a man in a dream,
or even if it should wrap its coils around his limbs, one should predict his imprisonment.
If a person is surrounded by creepers, clusters of tree trunks, or mechanical devices in a dream, one should predict that he will suffer imprisonment.
If all mechanical devices or snares and traps should be broken at the end of a dream, one is liberated from bondage.
Whoever sees rugged places, depressions, mountains, and cities at the end of a dream is swiftly liberated from affliction.
Whether it be a *pūtanā*, a *piśāca*, a wanton woman, or one who is filthy—
having seen such forms in a dream, discord is certain.

If one sees in a dream a man or a woman who is well-bathed, well-attired, fragrant, and dressed in white garments, there is great happiness. Furthermore, where grass, trees, or wood are seen growing [freshly], [that is auspicious].
Whether in the house or in the field, there will quickly be a loss of wealth.
Whether sitting on a noble seat or lying on a well-prepared bed,
a man obtains a woman, or a woman obtains a man.
If a man sees at the end of a dream a white garment smeared with white perfumes and ointments, one should predict for him the acquisition of a woman.
Indeed, he who sees food and ornaments as well as fetters shall obtain a wife, and a woman shall obtain a husband.
By obtaining a girdle, an earring, a garland, or the ornaments of women,
a man shall obtain a wife, and a woman shall obtain a husband.
That woman who pays homage to an elephant, a bull, a serpent, and the moon and sun along with the stars, shall soon obtain a husband. (672)
If any one of these enters the womb of a woman,
she will, in due time, give birth to a glorious son with all his limbs fully developed.
In her dream, a woman obtains all manner of fruits and lush green forests; she shall give birth to a glorious son.
Having seen in a dream an *utpala*, a *kumuda*, a *padma*, or a *puṇḍarīka* lotus, even with its bud, a woman shall give birth to a glorious son.
If a woman dreams that a ball of food is placed there between two strings of offerings,
she will give birth to a son; however,
if she sees a vessel or a staff, she will give birth to a daughter.
Furthermore, if at the end of summer one sees even one's own young wife withering away and likewise withered in a dream, there will be death within one's own faction.
If one's arms, eyes, or even fingers increase in size,
one's kinsmen will prosper and the death of enemies will occur.
389.012. He whose arms are bound and whose vision becomes confused, 389.013.
or he whose arm falls off, shall suffer the death of his own kinsmen. //679//
Whether it be a god or a preta, if in a dream he gives a woman clothing or fruits, a son will be born to her.
389.016. Or one who is drawn away, weeping, naked, or moreover filthy and emaciated; 389.017. or one who displays anger—one should designate him as such. //681//
If one obtains leather, a mechanical device, a calculation, a peg,
or even coagulated milk in a dream, one should know for certain that the acquisition of clothing will surely occur.
Whether it be a non-human being, a king, a god, a departed spirit, or a brahmin—
it will come to pass exactly as they speak in your dream.
389.022. ...that which was previously contemplated;
389.023. that which one recollects having seen, and that which one sees extensively. //684//
Just as one who has set out on a path awakens at the end of a dream,
so too does one encounter a treacherous road or a dangerous precipice.
Having extinguished a blazing and burning fire, one is praised;
the building of houses is commended, but their demolition is not praised.
A cloudless sky is praised, while one with clouds is not commended; clear water is praised, while turbid water is not commended.
Traveling on a journey is auspicious, but turning back anywhere is not;
seeing gold is auspicious, but possessing it is not praised.
The sight of meat is auspicious, but its consumption is not praised;
the sight of liquor is praised, but its drinking is not praised.
390.003. Green earth is praised; discolored earth is not commended.
390.004. Ascending a vehicle is taught [as auspicious]; falling from it is not commended. //690//
In dreams, weeping is auspicious, while laughing is not praised;
seeing things in concealment is auspicious, whereas being naked is never praised.
The sight of garlands is auspicious, but wearing them is not praised;
likewise, while a body that has been scarified is excellent, one that has been sprinkled with water is not praised.
A gentle wind is praised; an excessively strong wind is not praised. One who is ill or soiled is praised [for being present], but one who is adorned is not praised.
Ascending a mountain is praised, but descending from it there is not.
390.012. Smoke-colored clouds, the sound of drums and conchs, wind, and rain from the clouds on all sides; 390.014.
whatever is stable or mobile among all things, and whatever internal disorders are produced by defects—[all these shall cease]. //694//
390.016. Just as the royal sages and all the hosts of gods were described in the former forms, 390.018.
so too, O Brahmin, even this cutting of the limbs—all of these things are indeed auspicious. (695)
Whatever auspicious signs may appear in the preliminary omens, these bring such bad dreams to rest.
By the gift of cows and the honoring of the twice-born, this bad dream shall be overcome. (696)
When a person, possessed of devotion, worships a deity and also strives to honor others,
they say that the fruition of this occurs at the end of a year, having seen the dream during the first part of the evening.
That which occurs in the second [period] lasts for six months; that which occurs in the third lasts for six fortnights;
and that which occurs in the fourth bears fruit at the dawn of the night after one and a half months have passed.
391.001. <391> To an excellent brahmin, the gift of a vessel of sesame seeds, rites for pacification, and the performance of auspicious ceremonies;
391.003. worship of gurus and well-prepared food—these destroy bad dreams. //699//
391.005. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter on the interpretation of dreams.
391.006. Now, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall further explain another chapter on the interpretation of dreams;
let it be heard.
391.007. What then?
Let the Blessed One Triśaṅku relate another chapter on dreams.

391.009. Regarding the fruit that has been proclaimed for auspicious and inauspicious dreams, listen as I shall explain, in accordance with reality, what kind of omen corresponds to which dream. //700//
Whether awake or terrified, if one sees dreams during the day, no fear shall arise for him; the wise man should know this.
Whomever one may have as an enemy, or whomever one desires to be submissive—
if such a person sees a quarrel in a dream, affection will quickly arise.
391.015. He who has seen the giver of pleasure and pain during the first watch of the night, 391.016.
will likewise return after a long time upon his journey. //703//
In the middle [period] it does not occur at all, and in the last [period] it occurs slowly;
having seen a swift deviation from the path, one should predict the acquisition of a woman.
391.019. Having seen the aquatic fish, the wise man should know this:
391.020. "Whatever I shall undertake will very quickly come to pass. //705//
391.021. Or if one rubs one's testicles with the hand in dreams;
391.022. having awakened, one should know that one’s complexion will become thus. //706//
Indeed, all drinks are sweet and pleasant;
however, he who drinks at the end of a dream shall be endowed with gains.
391.025. In this dream, one is surrounded and devoured by dogs and jackals.
391.026. But upon waking, one should know that it is indeed an enemy who is being struck down. //708//
Crows and vultures are running above and flying overhead;
having awakened, one should realize: "An enemy will kill me."
391.029. When the dog of another's house urinates at one's door, 391.030. one who has awakened should know: "My wife desires a paramour. //710//
If one foot is on the ground and the second is placed upon the head, one who has awakened should know that the acquisition of a kingdom will occur. //711//
If he sees the ocean or desires to drink its water,
once awakened, he should know that the acquisition of a kingdom will come to pass.
392.003. Having climbed a tree, a mountain, an elephant, or likewise a horse, one who has awakened should know that the acquisition of a kingdom will come to pass. //713//
But he who sees his ancestors in a dream, or those others here in a different manner,
as well as his mother and father— if they appear thus, they live for a long time.
But he who, in the midst of a dream, sees his hair and beard shorn,
should understand upon waking that the accomplishment of his purpose will come to pass.
If one sees a boat fleeing from water toward the middle of a fire,
upon waking one should know that there will be an increase in the family.
392.011. Running, leaping, and wandering through villages—392.012.
one who has awakened should recognize himself as having been cut down. //717//
Furthermore, he who sees the assembly of thieves even in a dream, upon waking, should understand that he himself has been decapitated. //718//
If one sees oneself seized by a black snake at the end of a dream, upon waking one should know that there will be affliction from an enemy.
392.017. Whoever sees bracelets, earrings, anklets, armlets, and pendants—those shall become his circle of kinsmen.
392.018. And whoever sees such an ornament, he will have a group of relatives.
392.019. Here, they run back and forth against the walls and the enclosures of the house. 392.020. When the boatman is joined with wealth, the pestle strikes the mortar for a moment. (721)
392.021. But he who, within a dream, sees himself scorched by fire, 392.022. should know upon waking that a fever will soon arise. //722//
Seeing the king enraged and himself defiled, one who awakens should understand that his household will perish. (723)
392.025–392.026. Having repeatedly seen a heavy load of wood and grass upon one's own head, a severe illness will arise. //724//
But he who travels toward the eastern direction mounted upon a monkey should recognize, upon waking: "This is indeed the final night. (725)
Having grasped the sun and the moon with his hand, he strokes them;
one who has awakened should know that this is indeed the arrival of the Dharma of the Tathāgata.
392.031. Sumanas flowers, vārṣika flowers, as well as kumudas and utpalas— 392.032.
he who sees these at the end of a dream [foretells] a meeting with those worthy of offerings. //727//
Having seen a brahmin, a śramaṇa, a kṣapaṇa, or a leader of the gods, one who has awakened should understand: "The yakṣas are indeed compassionate toward me."
Having been smeared with blood and bathed in his own gore,
upon awakening he would realize that this was the attainment of supreme sovereignty.
If one sees mung beans, black gram, barley, other grains,
or the sight of fire within a dream, one should predict that there will be an abundance of food in that region.
If one sees gold, silver, and likewise a necklace of pearls within a dream, one should predict that there is a treasure-trove in that place.
Having seen much binding, as well as cutting and crushing, one who has awakened should understand that the accomplishment of his purpose will come to pass. //732//
393.011. "O Puṣkarasārin, this is another chapter on dreams."
393.012. Now, Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter entitled "The Examination of Months. 393.012. Let it be heard!
393.013. May the Blessed One Triśaṅku speak.
393.014. Examination of the Month.
393.015. If a thunderclap should occur during the month of Phālguna, it portends the death of human beings.
393.015. A new moon appears with a reddish luster, portending the failure of all crops. 393.016. If the god thunders, [the same result follows].
First, the great crops will flourish; the final crop will not come to fruition,
and it will incite strife.
If the rain-god thunders in the month of Caitra,
then he impels the growth of all crops.
If there is an eclipse of the moon, [the same occurs].
A great confluence [of calamities] will occur;
villages and fields will become desolate.
If the frost covers the ground, [the crops will perish].
And he urges [him] toward abundance.

If the deity thunders during the month of Vaiśākha, it portends an abundance of food. If there is a lunar eclipse in either the eastern or western horn [of the moon], [it likewise foretells prosperity].
He urges for security:
"If a meteor falls,
and in whichever region it falls,"
In that region, the destruction of the principal person occurs;
however, if there is an earthquake,
it portends an abundance of food.
393.024. If the deity thunders in the month of Jyeṣṭha, it portends disease.
If there is a solar eclipse, [the same result follows].
It portends the destruction of human beings.
If some sign of the moon or the sun is observed on either the eastern or western horizon, it portends security.
393.026. If there is a lunar eclipse at midnight, it portends mutual slaughter among human beings. Furthermore, if there is a thunderous roar from above, [the same result follows].
He reports the harassment of the superintendent and the arrival of a foreign army.
If there is a solar eclipse in the month of Āṣāḍha that possesses a beautiful luster, it portends an abundance of food.
393.028. If there is an eclipse of the moon, it portends disease. 393.029. If lightning flashes forth, [it portends the same].
It portends auspiciousness.
If the frost covers the ground,
it portends an abundance of food.
393.031. If there is a solar eclipse in the month of Śrāvaṇa, the kingdom will change.
393.031. If there is a lunar eclipse, [the same occurs].
In the first month, it portends famine;
by means of *śarabha* [animals], there will be the destruction of excellent crops,
wherever the stars fall upon that land.
In that regard, it incites war;
and if there is an excessive earthquake,
it incites disease.
394.001. If a sound occurs, it portends the destruction of whoever is the master of that house.
394.002. Furthermore, during this month, one must not put on new upper garments.
394.003. One should not perform marriage ceremonies;
one becomes despised.
394.004. If the god thunders in the month of Āśvayuja, it portends the destruction of human beings.
If there is a solar eclipse, [the same result follows].
It portends the destruction of great men.
If the sign of the moon is seen in the first watch of the night,
it portends an abundance of food.
394.006. If an earthquake occurs, it portends turmoil;
a foreign king will destroy the country.
And there, he foretells that humans will kill one another.
394.008. If the god rains during the month of Kārtika, it brings about great turmoil;
furthermore, living creatures will devour the grain.
394.009. If the wind blows with a single, uniform force, then people there will be confounded by the water;
it portends the destruction of a great-souled person.
394.010. If a portent occurs during the first watch of the night, there will be heavy rain,
and the death of a great man will occur.
394.011. If there is a sound, it portends disease.
394.012. If the deity thunders in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, there will be the destruction of the crops;
furthermore, another person shall become the master there.
394.013. And if a sound occurs in the sky, it portends illness for those people who dwell in the eastern region.
394.013. If there is an earthquake, [it portends the same].
Whoever is the leading man in that district shall be released from execution.
394.015. If the deity thunders in the month of Pauṣa, in the first case there will be the destruction of the country;
in the second, it portends the imprisonment of a great-souled man.
394.016. And if, during the first watch of the night, there is an eclipse of the moon and it appears red in color, it indicates the arrival of water; it also indicates a person of great soul.
394.017. It indicates a person of great soul.
394.017. If there is an eclipse of the sun, there will be battle among pure men. 394.018. If falling stars are seen, [there will be conflict].
In that region, he proclaims turmoil;
if a sound occurs in the sky,
he proclaims the death of men.

394.019. If there is a thunderclap in the second month, humans will be slain by thieves. 394.020. If, in this very month, the stars are cast down and the moon is not seen, [the same calamity follows].
It causes the crops to ripen.
If an earthquake occurs,
it indicates the death of a great man.
In this very month, a temple site must be established;
trees must be planted;
and a foundation for the roots must be laid.
394.023. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter named "The Examination of Months."
394.024. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter called "The Knowledge of the Khañjarīṭaka Bird.
394.024. Listen to that. 394.025. Very well.
394.025. May the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku—394.026. the knowledge of the wagtail.
394.027. Indeed, the treatise on the wagtail was [revealed] on Mount Gandhamādana.
O gentle one, when *kucara* is seen, there is great danger from *kucara*.
Whatever signs the *khañjarīṭaka* bird may display,
having seen them while it is moving about, the twice-born man who possesses five additional feet shall come into being.
395.001. In that regard, all should proceed wherever and upon whatever [ground] it may be. 395.002.
On grassy ground, there should be many layers of cloth; on cow dung, there should be a continuous layer. //735//
395.003. In Kañcāra there is an abundance of clothing; in Kardama, an abundance of food. 395.004. In Kṛkara there is a scarcity of clothing; in Purīṣa, however, there is meager hearing. //736//
395.005. In ashes, there is fruitless dispute; in sand, however, there is agitation. 395.006. At the gate of a deity, there is honor; in lotuses, great wealth. 395.007.
Regarding fruits, the result is said to be in accordance with their nature; in flowers, there is union with beloved ones.
395.008. There is fear regarding the turrets of the ramparts and the observation of enemies on the ridges.
395.009. A disease moves through the wings [of the army]; one should predict that death has fallen upon it. //738//

395.010. Fragrant oils will become available through sexual union; there will be the sight of hidden treasures. 395.011. A drink will be found at the top of a tree, and then, in the houses, there will be... [a sweet] flavor. (739)
When there is talk of the destruction of the country and when one is subjected to imprisonment and conflict,
if one sees the nectar remaining, there is no doubt that it is rice.
Success is certain on the back of a cow; victory is certain on the back of a horse. Riding on the backs of sheep and goats is praised for all purposes.
395.016. On the back of a camel there is certainly suffering; on the back of a dog there is flight;
and on the back of a donkey here, death—of this there is no doubt. (742)

395.018. One should know that death occurs at a stake and at the top of a sacrificial post; of this there is no doubt. 395.019. Or where one is seen dead in the place of a water-jar or in a cremation ground. //743//
If one sees a wagtail bird flying in the sky, one should declare it to be fruitless; however, if one sees a wagtail arriving at its dwelling in a joyful state, [it is auspicious].
One should describe the characteristics of humans according to their respective positions and colors:
if the lines are uneven and the armpits are very narrow, there will be constant strife;
if they are even and the field is uniform, one should describe those of equal color.
One should predict travel upon the river Śailavāhinī. //745//
395.026. There is not much concern regarding pieces of wood, nor is there loss of wealth regarding bones.
395.027–28. One should know that his departure toward whichever direction the bird with five toes on each foot has gone will be exactly as it was for him. (746)
Whether it be insects or even moths, if fear is seen here,
then one should indicate that although the man's bones may be abundant, they are to be known as such.

396.001. <396> He who sees the Khañjanaka bird near water, on the head of an elephant, at sunrise, in the presence of a Brahmin, in a primary light, or on the peak of a mountain, is fortunate. //748//
396.005. The wise King of the Mātaṅgas, Triśaṅku, spoke the truth regarding the Khañjana bird and the treatise:
396.007. One should indicate [the omen] on ground that is moist or dry, uneven or level, according to the faults and virtues as they have been described.
396.009. Having observed it there, the learned man should declare it; he should then predict the auspicious or inauspicious results thereof. //749//
396.011. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter entitled "The Knowledge of the Khañjarīṭaka."
396.011. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter named "The Cries of the Auspicious Bird.
396.012. Listen to it. 396.012. Very well.
396.013. May the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku—the cry of the jackal.
396.014–396.015. Homage to all the Noble Ones!
"Homage to all who speak the truth!
By means of the ascetic power and the heroic vigor of them all, I shall expound this chapter named 'The Cry of the Auspicious One' (Śivāruta).
Thus spoke the Blessed Triśaṅku.
He said this to Śāṇḍilya:
"Listen to me regarding the nature and the manner in which they cry out—all those cries. If it should cry out in the eastern direction,"
If a female jackal, standing facing the east, howls three times,
she announces prosperity;
if she howls four times, [the same result follows].
Here he announces an auspicious omen:
if it cries five times,
it announces rain.
If it cries out six times,
it announces fear from the enemy army.
If it cries out seven times, [it announces the same].
If it cries out eight times, it announces imprisonment; if it cries out eight times,
it announces a reunion with loved ones.
"If it cries out repeatedly,
it announces the fear of an enemy army.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
396.022. Standing facing south in the southern direction, one should cry out three times, "atṛ atṛ"; this indicates that death will occur there. 396.023.
If it cries out four times, [death will occur]...
Standing facing the south, it announces from that very direction a joyful reunion;
it also announces the acquisition of wealth.
It should cry out five times.
It announces the intended purpose;
if it cries out six times,
it announces success.
If it cries seven times, it announces a dispute or quarrel;
if it cries eight times,
it announces fear.
"It cries out repeatedly;
it announces something troubled.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
If a jackal stands facing west in the western quarter and howls three times,
it indicates death;
if it howls four times, [it indicates the same].
It announces the bondage;
it cries out five times,
announcing the year.
If it cries out six times,
it announces food and drink;
if it cries out seven times, [it announces the same].
It announces sexual union.
If it cries out eight times,
it announces the accomplishment of one's purpose.
"It cries out repeatedly;
this portends a great rain-cloud," so said the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
397.001. If, standing facing north in the northern direction, it cries out three times, the journey of the man who has set out will be fruitless.
397.002. If it cries out four times, [the same result follows].
He reports the danger from the king;
he cries out five times,
reporting a dispute.
If it cries out six times,
it announces what is auspicious;
if it cries out seven times, [it announces what is even more auspicious].
He announces the rains;
he cries out eight times,
announcing the royal punishment.
"It cries out incessantly;
this portends fear of yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, and kumbhāṇḍas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
397.006. Listen to my instruction regarding the cardinal and intermediate directions, as well as the mountain slopes and peaks:
"One who is afflicted by thirst should satisfy this [goddess], and likewise for the accomplishment of the vidyā-mantra.
397.008. The wise one should prescribe the attainment of the vidyā and the attainment of wealth.
If a female jackal is seen at the foot of a tree shaped like a sacred bathing place (tīrtha), [it portends misfortune]. //750//

397.010. One should point out success in all matters. And when there is fear of a jackal, one should think, "A female jackal (śivā) has approached me"; thus, being heedful and mindful, one should always worship the female jackal.
397.011. Service should be rendered with offerings of incense and flowers.
When worshipped in this manner, she will grant all accomplishments. 397.012.
Thus, "all his aims will be fulfilled, just as Triśaṅku’s word [declared]."
397.012. If the krauṣṭrika cries out, it announces the acquisition of wealth.
397.013. If it cries out with its face turned downward, [it portends misfortune].
Therein it announces a treasure;
if it cries with its face turned upward,
it announces rain there.
397.014. If it cries on a forked path, standing facing the east, it announces the acquisition of wealth.
397.015. If it cries facing the south, [it likewise portends gain].
It announces the meeting with loved ones.
If it dwells on a forked path facing westward,
it announces quarrels, disputes, conflict, and even death.
If it cries at the edge of a well,
it indicates wealth there;
if it cries on a grassy meadow, [it indicates the same].
It announces the accomplishment of one's purpose.
If it cries out in an excessively weak manner,
it announces illness therein.
397.018. If it cries out while carrying a song, it announces profit or loss.
397.019. With three calls it indicates profit; with four, loss; with five, a meeting with loved ones; with six, food; with seven, fear; and with eight, strife and dispute.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
397.021. “Furthermore, I shall speak again; listen to me in due order.
Whether he dwells in various places or stands upon the road, I shall tell you all of that; listen to me.”
When a man has set out on his journey, if a jackal howls while standing facing the east, it foretells a swift departure and the accomplishment of one's purpose.
However, if it howls facing the south, [it portends otherwise].
That which announces the accomplishment of one's purpose;
or if it cries facing westward,
it announces danger.
397.024. Now, if it cries facing north, it announces the acquisition of wealth.
397.025. Or, if it cries as one is setting out on a journey, [it foretells success].
If it stands in front, it announces a secondary affliction (*upakleśa*).
Then, if it cries out toward the south, it announces the success of an action (*karmasiddhi*) for one facing the southern direction.
If it cries from the west,
it portends harm from a thief and brings suffering and mental distress. Furthermore, if it cries from the right side while one is traveling on a road, [it is auspicious].
It indicates that thieves will plunder him from the great disease and misfortune.
If it howls facing south when he is ill, [it portends the same].
“He cannot be cured when impelled by the messenger of Death.
If he speaks while ill,
standing facing north, he announces the attainment of health and wealth.
397.030. Now, if it cries out from the top of its head, it announces a minor affliction.
Then, if it stands facing west and calls out to one another, [it indicates something else].
It announces the decree of Yama;
or, if it dwells on various kinds of food,
it announces agitation.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
398.001. If a jackal howls before a man who has set out on a journey, it indicates a safe path ahead.
398.002. It announces the accomplishment of one's purpose.
398.002. As he travels along the road, if a jackal comes from the left and goes toward the right, one should know this to be an auspicious path; it announces the accomplishment of one's purpose.
398.003. If, as a man travels on the road, a jackal comes from the left and howls in front of him...
One who perceives a path to be thus dangerous should turn back;
having gone toward the right, one should turn back from the left, thinking, "One must not go by that path, according to the word of Triśaṅku."
398.005. If a jackal goes before him and sits down in front, one should know that the path is dangerous;
398.006. a wise man should turn back.
398.006. If a jackal comes from the front and turns to the left, the wise man should know that there is danger here; by this, he should recognize fear.
398.007. When the army has been mobilized, if a jackal howls, [it portends ill].
He announces his final withdrawal:
"If there should be defeat upon advancing,
let the army not go forth."
398.008. When an army is marching, if a jackal comes from the front, it announces victory for the army.
398.009. And it announces the defeat of the enemy host.
398.009. When a caravan is traveling, if a jackal goes before them, it announces a safe path.
398.010. And likewise, there is the accomplishment of one's purpose.
398.011. If it cries to the left of a man walking on a path, it indicates the way.
"Therefore, one must proceed by that path, just as Triśaṅku did."
398.012. “In a village or even in a city, likewise at a shrine,” 398.012. “if a jackal howls to the east or to the north, it announces safety therein.”
If it cries in the south, the west, or the north,
it announces that there will be fear in those directions; likewise, they do not praise its crying from the left or from the intermediate quarters.
398.015. Or if [the tongue] is excessively long and excessively dry at the end of the month during that time;
398.016. I shall now describe the danger regarding the lower lip, according to the words of Triśaṅku. //751//
398.017. Knowing that the auspicious time has arrived with its honeyed tone, 398.018.
the wise should consider both security and the accomplishment of their goals. //752//
398.019. Diseases and calamities—all these shall indeed be pacified, just as by the word of Triśaṅku. 398.020.
One should observe the omens of the jackal’s howl throughout the cardinal and intermediate directions.
398.020. That day which is the day of Śivā should be recognized as such.
398.021. On that day, offerings of flowers, perfumes, garlands, and oblations should be prepared.
398.021. One must always be respectful toward the deities and one's teacher. 398.021. One must be respectful toward the queen. 398.022. Service must be rendered to the queen.
398.022. It will accomplish all aims;
it reports all tasks.
Whatever task he shall undertake, he reports it all [to her].
Incense of *sarjarasa* and *guggulu* should be burned for the Goddess.
398.025. And an offering of flowers should be presented at the proper time.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Triśaṅku.
398.026. Regarding the interpretation of the howling of jackals here, I shall declare the knowledge so that it may become true.
398.027. Homage to Āraṇyā! Svāhā to Cīriṇī! Incense of resinous *sarja* wood!
398.028. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter titled "The Cries of the Jackal."
399.001. Now, therefore, Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter on the lines of the hands.
Listen to that.
"Very well."
399.002. Let the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku—the lines on the hand.
399.003–399.004. Now, therefore, I shall fully explain that which resides upon the hands of men.
399.005. The characteristics of pleasure and pain, as well as life and death. //753//
399.006. Relying upon the base of the thumb, an upward line proceeds.
399.007. That which is born therein is most auspicious; the second [line] is within the knowledge [of the self]. //754//
399.008. That third line where the forefinger proceeds—399.009.
there, the reasons are stated in the treatise as being, in brief, fourfold. //755//
When there are nodes at non-parvan times and an affliction of the lunar mansions,
he who has emerged twice with a purified soul shall indeed live for a hundred years.
One should know that with a thirty-third part [of the lifespan], it is fifty when the lifespan is half;
with three-sevenths, it is one hundred when the lifespan has reached its maximum. //757//
399.014. As soon as the line of life is clearly seen, the intervening years are revealed.
399.015. By means of the designations of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), the meaning should likewise be understood by men. //758//
399.016. As many lines as there are on the surface of the thumb, 399.017.
so many children one should know that person will have; of this there is no doubt. (759)
One should know that a person will be long-lived if there is a long line;
however, one should know that a person will be short-lived if there is a short line.
If a barley grain is found at the base of the thumb during the night, one should predict birth;
however, if it is found on the thumb during the day, birth is certainly predicted.
399.022. Wherever the indistinct *yavaka* is situated, one should designate that as the ascendant (*lagna*).
399.023. The ascendant is to be known as masculine; one should designate it according to the day and night. //762//
399.024. One should designate birth as occurring during the day; at night, it is designated as female. 399.025.
Night is declared to be the twilight (saṃdhyā), along with the other portions; of this there is no doubt. 399.026.
One should state that their rising from the male designation occurs at the end of the day and night. //763//
399.027. At the base of the thumb, at the barley-grain mark, and at the *śala* joint, happiness is ordained.
399.028. One should recognize that what is auspicious regarding horses applies here to the barley-grain marks on the thumbs. //764//

399.029. If there is a garland of barley and a fish, and the thumb and barley [are present] during sexual union, one should predict happiness for her in childhood, youth, middle age, and old age. //765//

399.031. Those upon whose soles the barley-grain (*yavaka*), the water-vessel (*cāpa*), or likewise the *svastika* is seen—399.032. those men are indeed to be blessed; they are truly fortunate. //766//
400.001. In the first quarter of Pisces, there will be grain for enjoyment; in the first quarter of Aries, there will be wealth from meat and other such things.
400.002. One should know that there is enjoyment and good fortune in the first quarter of Pisces; of this there is no doubt.
By means of banners, flags, spears,
or lances, as well as by goads held at the base [of the chariot], one should recognize a lord of the earth;
and one born of a royal lineage should be designated as a mere king.
If five lines are sent by the branch, or indeed four on the hand,
one will become a Kṣatriya, an enjoyer of wealth, and honored even by kings.
A Vaiśya or a Kṣatriya who is eloquent will undoubtedly obtain wealth and grain;
a Śūdra, being devoted to the sacred festivals and firm in his vows, shall become a possessor of great fortune.
400.010. He should always be worthy of honor and speak kindly to everyone. 400.011.
Whether he is lacking in virtue or possesses a mere semblance of virtue, he should not be considered great by reason of his many [followers]. //771//
If that line is dark-colored or broken, he will be a partaker of suffering.
He on whose hand three lines are seen, complete and situated at the tip, shall be of great enjoyment and great learning, and he shall live for a hundred years. (772)
One should know that he whose royal parasol has the mark of a goat's foot, and is preceded by the conch and the discus, with these visible upon its surface, is a lord of the earth.
The king’s fortune is for his prosperity through banners, flags, elephants, horses, garlands, and goads;
the fish is for drinking, barley for wealth, the altar for sacrifice, and the cow-pen for cattle.
If the ring finger extends beyond the joint of the ring finger, he lives for a hundred years;
if they are equal, he lives for eighty years, as one might predict based on the seven rivers being full.
Having observed a line originating from the color of the body, possessing a crest, yet devoid of color—one should discern those of low, superior, or middling status as they move amidst poverty. (776)

Having rubbed the hand with ointments, powders for rubbing, perfumes, and the dust of the superintendent, and having washed it until the streaks have been thoroughly rubbed away, one should examine the hand with a one-pointed mind. //777//
401.001. <401> Adoring the Lord of Men who wears bracelets, three [lines] follow along at the wrist.
401.003. And again, in another existence, that Great-Souled One, possessing abundant wealth and glory, spoke of the acquisition of garments. //778//
One whose hand is constantly raised gives perpetually; one whose hand is long and fleshy for a long time acquires wealth.
One whose hand is covered with visible veins falls into ruin, while one whose hand is hidden by flesh attains riches.
401.009. O Sudṛśa, those who are honest have palms that are straight, while rogues have them that are crooked and closed.
401.011. One whose hands are very red, resembling blood, and remain clenched for a long time here will become a lord. //780//

One whose mind is firm and radiant, who possesses hands like flaming saffron-colored lotuses, becomes wealthy with many treasures, has hidden hands, and lives here for a long time, enjoying drinks and pleasures. (781)
401.017. Here, one with long and warm hands is fortunate; however, one with cold hands is certainly impotent.
401.019. For here, he who possesses great wealth and is endowed with strength is one whose hand-lines are well-formed and well-accumulated.
The line on the hand that brings wealth in this world is one produced at birth that is very long like water;
one that follows the shape of water, is golden-colored, and has depressions and elevations, acquires great wealth.
One whose palms are deeply red acquires wealth, and one whose fingers are broad and closely set likewise attains great fortune. However,
even a wealthy man may lose his riches if he has wrinkles on his palms, lacks control over his speech, and has broken or faded lines on his skin.
A man whose lines on the palms lack the color of ghee becomes wealthy and endowed with strength;
likewise, his wife shall be beautiful, well-adorned, virtuous, and faithful to him alone.

Though he may have been poor, having acquired great wealth, he possesses broad lines on the palms; having attained sacred learning, that fortunate lord has lines on his palms that are straight, blue-black, and stainless. (786)
402.005. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter on the lines on the palm of the hand.
402.006. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter named "The Cawing of the Crow.
Listen to it. 402.007.
"Very well," he replied.
402.007. May the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku. Homage to the Arhats!
Having paid homage to them—
The Cawing of Crows:
I shall now proclaim this treatise concerning the auspicious and inauspicious [omens] of crows,
as well as victory and defeat, and likewise gain and loss.
402.011. Happiness and suffering, the pleasant and the unpleasant, as well as life and death—402.012. I shall explain the accomplishment of the crows' speech according to the rule. //788//
The most excellent gods proclaim: "Homage, homage to the crows!
The crows who feed upon offerings have come to the world of men."
When a crow is ahead on the path of one who has set out,
perched upon a milky tree and crying out, it indicates the attainment of success in one's purpose.
402.017. With a voice full of satisfaction, he took refuge among the fruit-bearing trees; 402.018. and his return, as well as the accomplishment of his purpose, was announced. //781//
The leaves of the trees have grown large and they blow a sweet fragrance;
one should indicate that the food to be eaten is without soup, but consists of milk mixed with molasses.
If it is seen with its beak and feet rubbing itself, one should know that there is milk-rice mixed with ghee; of this there is no doubt.
He rubs his beak with a harsh sound and strokes his head;
having perched upon a fruit-bearing tree, there will certainly be a meal of meat.
402.025. Perched upon a fruit tree, he observes and speaks;
402.026. and he offers as food the meat killed by a hunter. //785//
402.027. A crow perched upon a tree utters a terrible cry;
402.028. one should know that there will be strife and the fear of battle there, without a doubt. //786//
Sitting upon a withered tree, one should speak words that are emaciated and dejected;
having engaged in a very great quarrel, no purpose whatsoever is accomplished therein.
Having sat beneath a milk-exuding tree (*kṣīrivṛkṣa*), one should speak words that are emaciated and dejected;
gradually, at a distance of a yoke’s length, no purpose whatsoever will be accomplished there.
403.001. Sitting upon a withered tree, it caws "akāmuka-aka. 403.002. At that very moment, one should announce that there will be danger from thieves there. //799//
403.003. Sitting upon a withered tree, he caws "akāmuka-kam. 403.004. If he shows his back, it indicates a burden; if he points [toward himself], it indicates affliction by hunger. //800//
If one sees a jackal shaking its flank and howling by the side of the road, one should not proceed there; the path is beset by thieves.
If a crow pulls at a rope or even a wooden plank, one should not proceed there; it is better not to go, for the path is beset by thieves.
If a crow cries out upon cow dung, dry wood, or even in the air, there will be quarrels, harsh words, and disease; nor will one's purpose be accomplished there.
If the bird always shows grass or wood,
and its claws are dry in front of one, there will be danger from thieves in that place.
Sitting atop the caravan, one should speak in a feeble and dejected manner;
one should fall down in the midst of the caravan—there is no doubt that this is the army of thieves.
When birds cry out in various ways while circling to the right or in a state of fear,
and sit upon a withered tree, one should know that there is great danger.
If a bird speaks while terrified, trembling,
and overcome with fear, and it circles all the directions, then danger has arrived.
One should follow after him as he goes, but standing before him, one should speak. One should not proceed there; this is the clearing of the path.
If one utters something emaciated or dejected while standing in the center of the site,
one should recognize that there will be disease either in that place or among the owners of the house.
Just as a crow cries out confidently at the sound of a cart,
one should recognize that someone has arrived from afar and predict their success.
If a crow perches and caws upon a gargara water-vessel, a small jar, or even on a cooking pot or a large earthenware vessel, a journey is certain and well-known to take place.
Whether on a seat, on a bed, or while standing or walking, if a crow caws,
it foretells a certain journey and a reunion with one who has gone abroad.
If a crow perches upon the place of Brahmā and caws steadily,
one should know that there will be the acquisition of wealth and the gain of riches.
Sitting in the Brahma-position, he cries out weakly and piteously;
at that time, a thief will surely carry off the joint—of this there is no doubt.
404.001. The deities of the deities and the groves of the god—whomever one should address with these words, for that person one should predict the attainment of wealth. //815//
If one should take lac, turmeric, madder, yellow orpiment,
and realgar from someone's presence, one should predict for that person the acquisition of gold.
Whether it be a bowl, a small vessel, or even an excellent earthenware pot—
whichever [item] one takes away, one should predict that person's acquisition of wealth.
404.007. Having formed a flock, the crow stands auspiciously at a distance of a yoke's length.
404.008. Or where crows carry a piece of wood to their nest, 404.009.
one should understand from this that there will be great danger from a beggar. //818//
If crows seize blue, yellow, or red objects, as well as things that have been discarded, one should predict that there will be disease in that place.
404.012. A crow crying at the edge of a village foretells danger; indeed, it certainly cries out. 404.013. Or if it cries individually, one should know that there is great danger therein. //820//
If a crow, having seized a bone, should go away toward the left,
and then sit upon a fruit-bearing tree, it indicates a feast of meat for me.
If a crow sits upon someone's head and pulls at their ear,
one should predict that his death will occur within seven nights.
If it cries on a Karaka or a Codaka tree, or in moist places,
while gazing upward with its face turned toward the sky, one should predict rain for the world.
If it cries among the trees at sacred fords with a contented voice, it foretells rain;
likewise, if it calls with its face turned upward, one should predict wind and rain.
If a crow cries out "kilakila" while scratching its body and flapping its wings in a moist place, it indicates that rain will fall immediately.
404.024. With a voice that is highly pleased, it cries out in a smooth and sweet manner. 404.025. If it cries out with a portion of liquid mixed with grains, there shall be food. //826//
If a crow perches upon a gate or at its top,
and repeatedly rubs its beak there, one should predict a battle in that place.
One should predict that there will be circular formations or whirlpools outside the city,
as well as fierce enmity and conflict.
Whether in a village or even in a city, wherever they perform the maṇḍala,
they cry out with their faces turned upward, and a state of dejection arises.
When a female crow caws to the east of the village,
forests, cities, and small bodies of water will overflow.
If a female crow caws on the front right side, it will rain in the first month, but thereafter the god will not rain;
the plowed grains will flourish, while the pulses and beans perish. (831)
405.006. When a female crow lays her eggs upon the top of a tree to the south, 405.007. there will be an abundance of frogs, insects, flies, and thieves. //832//
But when a female crow caws on the northwestern side,
lightning will strike there, and there shall be danger for wild beasts and birds.
When a female crow caws upon the northern branch-tip of a tree,
one should know that grain previously sown is successfully growing.
When a female crow caws from the top of a tree, one should know that there will be little water; one should plant seeds on dry land.
But when the female crow makes her nest in the middle of the tree, it rains moderately,
and a moderate harvest is produced.
When a female crow caws at the root of a tree's trunk, there will be a terrible drought; one should predict famine in that region.
When the female crow lays four or five eggs,
there will be an abundance of food in that place and a profusion of fruits.
405.020. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter entitled "The Cries of the Birds."
405.021. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter named "The Characteristics of Doors.
405.021. Listen to that. 405.022. Very well.
405.022. May the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku— 405.023. the characteristics of the gate.
405.024. Mohendra and the divine Māṅgalya are prescribed for the east.
In the southern direction, however, are Pūṣan and Pitrya.
One should designate Sugrīva and Puṣpadanta here in the west;
one should know Bhallātaka and Rājayakṣman in the north as auspicious.
405.028. [It effects] the attainment of birth, prosperity, misfortune, fields, security, and the subduing of enemies;
405.029. and furthermore, it brings wealth, friendship, and supreme delight. //841//
The wise and high-minded Viśvakarman spoke according to the rules: "I shall explain, in due order, the merits and defects of building sites."
406.001. The ground should be level, quadrangular, and indeed extensive;
406.002. for a Brahmin, a site abounding in milk-yielding trees is considered auspicious and highly praised. //843//
406.003. Or, that site which has the shape of a chariot wheel due to its former foundation, 406.004. and where the soil is red—such a place is praised for kings. //844//
A triangular site that is strewn with *kuśa* grass, level, and sweet, as well as one with water nearby for the exerting person— that is the site for wealth and medicinal herbs.
406.007. Having the appearance of glowing coals, the shape of a cow’s mouth, or the form of a cart;
406.008. that is declared to be uninhabitable, and it brings about the destruction of one's children.
That which has been discarded by the thickets of *kañjaraka* trees and by rainwater, as well as water that flows to the right (clockwise), one should avoid from afar. //847//
For a Brāhmaṇa it should be square, but for a Kṣatriya it is circular;
for a Vaiśya it is ten [aṅgulas] and for a Śūdra twelve—thus is the drawing performed there.
406.013. One should cause a cow-pen to be built in the northeastern part of the site;
likewise, one should build the fire-hall in the southeastern direction. //849//
One should establish the rain-shed and the armory to the south;
and here, toward the west and north, one should establish the merchandise of the merchants.
406.017. However, the unsurpassed latrine should be constructed in the north. 406.018. All [other structures] should be in the northeast, and the palace should face the east.
If one deviates from the prescribed rule, there shall be enmity and death therein;
for all doors that have been constructed, the length is considered to be double [the width].
406.021. One may construct doorways for divine abodes as one desires;
however, women seen at the edge of those doorposts bring about harm. //853//
406.023. Might there not be the seizing of the hand at the gate of a hostile person living in the same world?
406.024. Or might there be sovereignty in the city of Mahendra, or solar radiance like that of the sun? //854//
In the Satya (East) direction, there is a mild deer; in the Antariksha (North-East), a hero and the loss of wealth.
In the Vayavya (North-West), however, there is much disease; in the Bhaga (South-West), a reversal of fortune.
In Puṣya, one is always fortunate; in Vitatha, one becomes unfortunate.
In Śoka, there will be a physical affliction; in Śoṣa, there is dejection.
406.029. Dwelling in a house made of *bhallātaka* wood brings about the onset of pulmonary consumption (*rājayakṣman*).
406.030. When there is a settling of dust in a lake, a period of strife (*kalidhruvam*) will certainly occur during the sun's course. //857//
If there is great fear of *nāgas* from the *nāga*-king, there will be long life;
however, one should predict fear of fire at whatever gate this [sign] occurs.
407.001. One should know the destruction of that very wealth and of one's lineage; 407.002. one should recognize death within the family, even for the most excellent and noble. 407.003.
When Bhṛṅgirāja appears, the wise man [should know] the scent and garlands of the Gandharvas. (859)
In Bhṛṅga, there is anger and strife; in Pitṛ, there is abundance of enjoyments.
In Dauvārika, there is meager wealth; in Sugrīva, one is honored by kings.

407.006. Under Puṣpadanta, there is the acquisition of wealth; under Varuṇa, there is splendor in water. 407.007. Under Asura, there is terrible death; under Roga, however, there is a multitude of afflictions. //861//
407.008. I shall now describe the offerings and oblations according to each household.
407.009. Having honored [the deity] with various perfumes and fragrances from the intermediate directions, one should present the oblation.
In the Kalatra [house], the seeds of causes are indeed acquired; in the Madhyama [house], flowers are released; in Mahendra, flowers are released; and in Pāvaka, milk and curd.
407.012. Under Āditya, however, one should offer rice-milk porridge and millet (*priyaṅgu*).
407.013. Under Antarīkṣa, divine water and aquatic flowers. //864//
The first lunar day (pratipad) is to be known as Nandā, and the sixth and thirteenth as Jayā.
On those respective days, a wise and discerning person should certainly perform [the rite]. //865//
407.016. This, O Puṣkarasārin, is the chapter named "The Characteristics of the Gate."
407.017. Now then, O Puṣkarasārin, I shall explain the chapter named "The Twelve Houses.
Listen to it. 407.018. Very well.
407.018. Let the Blessed One speak concerning Triśaṅku—the one consisting of twelve signs.
407.020. Hereafter, I shall proclaim the section on mind and consciousness.
Just as it has been illustrated by this very example for the sake of human beings. //866//
Therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme consciousness of the mind;
for there are indeed twelve such minds that circulate within the world.
407.024. I shall explain them to you; therefore, listen to me according to the truth.
407.025. A wise person should indeed construct twelve mandalas. //868//
The first is called Aries; the second is known as Taurus;
the third is named Gemini; and the fourth is Cancer.
The fifth is Leo, and the sixth is known as Virgo;
Libra should be known as the seventh, and Scorpio likewise as the eighth.
The ninth is to be known as Sagittarius (Dhanvī), and the tenth is remembered as Capricorn (Makara).
Aquarius (Kumbha) is to be known as the eleventh, and Pisces (Mīna) is said to be the twelfth.
408.001. <408> The first house is the body of the one born; in the second, one considers wealth. 408.002.
In the third are brothers, and likewise in the fourth are one's own kinsmen. //872//
In the fifth [house], a son is considered; in the sixth, enmity.
In the seventh, union with a wife; in the eighth, death is traditionally taught.
In the ninth [house], dharma is considered; in the tenth, the fruit born of action.
In the eleventh, there is the gain of wealth; in the twelfth, the occurrence of futility.
These twelve states of mind have been perceived by the great seers;
they are the self-nature of all beings and should be understood as they truly are by those who possess bodies.
408.009. When someone arrives and asks a question, they should first touch the mandala. 408.010. Furthermore, one who touches the head and a sound is perceived—[these are signs]. //876//
If one should say that he himself is afflicted by disease and that fiery destructions have occurred,
then that [statement] would be considered to be for his own sake.
Gold, silver, copper, and iron shall indeed become abundant;
and that fire, being all-pervading, certainly consumes them all.
408.015. Having seen such a fiery portent, one should indicate it as belonging to him. 408.016.
And whatever the sound may be, by that [sound] his intention is to be discerned. //879//
408.017. A certain man might come and touch the second mandala;
408.018. or he might stroke his neck, his throat, and again his chin. //880//
408.019. If the sound is heard and the cows are likewise seen, 408.020. having observed such an omen, one should indicate the sound of the cows there. 408.021.
Or rather, whatever the sound may be, by that [sound] his thought is indicated. //881//
If some man should come and touch the third mandala, one should cleanse his face; this indicates that he possesses a woman's mind.
408.024. Now, if there should be a sound there, let such things as those be heard by you:
"born," "already born," "about to be born," and likewise, "he will be born. (883)
Having observed such an omen, one should predict the nature of his conception; or rather, whatever the sound was like, by that he [the fetus] has been conceived.
If some man arrives and touches the fourth mandala, he who touches the tortoise should predict a quarrel; there will undoubtedly be legal proceedings involving his own kinsmen. (885)
408.031. When sounds such as "ākaṭṭā" and "kaṭṭeti" arise continuously, 408.032. having seen such an omen, one should predict a quarrel there. //886//
409.001. A certain man might come and touch the fifth mandala.
409.002. He who touches the heart has offspring there in his thought. //887//
One who has gone abroad and died in another village should be known as such;
and whatever weapons or property he possessed that remained in the family of the Brahmins [should be returned]. //888//
409.005. Then, if a sound should arise there, which the great seers have observed; 409.006. if the cry "Son! Son! is heard, and wherever that sound goes, right there it passes away; 409.007.
having seen such an omen as this, one should predict death in that very place. //889//
409.008. A certain man comes and touches the sixth mandala.
409.009. He also touches the sides; thus, anxiety regarding his limbs has been considered. //890//
A most terrible conflict will arise, and even an enemy will be slain;
or else, whatever sounds are heard there, they shall undoubtedly come to pass.
409.012. But this [creature] is thus emitting its secretions, struck down, and likewise slaughtered.
409.013. Seeing such a portent, one should predict a conflict with enemies.
409.014. Or else, whatever the sound may be, by that very thing his intention is revealed.
409.015. A certain man might come and touch the seventh mandala; 409.016. he might rub hand against hand, and likewise rub the channel. //893//
409.017. One should understand that thoughts concerning a dwelling may pertain to another village.
409.018. Therefore, these sounds must be heard by one desiring land. //894//
Whether it be standing, seated, moving, or having been completed, or likewise brought into one's hand—
having seen such an omen, one should predict his dwelling.
Or rather, whatever sound was heard, by that he should determine what was intended.
409.022. A certain man might come and touch the eighth mandala. 409.023. He should then rub both the belly and the buttocks. //896//
409.024. His end is seen, and his death is also seen.
409.025. If there were to be death, it would be for one who has met with another beloved. (897)
409.026. Therefore, these sounds should be heard [as omens]: "He will surely die. 409.027. Having seen such a portent, one should predict his calamity. //898//
